## Waiting delayed typed conditional references

The CR 609.7a declaration query `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources` now
traverses typed conditional operands and all potential bodies without executing
them. Card-type and cast branches retain body reads; enchantment-subtype branches
retain subject and body reads; positive branches retain value and body reads.
State branches and waiting intervening-if conditions retain explicit typed
source, counter, combat, control and history reads, including all/any/not trees.
Activation-history branches retain the exact source incarnation in their history
key, even when the count is zero. Coin branches retain player and both result
bodies. Control-history alternatives retain their player operand. A scoped
player snapshot declares the source read that produces its local binding.

False conditions, zero values and unselected outcomes still supply references.
Queries do not evaluate conditions, values or callbacks, consume RNG, make
choices, perform payments or execute bodies. Opaque callbacks, implicit
attachments and not-yet-created nested delays remain excluded. No callback
introspection or general battlefield scan infers additional identities.

CR 400.7 and 603.7a–e still govern exact identity and delayed creation. Departure
and phasing retain saved references; returns cannot replace them. One-shot
trigger detection ends waiting eligibility. An intervening-if condition that is
false at detection retains its wait; a true detection consumes the wait and the
condition is checked again at resolution. Existing condition-specific current
state and LKI policies remain unchanged. Copies and clones keep independent
binding frames, waiting lifetimes and random queues.

RON scoped coin lowering uses the same `FlipCoin` service as unscoped branches.
Player scope comes from the existing typed reference or per-instance player
snapshot. The flip occurs only at resolution and consumes one queued outcome.
The selected body retains its lexical player scope. Payment transactions,
replacement ordering and simultaneous-operation mechanics are unchanged.

Evidence: `TestWaitingDelayedBranchOperands` (31 native operand forms),
`TestWaitingDelayedBranchPurity`, `TestWaitingDelayedBranchIntervening`,
`TestRONWaitingDelayedBranchProtection` (seven real protection subrules across
98 branch/lifecycle cases), `TestRONWaitingDelayedBranchScopedCoin`,
`TestRONWaitingDelayedBranchInstances` and `TestRONWaitingDelayedBranchInvalid`.
Complete protection records still reject unsupported general source aggregation.

## Source operands of waiting resolution choices

`ChooseAtResolution(PlayerRef, ...ResolutionOption) ResolvingEffect` declares
explicit permanent source reads from its chooser, every `When` condition and
every `Body` to `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources() []DamageSource`.
Nested choices use the same declaration. An unavailable or unselected option
still refers to its declared objects under CR 609.7a. Queries do not call player
choices, evaluate conditions or values, or execute bodies. Opaque predicates,
implicit attachment references and future delays do not infer a source read.

The saved delayed source retains its incarnation through phasing and departure;
a returned card cannot replace it (CR 400.7 and 603.7c). Trigger detection ends
one-shot waiting availability. Existing capture, information, deduplication,
clone, option legality and per-resolution binding services remain in use.
There is no new replacement, payment or simultaneous-operation contract.

`TestWaitingDelayedChoiceOperands` and `TestWaitingDelayedChoicePurity` establish
chooser/body/condition traversal, nested options, purity, phasing, departure and
return, independent clone lifetimes and execution at resolution.
`TestRONWaitingDelayedChoiceAbility`, `ScopedCounter`, `Invalid` and `Protection`
establish RON lowering, copies, scoped players, compile-time rejection and seven
real protection cost/filter/shield subrules. These subrules do not establish
complete protection-card gameplay or complete general damage-source selection.

## Waiting delayed token-creation operands

`CreateTokenCopies(PlayerRef, ResolutionValue, TokenDefinition) ResolvingEffect`
and `CreateTokenCopiesInto(PlayerRef, ResolutionValue, TokenDefinition,
*CreatedTokensBinding) ResolvingEffect` declare explicit permanent source reads
from their player and count to `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources()`.
`CreateOneToken(PlayerRef, TokenDefinition, *PermanentBinding) ResolvingEffect`
declares reads from its player. Existing typed player/value traversal supplies
nested arithmetic, permanent information and collection operands. Zero counts
retain declarations. The query does not resolve a player, evaluate a count,
create tokens, or run token abilities. Token ability bodies use the created
token's scope and cannot declare the producer's source. Implicit attachments,
opaque values and future delayed producers do not infer explicit source reads.

Existing delayed capture, LKI, deduplication and clone services keep exact source
incarnations through phasing and departure. A returned object cannot replace the
saved reference. One-shot detection ends waiting availability. Execution retains
existing player/value resolution and token batch/replacement behavior. CR 400.7,
603.7a–e and 609.7a govern identity, lifetime and waiting source availability;
CR 111.2 and 701.7 govern token creation. No new replacement ordering is added.

RON `CreateTokens/2` now uses the lexical player and supports the existing full
single-instruction, empty-modifier shape inside `PlayerAction/2` and
`PlayerActions/2`. The latter captures its player once; nested `ActionPlayer`
references retain their lexical binding. Token ability compilation keeps its
separate permanent source scope. Saved token results remain outside this adapter.

`TestWaitingDelayedTokenOperands` covers all three native constructors, player
and count reads, zero arithmetic, exact identity, phasing, departure/return, LKI,
clone isolation and execution. `TestWaitingDelayedTokenPurity` proves enumeration
does not evaluate a count; resolution evaluates it once. `TestWaitingDelayedTokenScope`
excludes token ability bodies, implicit attachments and future delays.
`TestRONWaitingDelayedToken` covers 20 operand/lifecycle combinations, including
stack copies and lexical player execution. `TestRONWaitingDelayedTokenInvalid`
rejects four malformed scopes/modifiers. `TestRONWaitingDelayedTokenRukhEgg`
loads the complete real record and checks constant-token exclusion, delayed
controller, token characteristics and clone lifetime. The seven protection
records map to `TestRONWaitingDelayedTokenProtection`: their real costs, filters
and shield bodies can select a departed source retained only by a RON token count.
Those scenarios establish subrules; general `ChooseADamageSource` still rejects.
Existing token-creation tests retain payment, legality and simultaneous-batch
coverage. No complete-card coverage or loader acceptance gain is claimed.

## Waiting number snapshots and RON resolution values

`SnapshotNumber(ResolutionValue, *NumberBinding) ResolvingEffect` declares explicit
source reads in its operand to `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources()`.
Typed arithmetic, information, player and collection operands use the existing
source traversal. Zero values retain their declarations. Enumeration does not
read the value or write the binding. The saved source incarnation survives
phasing and departure; a returned card cannot replace it. Trigger detection ends
waiting availability. Implicit attachments, opaque values, saved numbers without
an object reference and future delays do not infer source reads (CR 400.7,
603.7a–e and 609.7a).

RON `CreateValueX(value)` in an action sequence lowers to `SnapshotNumber` and a
fresh per-instance number binding. Its operand uses the existing typed resolution
value compiler. Subsequent `ValueX` reads in that sequence and its nested bodies
read the saved number. A later producer reads the previous scope in its operand
and establishes a new binding for its continuation. A branch or future delay
cannot export a producer into its enclosing sequence. An announced X remains
available before a producer; the saved number takes precedence after it.
Contexts that require announcement or legacy values reject a saved-number read.
Dynamic resolution `PayManaX` accepts the saved number without changing announced
X, payment transactions or damage execution. The snapshot runs in action order,
not at announcement or trigger placement (CR 608.2c). Existing resolution frames,
delayed captures, stack copies and game clones retain separate values.

`TestWaitingDelayedNumberOperands`, `Purity` and `Scope` establish declaration,
identity, LKI, clone lifetime, zero operands and pure enumeration.
`TestRONCreatedValueSnapshot`, `Ordering`, `AnnouncedX`, `Invalid` and `Inventory`
establish lowering, dominance, repeated producers, copies, delayed transfer and
semantic operand reporting. `TestRONCreatedValuePrimordialOoze`, `OozeAttack` and
`OozePaymentTiming` load the complete Primordial Ooze record and cover its attack
requirement, controller upkeep, counter-before-payment order, paid/unpaid and
unaffordable payments, source departure/return, phasing, control and stack copies.
`TestRONCreatedValueProtection` covers real cost/filter/shield subrules for the
six Circles of Protection and Greater Realm of Preservation. Their complete
records still reject general damage-source aggregation.


## Source operands of waiting delayed prevention

Finite, unlimited-recipient, next-permanent-source and exact-source prevention
installations declare explicit source reads through `refersToSourcePermanent`.
`Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources() []DamageSource` retains the original
incarnation when a waiting body uses `This`, `DamageSourceOf(This)`, a typed
source-derived player or a typed finite amount. Arithmetic preserves declarations,
even for zero values. Queries do not resolve recipients, evaluate amounts, run
filters or install shields. Sequence traversal uses the existing declaration
service. Implicit attachments, opaque callbacks and future delayed bodies do
not infer references.

Departure and phasing retain exact information. A returned object cannot replace
the reference, and clearing short LKI does not erase exact departure information.
Queries copy mutable card facts; game clones keep independent waiting lifetimes.
One-shot detection ends this category before stack placement. Shield execution
still uses original recipient legality, exact source identity, current or retained
player information, shared replacement ordering, consumption and cleanup
(CR 400.7, 603.7a–e, 609.7a–b and 615.4/6/9).

RON finite prevention amounts now use the typed resolution-value adapter, including
created `ValueX`. Each factory receives its own binding; ordered snapshots and
copied delayed bodies retain independent resolution values. Amounts are read at
installation, and the installed finite shield does not track later value changes.
Literal negative amounts and invalid scope, arity or recipient declarations remain
errors. Computed nonpositive values create no effective prevention.

`TestWaitingDelayedPreventionOperands` covers all four native installer types,
source-derived players, zero values, six identity/control states, cleared LKI,
query snapshot isolation and clone lifetime. `TestWaitingDelayedPreventionPurityAndScope`
proves no query-time value evaluation and one installation-time evaluation,
and excludes implicit and future reads. `TestRONWaitingDelayedPreventionOperands`,
`CreatedAmount` and `Invalid` establish AST lowering, resolution timing, phasing,
returned recipient exclusion, copies, clone isolation, consumption and declaration
rejection. `TestRONWaitingDelayedPreventionProtection` uses complete records for
the six Circles of Protection and Greater Realm of Preservation to test their
cost/filter/shield subrules against a departed source retained only by a waiting
shield body. These records still reject general `ChooseADamageSource`; this is
subrule evidence, not full-card gameplay coverage. Existing finite-prevention,
recipient-prevention and allocation tests retain real-card payment, targeting,
replacement and simultaneous-damage evidence.

## Source operands of waiting delayed redirection

Both typed redirection installations implement the existing
`delayedSourcePermanentReference` declaration contract. Selected-source
redirection checks its damage source, permanent subject and player. Permanent
redirection checks its source, destination and player. The existing typed source
traversals recognize `This`, `DamageSourceOf(This)`, controller and owner reads.
Sequences preserve these declarations. Queries do not resolve operands, apply
filters, select sources or install rules. Implicit attachment references, opaque
references and future delayed bodies do not infer the current source.

`Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources` uses the saved delayed source incarnation,
current or exact retained information, isolated card snapshots and deterministic
deduplication. Departure, short LKI clearing and phasing retain eligibility;
return cannot replace the original object (CR 400.7, 702.26b). Detection ends
one-shot eligibility before pending placement (CR 603.7a–e). CR 609.7a permits
choice of the saved object without a damage ability. Queries and cloned games
retain separate mutable information and lifetimes.

Installation keeps the existing exact-identity contracts. A phased destination
can be saved at installation; damage cannot reach it until it phases in. A
returned destination cannot inherit the rule. A source-derived player is read
at installation, including exact departure information, then saved. Selected
source properties recheck at damage time (CR 609.7b). One-shot consumption,
simultaneous damage, replacement ordering, permanent-spell continuity, target
legality, cost rollback and cleanup retain their existing services.

`TestWaitingDelayedRedirectOperands` covers eight operand forms over six lifecycle
states, current control, cleared LKI, query snapshots and clone lifetime.
`TestWaitingDelayedRedirectScopeAndPurity` proves no query-time player resolution
and excludes implicit and future references. `TestRONWaitingDelayedRedirectOperands`
covers three fully lowered permanent redirection contexts over eight states,
including resolution timing, failed payment, stack copies and cleanup.
`TestRONWaitingDelayedSelectedRedirect` covers lowered selected-source subjects
and source-derived players with an explicit producer inside each delayed body;
copies retain separate controllers and independent one-shot rules.
`TestRONWaitingDelayedRedirectInvalid` rejects malformed or out-of-scope delayed
contexts. Existing native and RON selected/temporary redirection tests retain
invalid-definition, target, simultaneous, ordering and continuity coverage.

`TestRONWaitingDelayedRedirectProtection` reads the complete records of all six
Circles of Protection and Greater Realm of Preservation. Their actual costs,
filters and prevention bodies choose a departed source retained only by a waiting
redirection body. Payment failure makes no choice; paid resolution prevents one
event, then consumes the shield. These are subrule mappings, not full-card
acceptance. Jade Monolith's existing real target/redirection mappings and Shimian
Night Stalker's complete RON gameplay mappings remain in the regression suite.
No source spelling, registry or runtime cutover behavior changes.


## Source operands of waiting damage-source choices

`ChooseDamageSourceFrom(PlayerRef, []DamageSourceRef, *DamageSourceBinding)
ResolvingEffect` and `ChooseDamageSourceMatchingFrom(PlayerRef,
[]DamageSourceRef, DamageSourceFilter, *DamageSourceBinding) ResolvingEffect`
declare explicit permanent source reads in their player and fixed source list
through `damageSourceChoice.refersToSourcePermanent() bool`.
Category choices use the same typed player declaration. The query
`Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources() []DamageSource` retains the saved exact
incarnation when the player reads its controller or owner, or the list contains
`This` or `DamageSourceOf(This)`. Lists with duplicate operands still supply
one reference. Filters that cannot match do not remove declarations.

Queries do not resolve references or players, apply filters, select candidates,
write choice bindings or install damage rules. Implicit attachments, opaque
references, category enumeration alone and future delayed bodies do not infer
source reads. Departure and phasing retain the saved incarnation and current or
exact departure facts; a return cannot replace it. One-shot detection ends
waiting availability before stack placement. These boundaries follow CR 400.7,
603.7a–e, 609.7a–b and 702.26b.

Execution reuses source choice, exact-object deduplication, per-instance binding
frames, clone isolation and the shared damage/replacement services. RON reuses
`compileChosenDamageSourceChoice`, `compileSelfDamageSource`, `compilePlayerRef`,
`compileActions`, `compileExactSourcePrevention` and the existing category
lowering. No new RON spelling or general source aggregation is enabled.
`ChooseADamageSource/1` continues to reject in production.

`TestWaitingDelayedDamageChoiceOperands`, `PurityAndBoundaries` and `Invalid`
establish lifecycle declarations, snapshot isolation, query purity, implicit and
opaque boundaries, clone lifetime and definition validation.
`TestRONWaitingDelayedDamageChoiceOperands`, `Protection` and `Invalid` establish
RON typed operand and consuming-operation lowering, copies, failed payment,
resolution timing, exact identity, independent consumption and rejection of
invalid declarations. Jade Monolith supplies the target/redirection body; six
Circles and Greater Realm supply actual costs, filters and prevention bodies.
Their explicit-list/category test seams establish subrules, not complete-card
gameplay or complete CR 609.7a aggregation. Existing choice and redirection tests
continue to establish simultaneous packets, replacement ordering and legality.


## RON singular layer duration at end of combat

`CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil/3` accepts bare `UntilEndOfCombat` in each
supported resolving context. The compiler has no activation or trigger-event
restriction on this duration. The existing typed subject and modification
checks still apply. Collection layers and installed event subscriptions use
separate adapters and gain no support from this change.

The engine service is `Until(EndOfCombat, ...ContinuousModification)`.
It captures subject incarnations at resolution (CR 611.2a, 611.2c–d, 400.7).
Departure and removal from combat cannot transfer or end the saved modification.
A phase cycle keeps identity; application is suspended while phased out
(CR 702.26b). The end-of-combat step first detects triggers and runs priority.
Only then does native turn execution remove combat-duration effects and reset
combat (CR 511.2–3). Effects installed during that priority round expire at the
same boundary. Clones keep separate effect lists and expiry.

Glyph of Destruction's +10/+0 ends there. Its independent turn-long prevention
continues until cleanup, and its next-end-step destruction can still resolve.
Destruction permits regeneration. Returned or phased targets are illegal at
spell resolution; a resolved delayed destruction cannot follow a returned Wall.

Evidence: `TestEndCombatLayerPhaseBoundary`, `TestRONEndCombatLayerGlyph`,
`TestRONEndCombatLayerDelayedResolution`, and `TestRONEndCombatLayerInvalid`.
No new replacement ordering, cost transaction or damage batch behavior is
introduced. Those tests use the existing shared services.

## Token static quality ability isolation

`GrantBandsWithOther(PermanentRef, PermanentFilter) ContinuousModification`
grants one quality ability to a singular subject in layer 6. It uses the same
captured modification and combat services as `GrantEachBandsWithOther`.
Multiple qualities remain independent (CR 702.22c/m). They grant no ordinary
banding. Ability loss preserves a formed band but changes damage assignment
permission (CR 702.22b/e/j/k). Phasing suspends the ability (CR 702.26b).

`cloneTokenAbility` now copies static continuous effects with the existing
`deepCloneableEffect` service and existing copy fallback. Each token keeps its
own source state. Permanent spell copies and token `BaseCard.Copy` use this same service. The immutable
rule and filter declarations remain shared. Definition validation enters a
permanent ability context at `tokenAbilityDefinition`; its existing binding
scope still excludes producer targets and bindings. This supports a token's
`This` reference when its producer is a spell.

`TestTokenBandsCardCopy` verifies separate source state and continued original
quality after copy departure. `TestTokenBandsSingularGrant` verifies two batch members with two qualities,
singular membership, separate ability identities, removal, clone isolation,
phase cycles, restoration and nil-subject rejection. RON tests
`TestRONTokenBandsMaster`, `Combat`, `Lifecycle`, `SpellBatch` and `Invalid`
cover the full Master of the Hunt record, costs, timing, copied activations,
changed source controller/incarnation, token-card copies, named/type qualities,
attacking and blocking damage decisions, prevention and invalid declarations.

`Mill(PlayerRef, ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect` declares explicit source
reads from its player and amount to `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources()`.

remain rejected. Native `Mill` also rejects a negative `Fixed` declaration.
A nonpositive computed amount moves no cards. Optional mill costs retain their
positive fixed-count shape and transaction contract. All-player milling remains

CR 701.17a–b milling uses the existing shared mill service, modifiers and owner
ordering. This slice adds no replacement ordering policy or zone service.
Evidence: `TestWaitingDelayedMillOperands`, `TestWaitingDelayedMillPurityAndScope`,
`TestRONWaitingDelayedMillGameplay`, `Invalid`, `Instances`, `Modifiers` and

`TestRONMillstone`, `TestRONDeepSpawn*`, `TestRONMillModifiersAndPaymentFrames`
and `TestRONMillRealCardOwnerOrder` retain complete-record mill evidence.

`LookAtLibraryTopNumber(viewer, library PlayerRef, count ResolutionValue,

`Regenerate(subject PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect` declares an explicit `This`
subject to `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources()`. The query uses the shared
source-read declaration and saved delayed incarnation. It does not resolve a
subject, create a shield, consume a shield or change combat. Sequences and modes
preserve the declaration. Departure, cleared transient LKI and phasing keep the
reference until trigger detection. A returned object cannot replace it.
Implicit attachments, opaque references and nested future bodies do not infer
source reads. Target and saved bindings use the existing captured frame service.

At resolution the shared regeneration service protects only a present,
phased-in subject with the saved identity. Current control does not change that
identity. Copies create separate shields; clones keep separate frames and shield
lifetimes. Destruction consumes one shield, removes damage, taps the subject and
removes it from combat. Later shroud does not invalidate an already saved delayed
subject. A departed or returned target receives no shield. Implicit Aura hosts
use the attachment at body resolution (CR 400.7, 603.7a–e, 609.7a, 701.19a–c,
702.26b–d). No replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation contract changes.

RON `compileRegeneration(Node, scope) (effectFactory, error)` lowers
`RegeneratePermanent(permanent)/1` through `compilePermanentRef`. Existing source,
Aura host, target and event scopes remain unchanged, including supported delayed
resolving bodies. Wrong arity, wrong roles and unbound references reject before
factory publication. Fresh factories retain distinct target bindings.

Evidence: native `TestWaitingDelayedRegenerationOperands`, `Boundaries` and
`ModesAndPurity`; RON `TestRONWaitingDelayedRegenerationGameplay`, `Instances`,
`Invalid`, `Host`, `Records` and `Protection`. Seven complete protection records
supply actual costs, source filters and one-use prevention in category-specific
tests. Full general source choice remains rejected. Unchanged Drudge Skeletons,
Living Wall, Uthden Troll, Wall of Bone, Wall of Brambles, Will-o'-the-Wisp and
Regeneration records retain immediate gameplay evidence. This slice adds no
new complete-card compilation claim.

### Typed fight delayed source operands

`Fight(first, second PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect` declares a direct source
read in either operand to `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources`. The declaration
uses `permanentRefReadsSourcePermanent`; it does not resolve operands. Sequences
and delayed modes preserve it. Saved frames separately retain bound targets.
Implicit attachments, opaque references and future delayed bodies do not infer
reads. The query performs no damage, target choice or fight event.

The saved source incarnation remains available after departure, transient LKI
clearing and phasing until trigger detection. Returned objects cannot replace
it. Clones keep independent waiting lifetimes. Resolution still requires both
original objects to be present creatures; delayed saved references do not become
new targets. This establishes the source declaration, without changing the
existing simultaneous damage, prevention, replacement or fight-event services.
Rules: CR 400.7, 603.7a–e, 609.7a, 701.14a–d and 702.26b.

Evidence: `TestWaitingDelayedFightOperands`, `TestWaitingDelayedFightBoundaries`,
`TestRONFightArena`, `TestRONFightDelayed`, `TestRONFightHost`,
`TestRONFightSelfAndNoncombat`, `TestRONFightInstances`,
`TestRONFightWaitingProtection` and existing native `TestFight*` tests.

### Delayed battlefield-return controller source reads

`ReturnCardToBattlefield(card CardRef, controller PlayerRef,
options ...BattlefieldEntryOption) ResolvingEffect` declares an explicit source
read in its controller through `playerRefReadsSourcePermanent`. This covers
`ControllerOf(This)`, `ControllerOfWithLKI(This)` and `OwnerOf(This)`.
Sequences and delayed modes retain the declaration, including tapped entry.
The waiting query does not resolve either operand or move a card, and does not
infer an implicit host, opaque player or nested future body's references.

The saved source incarnation remains available after departure, transient LKI
clearing and phasing until detection. Returned objects cannot replace it.
Detection removes waiting availability before body resolution. Clones keep
independent waiting lifetimes. Existing saved target frames keep exact graveyard
visits; the return cannot follow a card that leaves and returns. Existing
controller information reads use current control or retained departure/phase
information for the exact source. `You` retains the delayed ability's controller.
This declaration does not change zone moves, entry replacement ordering,
simultaneous operations or cost transactions (CR 400.6–7, 603.7a–e, 609.7a,
702.26b–d).

RON supports one creature graveyard target with one entry operation, either
`EntersNormally` or `EntersUnderPlayersControl(player)/1`, in existing resolving
scopes. Invalid player roles, arity and scope reject before publication.

Evidence: `TestWaitingDelayedReturnController`, `TestWaitingDelayedReturnBoundaries`,
`TestRONWaitingDelayedReturnGameplay`, `Instances`, `Host`, `Invalid`, `Inventory`
and `Protection`, plus existing `TestRONGraveyardReturn*` and native typed
graveyard-return tests. Seven protection records gain bounded source-choice
evidence; this does not establish full general aggregation or Animate Dead
gameplay.

### Source reads in delayed library-choice amounts

`ScryAtResolution(amount ResolutionValue)` and
`SurveilAtResolution(amount ResolutionValue)` declare explicit source reads in
`amount` to `Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources`. Nested typed operands retain
these reads even when the resulting amount is zero. Enumeration does not resolve
values, inspect libraries, choose placement, move cards or emit action events.
Sequences and delayed modes retain the declaration. Implicit attachments,
opaque values and future delayed bodies do not infer a source read.

The waiting frame retains the exact source through departure, cleared transient
LKI and phasing. A returned object cannot replace it. One-shot trigger detection
ends waiting availability before body resolution; game clones have separate
waiting lifetimes. The body reads the amount once in its saved frame and uses
the delayed ability's controller with the existing scry/surveil services.
Current source control does not change that player. Nonpositive amounts make
no placement choice. Card inspection remains private.

Rules: local CR 603.7a–e, 609.7a, 701.22, 701.25 and 702.26b–d.
Evidence: `TestWaitingDelayedLibraryChoice*` and
`TestRONWaitingDelayedLibraryChoice*`. The RON tests use existing typed value,
cost, chosen-source filter and shield lowering with a native delayed library
body. There is no scry/surveil spelling in the collection, and this contract
adds none. Seven protection subrules gain bounded source-choice evidence;
general source aggregation and complete-card coverage remain separate gates.


## General CR 609.7a damage-source aggregation

`Game.DamageSourcesFor(uuid.UUID) []DamageSource` combines the existing live,
stack/resolving, waiting replacement/prevention, waiting delayed, and face-up
command categories. It keeps their lifetime and exact-information rules.
Current or retained incarnation, stack identity and zone-visit facts prevent a
returned object from replacing an earlier reference. A phased permanent is
excluded from live enumeration but can remain an explicitly referred source.
Sources of graveyard activated abilities also supply their saved graveyard
visit through the existing current/departure information reader. Removal of
the last referring ability ends availability; returning the card does not
replace the visit. The combined list removes exact duplicates; different casts and returned
incarnations remain separate. Results have separate mutable card data.

Hand information is normalized for the choosing player after collection,
including hand visits supplied only through captured damage-source bindings.
This prevents a category's public snapshot from hiding information from the
hand player or exposing private information to another player. Unreferred hand
cards remain excluded; a saved reference does not extend a reveal.

`ChooseDamageSource(PlayerRef, DamageSourceFilter, *DamageSourceBinding)
ResolvingEffect` uses this query at resolution, then filters and makes one
non-targeted choice. It clears a stale result if no player or matching source
exists. The shared chooser copies option data and validates the returned index.
Declaration validation requires a player and a named result binding. Queries
make no decisions, read no delayed operands and install no replacement rules.

RON lowering declares each result in the continuation of `ChooseADamageSource/1`
inside an action sequence. Factory instances allocate separate bindings;
branches do not export a declaration. The next-source prevention and targeted
redirection adapters retain their existing mechanics. Property mismatch does
not consume a shield; matching simultaneous damage consumes it once. Permanent
spells continue to their exact permanent before entry effects run. Native
replacement ordering and cost transactions remain in their shared services.
Rules: CR 120.7, 400.7, 603.7, 609.7a–b, 615.9 and 702.26b–d.

Evidence: `TestGeneralDamageSourceUnion`, `TestGeneralDamageSourceDeclarations`,
`TestGeneralDamageSourceStackAndPrivacy`,
`TestGeneralDamageSourceGraveyardAbility`, and `TestRONGeneralDamageSource*`.
The seven full protection records and Jade Monolith have complete RON gameplay
mappings. Existing bounded-category tests retain their behavior assertions and
now require the supported full records to compile. The three different
replacement bodies in Reverse Damage, Dark Sphere and Eye for an Eye still
reject. This section supersedes earlier claims that general aggregation is
unavailable; those sections retain their bounded operand contracts.

## Required player choices at resolution

`ChoosePlayer(PlayerRef, PlayerSet, *PlayerBinding) ResolvingEffect` makes a
non-targeting choice when its instruction resolves (CR 115.10 and 608.2c–d).
The chosen player is saved in the existing resolution frame. Reads require a
preceding producer. Empty membership or an absent chooser clears the binding;
independent later instructions still run. Multiple candidates use the specified
player's existing decision interface with bounds of one. Invalid responses use
the first legal candidate. No announcement target or random choice is added.

`PlayersWhoCastSorceryThisTurn() PlayerSet` reads existing cast-time history at
execution, in active-player-first order (CR 608.2i). Resolution and countering
do not erase a successful cast. Failed payments and copies do not add casts.
The turn tracker clears at final cleanup. This API does not track resolved
spells or their damage totals and does not supply arbitrary spell filtering.

Factory instances use separate typed declarations. Sequential choices do not
change earlier captures. Existing delayed frames retain saved player identities;
choices inside a delayed body run at resolution, using its saved controller.
Source control changes, phasing and returned sources do not replace that player.
The chooser and player set declare explicit source reads to waiting delayed
queries. Queries do not resolve those operands or make a decision. Saved source
incarnations and LKI use existing information services; clones retain separate
bindings and waiting lifetimes (CR 400.7 and 603.7).

Evidence: `TestPlayerChoiceResolution`, `AbsenceAndClone`, `Declaration` and
`WaitingSource`; `TestRONPlayerChoiceGameplay`, `SequenceAndDelay`, `CastHistory`,
`ActivationAndExplicitChooser`, `LateCastAndIndependentBindings`,
`SourceLifecycle`, `Invalid`, `InventoryAndAbilityScope`, `CompleteRecords` and
`RecordPrerequisites`. Exact Backdraft and Rainbow Vale choice nodes receive
prerequisite execution evidence. Complete-card gameplay remains blocked by
resolved-spell history and explicit-player control transfer, respectively.

## Fresh printed-definition construction plans

`NewCardDefinitionPlan(CardFactory) (*CardDefinitionPlan, error)` accepts pure,
instance-independent builders that return `*BaseCard`. It validates two builds
with `ValidateCardDefinition` and compares card identities, ability UUIDs,
cast/ability targets, nonempty pointer costs, and typed target and saved-binding
identities through the existing structural definition tree. Immutable values
can be shared. Zero-size costs have no instance state and are excluded from
pointer comparisons because Go can give them the same address. The builder
contract requires fresh declarations on every call; sampling is a declaration
check, not a proof that an arbitrary Go callback is pure.

`(*CardDefinitionPlan).Build() (Card, error)` validates a new build, checks it
against both private validation builds, and retains the plan on the new card.
The plan contains an immutable identity set and a construction callback; it
contains no game, owner, target selections or resolution frame. Nil builders,
nil results, unsupported card implementations, captured owners/source/controller,
preselected targets, shared declarations, invalid binding dominance and
builder panics produce errors. No game-time declaration panic is required.
`WithCardDefinitionPlan(*CardDefinitionPlan) CardOption` retains a construction
plan; `RebuildCardDefinition(Card) (Card, error)` uses it without a registry.
A legacy card without a plan returns an error. `BaseCard.Copy` preserves the
immutable plan; `CloneFrom` clears it before legacy rule replacement. Existing
copy, cast, zone, layer and replacement execution remains unchanged.
Definition validation now accepts the existing fixed 0/0 permanent collection
target contract. The collection remains empty and later instructions still run.
Zero-sized damage groups and other invalid target bounds remain rejected.

CR 707.2a requires the copied rules to supply the acquired abilities, and
707.6–7 requires independent entry choices and correctly linked copied
abilities. This slice supplies fresh printed declarations for later copy
services. It does not establish the current copiable snapshot required by
707.2–3, early entry copying under 707.5, copy exceptions under 707.9, or stack
choice transfer under 707.10. Those remain explicit dependencies.

Evidence: `TestCardDefinitionPlanFreshDeclarations`, `Invalid`, `BuildErrors`;
`TestRONDefinitionPlanGameplay`, `TargetsAndLKI`, `DelayedBindings`,
`AuraAndMetadata`, `AcceptedCollection`, `CopyConsumersRemainRejected`. Tests
cover new card/ability/target/binding identities, fresh owner and source context,
independent counter costs, failed mana payment, target departure information,
separate Aura attachments, saved delayed frames and game clones. All accepted
collection records are reconstructed and validated. The three copy consumers
remain rejected and receive no complete-card gameplay claim from this slice.

## Immutable permanent copiable snapshots

`(*Game).CaptureCopiableValues(*Permanent) (*CopiableValues, error)` reads the
current state of the supplied live incarnation. It uses the game's object, so a
corresponding reference in a clone reads that clone. A departed, returned or
phased object cannot supply a new capture. Previously saved values remain usable
through departure, control changes, phasing and source changes (CR 400.7,
707.2b). No LKI lookup, decision, payment, builder call or action occurs at capture.

The supported face-up context is a `BaseCard` with validated definition provenance,
or a prototype built from a saved snapshot. Printed name, mana cost and its
presence, color indicator, types, supertypes, subtypes, P/T, keyword seeds and
mode metadata are immutable. Fresh rules, targets, costs and bindings come from
the retained definition plan. Capture excludes ordinary layers, counters,
controller, owner, token status, attachments, entry choices and saved targets
(CR 707.2, 707.2a, 707.6). Snapshot builds have fresh identities and declarations.
Copying a snapshot prototype uses its same copiable provenance (CR 707.3).
Source choices and costs already paid do not transfer to the new instance.

Standard `Permanent.FaceDown` status supplies a nameless, colorless 2/2 creature
with no mana cost, supertypes, subtypes, keywords or abilities (CR 708.2a).
`(*CopiableValues).Build() (Card, error)` constructs a face-up prototype; it does
not copy face-down status or permit a face-up copy to turn up again. Its saved
values persist if the original turns face up. The engine's standard face-down
representation is the only face-down shape established here.

`(*CardDefinitionPlan).CopiableValues() *CopiableValues` exposes immutable printed
provenance. The plan checks printed metadata across its initial validation builds
and later builds. `WithCopiableValues(*CopiableValues) CardOption` retains that
provenance after construction. Capture checks both metadata and plan association.
`BaseCard.Copy` retains provenance and copies mutable hybrid-mana and color data;
`CloneFrom` and rule additions clear copy provenance. Builders must still obey
the existing pure, independent-declaration contract. Snapshot validation does not
prove arbitrary callback purity or permit mutation of lowered rule declarations.

`(*BaseCard).HasManaCost() bool`, `WithManaCostPresence(bool) CardOption` and
`(*CopiableValues).HasManaCost() bool` retain absent versus printed-zero costs.
Native constructors derive presence from the cost string. RON lowers field
presence, including explicit empty or zero-valued cost lists. This metadata does
not change legacy casting payment or permission checks; prototypes do not grant
casting permission (CR 202.1b and 118.6). Token status is also excluded: the caller
selects the new object's lifecycle.

Nil/uninitialized snapshots, absent games or objects, missing provenance,
untracked characteristic changes and mismatched plans return errors. For a
face-up source, any active legacy layer-1 effect causes conservative rejection,
because the legacy layer interface cannot declare complete affected subjects or
copiable values. A standard face-down source still has its complete replacement
characteristics. No legacy approximate copy result is used as a fallback.

This establishes saved prototypes, not early entry-copy scheduling, live copy
layer installation, exceptions under CR 707.9, special entry-set characteristics,
double-faced objects, nonstandard face-down shapes, or stack announcement copying.
Clone, Copy Artifact and Vesuvan Doppelganger still reject. Their later adapters
must use the snapshot and independent rule builders with their own entry/layer
contracts. Existing layer, replacement, damage and simultaneous services remain.

Evidence: native `TestCopiableValuesIndependence`, `FaceDownAndCopies`, `Invalid`,
`BuilderDrift`, `CostPresenceAndTokens`, `ReadOnlyAndColor`; RON
`TestRONCopiableValuesGameplay`, `LayersAndFaceDown`, `AuraTargets`,
`ProvenanceAndInvalid`, `ManaCostPresence`, `ColorIndicator`. Real records cover
Icatian Javelineers costs/entry/targets, Air Elemental with Giant Growth,
Holy Strength on Wall of Wood/Hill Giant, and Birds of Paradise metadata.
These tests supply prerequisite gameplay evidence, not new complete copy-card
coverage. The accepted-collection reconstruction regression remains required.


## Entry-copy physical identity

`BuildEntryCopy(original Card, values *CopiableValues) (Card, error)` builds
independent effective declarations for a physical card's next battlefield entry.
It also builds independent printed declarations for departure. Both retain the
original ID, owner and token status. The original card and the snapshot stay
unchanged. `WithPrintedCardDefinitionPlan` retains this separate printed origin
in RON factories; native `CardDefinitionPlan.Build` supplies it too.

Current copiable provenance must match the input's effective characteristics.
Missing, changed or mismatched provenance, nil IDs, nonpermanent definitions,
invalid snapshots and builder drift return errors before entry. Reapplying the
builder retains the original physical origin. Copying another copy's values
uses the new physical card's origin. Standard face-down snapshots produce a
face-up nameless 2/2 without transferring face-down status (CR 707.2–3, 708.2).

Normal entry executes acquired counters, choices and abilities with fresh
bindings (CR 707.5–7). Printed physical entry rules do not run. Phasing preserves
the copy. Destroy, sacrifice, direct graveyard placement, bounce, exile, ante,
legacy gathered bounce, return-to-hand costs and failed entry use the physical
printed card. LKI and queued abilities retain the battlefield copy's information
(CR 400.7, 603.6c). Ordinary Card.Copy and identity/owner setters keep departure
identity separate; game clones retain the origin through their existing card
sharing and zone cloning contracts.

This is a pure prototype-building prerequisite. The caller must remove the
physical card from its prior zone and supply entry permission, copy choices and
replacement ordering. It does not schedule copy replacements, supply copy
exceptions, attach copied Auras, install live copy layers or grant casting
permission. Clone, Copy Artifact and Vesuvan Doppelganger remain rejected.

Tests: native `TestEntryCopyIdentityInvalid`, `IndependentAndCopyOfCopy`,
`FaceDownAndTokens`; RON `TestRONEntryCopyIdentityGameplay`, `Departure`,
`EntryReplacements`, `DeathAndFreshEntryChoices`. Existing accepted-definition
and copy-consumer rejection tests retain the collection boundaries.

## Token copiable definition provenance

`NewTokenDefinitionFactory(build TokenDefinitionFactory)
(TokenDefinitionFactory, error)` validates a pure builder and independent token
rules with the shared card-definition plan. Nil builders, invalid declarations,
construction panics and shared scoped bindings return declaration errors.
The returned declarations retain a plan for fresh cards; game-time builds return
errors through the effect instead of raising declaration panics. Existing native
`DefineToken` callers keep their construction path.

RON lowers all currently supported creature token forms through this service.
`CreateTokenCopies`, `CreateTokenCopiesInto` and `CreateOneToken` build every card
before entering any member of the shared token batch. A later build failure
installs no members. Each result-producing effect clears its old result before
building. Entry replacement, simultaneous visibility and event ordering use the
existing entry batch; this service adds no replacement scheduling or new cost.

Tokens retain the characteristics and rules set by the creating instruction
(CR 111.3). The retained plan supplies copiable name, types, subtypes, colors,
printed P/T, keywords and independent abilities (CR 707.2–3). Token mana cost is
absent for these declarations (CR 111.3). Token status, owner, controller, counters, attachments and saved
choices do not transfer to a snapshot prototype (CR 707.2, 707.6).
`CopiableValues.Build` produces a nontoken prototype. `BuildEntryCopy` instead
preserves the physical object's token status while it applies the saved rules.
New capture requires a live exact incarnation; saved values remain usable after
phasing or departure. Standard face-down values keep their existing contract.
Untracked legacy definitions and copy layers still reject snapshot capture.

Tests: native `TestTokenDefinitionPlanInvalid`, `CreationAndDrift`, `ResultPaths`;
RON `TestRONTokenCopiableValuesGameplay` (The Hive, Boris Devilboon, Master of the
Hunt, Serpent Generator, with reconstructed poison trigger and physical departure)
and `Declarations` (15 token declarations from 17 complete unique records;
Stangg and Tetravus retain unsupported token forms). Existing creation and token
banding suites retain payment, combat, clone and simultaneous-entry contracts.
Clone, Copy Artifact and Vesuvan Doppelganger remain rejected pending scheduling
and copy exceptions. No complete copy-card gameplay is claimed.

## Optional early entry-copy scheduling

`MayCopyAsEnters(PermanentFilter) Ability` declares an optional copy replacement
on a permanent with a retained physical definition plan. The supported source
contract is the existing immutable copiable snapshot service, including supported
RON-created tokens, copied entries and standard face-down permanents. Legacy
untracked definitions and copy layers remain outside that snapshot contract.
No approximate copy or Go-card fallback is used.

Battlefield preparation creates an event-local `battlefieldEntryAction` before
entry counters, tapped status and ordinary entry operations. `EffectManager`
combines its current copy declarations with registered replacement candidates.
Existing priority selection and affected-player ordering apply (CR 616.1c,
616.1f). Each recheck reads the current effective definition. Rules removed by
copying cannot run; acquired copy rules can become applicable (CR 707.5).
A `(CardDefinitionPlan, ability position)` key retains one replacement object
through reconstruction. The shared applied set therefore prevents repeated use
of that declaration in one entry event (CR 614.5). Each subsequent entry has a
new applied set. Independent declarations remain separate choices.

The entry controller chooses at entry, after casting payments and resolution,
without targeting. Phased permanents are excluded. The chosen member is checked
against the original candidate incarnation and the current filter before capture
(CR 400.7, 702.26b). Invalid or absent chooser output uses the first legal offered
member, consistent with required native choices. An offered member that departed,
returned, phased or stopped matching cannot supply the copy. Empty sets and a
declined optional choice permit ordinary entry. Snapshot or physical builder
failure rejects entry through the existing failed-entry path; it cannot install
an approximate copy or execute the remaining entry operations.

The new effective permanent keeps the physical ID, owner, token status, entry
incarnation, controller and previously supplied entry state. Fresh attributes and
abilities come from the snapshot. It receives acquired entry counters and fresh
choices, not the source's counters or saved choices (CR 707.2, 707.5–7).
The existing entry-counter replacement pipeline and simultaneous token-entry
batch are retained. ETB abilities and outside observers see the copied permanent.
The existing physical departure and LKI services keep printed destination rules
and copied event information respectively. Phasing does not repeat entry.
Cloned pending spells use separate choices and declarations.

RON accepts a sole optional `EnterAsACopyOfAPermanent(filter, NoCopyEffects)`
under `AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent, ...)`, and the type additions below.
Other copy modifications, required or
mixed entry-copy sequences, external copy grants, live copy layers, back faces
and other face-down shapes remain separate contracts. This does not establish a
general migration of all legacy entry replacements to proposed entry events.

Tests: native `TestEntryCopyDeclaration`, `TestEntryCopyAcquiredRules`,
`TestEntryCopyRecheck`, `TestEntryCopyPriorityAndRepetition` and
`TestEntryCopyBatch`; RON `TestRONEntryCopyGameplay`, `TestRONEntryCopyInvalid`,
`TestRONEntryCopySources` and `TestRONEntryCopyAcquiredChoiceAndObserver`.
Real Clone scenarios cover payments, timing, decline, copied activation rollback,
phasing, departure/LKI, clone isolation, token and copied donors, face-down values
and acquired entry choices. Existing entry-copy identity tests retain copied death
abilities and all departure destinations. All six Clone reprints compile; Copy
Artifact now uses the copiable type-addition contract below. Vesuvan Doppelganger
still rejects its added-ability and live-copy rules.

## Copiable type additions in entry copies

`CopyAddCardTypes(...core.CardType) CopyModification` adds permanent types as
part of copying (CR 707.9b). `CopiableValues.WithModifications` creates a new
validated definition plan and snapshot without changing the source snapshot.
Each build reconstructs independent rules through the retained source plan.
Duplicate additions do not duplicate types. Existing abilities, including any
characteristic-defining abilities, remain (CR 707.9d). There is no Layer 4 effect
that reasserts the exception after later type changes: modified copiable values
supply the starting characteristics before ordinary layers (CR 613.1a/d, 613.2c).
Later copies inherit those values (CR 707.3). Ordinary layers remain excluded.

`MayCopyAsEntersWithModifications(PermanentFilter, ...CopyModification) Ability`
uses this snapshot before `BuildEntryCopy` and the existing copy-priority entry
pipeline. Type-only derived plans retain their original declaration provenance.
The event key still identifies each existing ability position, so reconstruction
cannot repeat an already used replacement (CR 614.5). Type additions cannot
create a new rule or remove the existing abilities. Later entries use fresh
applied sets. Future ability-changing exceptions need their own provenance.

Nil modifications, empty type additions, invalid types and Instant/Sorcery type
additions reject during definition validation. Missing snapshots and failed
builders return errors. Entry failure keeps the existing failed-entry path.
Supported RON spelling is the sole optional entry-copy context with nonempty
`CopyEffects([AddCardtypes([...]), ...])`. Other modifications remain rejected;
color retention uses the contract below. Added abilities and live layers still reject.

Physical identity, ownership, departure rules, LKI, choice timing, phasing,
replacement priority and simultaneous preparation retain the existing contracts.
Native `TestCopyTypeModificationSnapshots`, `TestCopyTypeModificationInvalid`,
`TestCopyTypeModificationRepetition` and `TestCopyTypeModificationBatchAndPriority`
cover immutable inputs, fresh rules, entry counters, ordinary-layer exclusion,
invalid declarations, one-use identity, fresh later entries, copy priority and
independent simultaneous entries. RON `TestRONCopyTypeModificationGameplay`,
`TestRONCopyTypeModificationManaAndLegality`, `TestRONCopyTypeModificationLayers`,
`TestRONCopyTypeModificationComposedTypes` and `TestRONCopyTypeModificationInvalid`
cover real Copy Artifact with Juggernaut/Sol Ring donors, copied combat/mana rules,
payment rollback, entry timing, nontarget choice, subsequent Clone copying,
phasing, cloned pending-spell choices, departure/LKI, Disenchant legality,
ordinary type/color/P/T layers, cleanup, composed additions and rejection.
All six Copy Artifact reprints compile; compilation and gameplay evidence remain
separate from complete collection validation.

## Retained copy colors and color-definition omission

`CopyRetainColors(...core.Color) CopyModification` supplies immutable saved
colors to `CopiableValues.WithModifications`. Empty sets are explicitly
colorless, separate from absent overrides that derive colors from mana cost.
The constructor normalizes Colorless and duplicates, copies input slices and
rejects AnyColor or invalid values during validation. The donor's name, mana
cost, types, P/T and remaining rules retain their existing copy contracts.
The donor's color indicator is replaced, not combined with the saved colors
(CR 707.9c–d). Subsequent copies keep these values (CR 707.3, 707.9b).

`ColorCharacteristicDefinition` is the explicit copy classification contract
for static continuous effects. `DefinesColor() bool` must return true for a
color-defining effect and false, or remain absent, for an ordinary color change.
When an effect in a StaticAbilityHolder defines color, the whole ability is
omitted from the modified definition (CR 707.9d). Other abilities remain,
including P/T definitions and ordinary color effects. This contract does not
introduce a color-CDA constructor or change all-zone color evaluation.

`MayCopyAsEntersKeepingColors(PermanentFilter, ...CopyModification) Ability`
reads the entering object's copiable colors at replacement application. The
current definition supplies these colors before ordinary color layers (CR 613.2).
A changed spell color can continue to entry as an ordinary color effect, but it
cannot enter the retained copiable values. Later copies inherit the retained
colors; ordinary layers remain excluded from copy snapshots.
Choice remains optional and nontargeted at resolution, before later entry
replacements, counters and triggers (CR 614.12, 707.5). Replacement keys use the
original plan and the entry-copy rule ordinal, so omitting another ability
cannot repeat an already applied rule in the same entry (CR 614.5). Later
entries start fresh. No new provenance is inferred for added abilities.

Physical departure restores printed rules; departure LKI retains the copied
object's current colors. Phasing keeps copied values without another choice.
Snapshots, payment transactions, clone isolation and simultaneous entry
preparation use the existing shared services. No copy state is stored globally.

Native TestCopyColorSnapshots covers colored, multicolor, colorless, duplicate,
immutable-input, indicator, fresh-rule, entry-counter, ordinary-layer and invalid
color cases. TestCopyColorDefinitionAndReplacementIdentity distinguishes a
color definition from an ordinary color-changing ability, proves omission,
donor independence and one-use entry identity. TestCopyColorBatchAndPriority
covers separate color sets within one batch, early replacement priority and
invalid entry declarations. RON TestRONCopyColorGameplay uses complete Birds of
Paradise and Clone records as donor and subsequent-copy interactions. It covers
nontarget choice of a shrouded donor, colors, copied flying/type/mana metadata,
ordinary layers, phasing, cloned-game changes, physical departure/LKI and return.
TestRONCopyColorSpellTiming covers failed payment, resolution-time choice,
spell color continuity without inclusion in copiable values, subsequent copying
and cloned pending-spell decline.
TestRONCopyColorInvalid and Dependencies cover invalid symbols and all six
Vesuvan Doppelganger reprints' continued rejection at AddAbility. The synthetic
KeepColor producer does not claim complete Doppelganger gameplay.

## Next combat-source event with an unprevented amount

`PreventNextCombatDamageFromPermanentExcept(PermanentRef, PlayerRef,
ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect` installs one end-of-turn source-prevention rule
in the existing replacement service. Installation requires a present, unphased
creature and an existing player. The source incarnation, recipient and amount
are saved at resolution. Nil/unbound/undeclared references, nil amounts and
negative fixed amounts reject during definition validation. Dynamic negative
amounts become zero. Later power changes do not recalculate a saved amount.

The rule matches positive combat damage to that player from the exact creature.
Creature type is checked with current or exact retained source information
(CR 609.7b, 615.9). It does not reselect a source or follow a returned card
(CR 400.7). Phasing keeps saved identity and does not consume a shield.
Noncombat damage, zero damage and damage to another recipient do not use it.
An absent or phased subject at installation produces no rule. Forcefield's
unblocked choice remains in the existing resolution-time permanent-choice set;
this engine operation does not impose a targeting or combat-choice restriction.

All matching packets in one simultaneous event share the saved unprevented
amount. The rule is applied once per packet through the existing batch pipeline;
actual prevention in any matching packet consumes it for later events. A packet
or event that prevents no damage keeps the shield under CR 609.7b. Thus a
one-point Forcefield event leaves its shield available, and two independent
shields need not both be consumed by the same event. If another prevention
removes the event, unapplied shields remain. Affected-player replacement order
and rechecks use the shared service (CR 614.5, 616.1). Damage history, lifelink and
notifications use the resulting damage, not the originally proposed amount.

The existing source-replacement clone and cleanup paths isolate consumption and
expire the rule. `WaitingPreventionPermanentSources` supplies the exact source
while active, including a shield that prevented no damage. Explicit source reads
in subject, player and amount also qualify in waiting delayed bodies; queries do
not install prevention or read amounts. No new damage-source category or
unpreventable-damage rule is introduced.

Native evidence: `TestNextCombatPreventionIdentity`, `BatchAndAmount`, `Order`,
`Declarations`, `IndependentBindings`, `AmountAndWaiting` and `ActualDamage` cover
identity/LKI with cleared cache, phasing, control, property rechecks, cleanup,
clones, simultaneous packets, zero/large allowances, no-prevention retention,
competing shields, payment failure, stack copies, saved amounts, waiting queries,
actual combat notifications and lifelink. Existing next-source tests retain
prior API behavior. RON `TestRONNextCombatPreventionForcefield` executes all five
complete records with failed payment, nontarget shrouded choices, empty early
choice, deferred decisions, double strike and pending clones. `Lifecycle` covers
phase cycles, return exclusion, provider departure, later blocked status and
cleanup. `Invalid` rejects unsupported shapes and `Inventory` checks semantic
source/amount roles. This adds full-record Forcefield gameplay coverage without
claiming complete collection gameplay.

## Proposed amounts and outcomes of selected-source prevention

`PreventNextDamageFromSelectedSourceWithOperations(source DamageSourceRef,
recipient PlayerRef, filter DamageSourceFilter, operations
...SourcePreventionOperation) ResolvingEffect` accepts one
`PreventProposedDamage(amount ProposedDamageValue)` followed by at most one
`GainLifeFromPreventedDamage(player PlayerRef)`. Definition validation rejects
empty, nil,
reversed or duplicate operations, nil amounts, invalid filters and nil or
unbound references. Existing selected-source and exact-source APIs keep their
contracts.

`ProposedDamageAmount()` and `HalfProposedDamageRoundedDown()` are immutable
values that read the positive matching damage when prevention applies, after
previous replacements. They cannot read resolution bindings. All matching
simultaneous packets from the saved source to the saved player form one amount;
half is rounded down once, then removed across those packets. Other sources and
recipients do not contribute. Single-event and batch execution use the same
amount operation. Actual prevention consumes the rule before its additional
life gain; prevention of zero keeps the rule (CR 609.7b and 615.8). Each packet
marks the rule applied even when it prevents zero (CR 614.5).

The additional life gain saves its own typed player at installation, separate
from the protected player. RON implicit `GainLife` uses the saved action
controller (`You`), even when the event protects another player. Explicit source
reads in the gain player also qualify for waiting delayed queries without
resolving that player. The additional gain uses this rule's actual prevention,
once per source event. It takes place immediately after the original damage
event (CR 615.5) through
`gainLifeWithEvent`, including modifiers, life-gain replacements, Lich, history
and actual-gain triggers. Single and simultaneous damage keep a local list of
additional outcomes; all original damage finishes before those gains run. No
result is stored on the game or in a global action slot. Damage caused during
a life-gain replacement cannot
reuse the consumed rule. Prevented damage never enters damage history or
supplies lifelink. The shared pipeline retains affected-player replacement
choices and rechecks (CR 616.1).

Source selection remains a resolution-only non-target choice. Installation saves
an exact source and player, independent of later bindings. Current or retained
source properties, spell identity, permanent-spell continuity before entry,
returned-incarnation exclusion, phasing, waiting queries, cleanup and clone
isolation use the existing selected-source services. This adds no general
unpreventable-damage contract or arbitrary replacement-body executor.

RON supports `NextTimeDamageWouldBeDealtThisTurnBySourceToRecipient(
TheChosenDamageSource, Player(playerRef))` inside `CreateFuturePreventDamage/2`
in resolving action contexts. Its operation list starts with bare
`PreventThatDamage` or `PreventSomeOfThatDamage(proposedValue)`. A proposed value
is bare `WouldDealDamage_ThatMuchDamage` or
`HalfRoundedDown(WouldDealDamage_ThatMuchDamage)`. An optional second operation
is `GainLife(TheAmountOfDamagePreventedThisWay)`. The proposed amount and actual
result are private to this operation list and cannot appear in normal actions,
costs or other value contexts. Wrong arities, unbound choices, incompatible
recipients, reversed or repeated operations and other value forms reject before
factory publication. RON owns syntax and lexical scope; mage owns the rules.

Evidence: native `TestSourcePreventionOperationsAmounts`, `Identity`,
`Declarations`, `Order`, `LifeGain`, `SpellIdentity`, `LifeOutcomes`,
`AdditionalEffectTiming` and `GainPlayerAndWaiting`; RON
`TestRONSourcePreventionOperationsGameplay`, `Invalid`, `Inventory`, `Lifecycle`,
`CopyBindings`, `SupportedPrograms`, `Combat` and `ExplicitPlayers`. Gameplay
covers the complete Dark Sphere record and all six
Reverse Damage records, including payment, sacrifice, source choices,
simultaneous outcomes, lifelink, spell continuation, copies and clones.

## Temporary mana type replacements

`ReplaceTappedManaTypeForPlayerThisTurn(player PlayerRef, filter PermanentFilter,
 to Color) ResolvingEffect` saves the player at resolution. It changes every
mana type produced by a matching permanent controlled by that player when that
player activates its mana ability with a tap symbol. Membership and control are
read at production. Later entries qualify. Source departure and ability removal
do not end the effect; cleanup ends it.

`ReplaceTappedManaTypeUntilLeaves(subject PermanentRef, from, to Color)
 ResolvingEffect` saves a present incarnation at resolution. It changes only the
specified type when that permanent is tapped for mana, regardless of controller
or later subtype changes. Phasing suspends production but preserves the rule.
Departure ends it permanently, including leave-and-return of the physical card.
Both declarations require concrete types and valid typed operands.

The internal `manaProductionAction` carries one proposed production event with
its source incarnation, activating player, tap-symbol context and independent
production entries. Shared replacement candidates, priorities, affected-player
choices and once-per-event application implement CR 106.12b and 616.1. Amounts
and spending restrictions remain on their entries (CR 106.6). Actual produced
types supply tap bonuses and `EvtTappedForMana`; separate typed add instructions
remain separate production events. Spells, non-tap conversions and triggered
bonus production cannot inherit a tap-symbol context.

Manual, direct and typed mana activation use the replacement pipeline before
pool addition. Automatic planning enumerates pure typed transformations with the
same candidate and priority checks. It makes no choices or resource changes.
Conditional type replacement enumerates concrete color choices; identical rule
transformations and equivalent projection states avoid permutation repetition.
Execution rechecks the selected source, output, restrictions, costs and bonuses
before payment and runs its selected replacement order. Stable rule IDs keep
orders valid in cloned games. Planned bodies retain their delayed operations.
Failed casting payments keep live sources, pools, hands and stacks unchanged.

`(*Game).ManaTypesAbilityCouldProduce(ability Ability, sourceID uuid.UUID)
 []Color` includes all possible type outcomes without checking payment or tapped
status (CR 106.7). The opponent-land color service uses it. Existing raw mana
production metadata APIs retain their behavior.
`(*Game).WaitingManaReplacementPermanentSources() []DamageSource` supplies exact
subjects of active indefinite mana replacements to general damage-source choices
(CR 609.7a). A phased subject remains available; departure ends its reference.
Player/filter replacements do not invent permanent references.

RON accepts two resolving-action contexts:

- `CreateReplaceWouldProduceManaUntil(
  PlayerTappingAPermanentWouldProduceMana(You, controlledFilter),
  [WouldProduceMana_ReplaceType(concreteType)], UntilEndOfTurn)`.
  `controlledFilter` must include `ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))` and
  cannot exclude the source. Existing independent permanent filters compose.
- `CreateReplaceWouldProduceManaUntil(
  TappingPermanentWouldProduceMana(permanentRef),
  [WouldProduceMana_ReplaceTypeOfType(fromType, toType)],
  UntilPermanentLeavesBattlefield(theSamePermanentRef))`.
  Typed references retain declaration scopes and per-instance target bindings.

Other events, operations, recipients and durations remain compilation errors.
RON owns syntax and declaration checks; mage owns event mechanics and identity.
Local `data/LEG.json` Oracle text requires Quarum Trench Gnomes to replace white
mana only. Its sole RON record now uses the explicit two-type operation. Deep
Water retains its all-type operation and preserves the produced amount.

Evidence: native `TestManaTypeReplacementProductionPaths`, `WhiteOnly`,
`Declarations`, `AnyColorPlanning`, `OrderAndPurity`, `RestrictionsAndBonuses`,
`TimingAndIdentity`, `NonTapAndZero`, `CouldProduce`, `RepeatedOrders`,
`WaitingSubject`, and `StalePlanAndRollback`; RON
`TestRONManaTypeReplacementCompleteRecords`, `Invalid`, `Lifecycle`,
`GnomesTargetPayment`, `CopyAndInstances`, and `Inventory`. Complete-record
behavior mappings cover Deep Water and Quarum Trench Gnomes, two unique names
and two records. They do not establish complete collection gameplay coverage.

## Typed library-top ante actions

`AnteTopFor(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect` and
`AnteTopEach(subjects PlayerSet) ResolvingEffect` select players at resolution.
`(*Game).AnteLibraryTops(players []uuid.UUID)` moves each eligible current top
from that player's library to the shared public ante zone. It preserves card ID,
owner and remaining library order. Duplicate player IDs contribute once;
unknown players, empty libraries, tokens and tops owned by another player do
not contribute. Ante-disabled and settled games perform no movement. An
ineligible player does not prevent another player from performing the action.

All moves finish before any library-to-ante zone event (CR 101.4). Each moved
card supplies one `EvtZoneChange` with its ID and library player, from
`ZoneLibrary` to `ZoneAnte`. No draw, reveal choice, payment, ownership change
or random selection occurs. Existing `MoveToAnte` behavior for other zones is
unchanged. Legacy `AnteLibraryTop().Targeting(...)` now shares this batch service.
CR 407.2 establishes public ante; CR 407.4 restricts ante to the owner.
CR 609.3 permits other instructions to continue when a library is empty.

Typed operands retain existing per-instance player bindings, exact source
incarnations, LKI and clone behavior. Explicit source reads qualify for waiting
queries without executing the action. A delayed source-controller operand
cannot follow a returned source. Each spell copy reads its own controller and
current library top; no top-card result is saved globally.

RON supports bare `AnteTopCardOfLibrary` in ordinary resolving actions,
`PlayerAction(playerRef, AnteTopCardOfLibrary)`, scoped `PlayerActions` bodies,
and `EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer, AnteTopCardOfLibrary)`. Existing trigger, modal,
conditional and delayed action contexts use the same adapter. Tuple spellings,
cost, entry and static contexts reject. The all-player form permits only bare
`AnyPlayer`; it does not create an `ActionPlayer` binding. Optional ante payments
and paid-player results remain separate unsupported contracts.

Contract from Below also routes bare ordinary `DiscardHand` into the existing
`DiscardMatchingHand` adapter. Discard, ante and draw run in the printed order
(CR 608.2c); hand discard retains its existing replacements and batch events.
No new hand-discard rule is established here.

Evidence: native `TestAnteTopBatch`, `Legality`, `BatchIdentityAndClone` and
`Definition`, existing `TestAnteLibraryTopTargetsControllerOrEachPlayer`; RON
`TestRONAnteTopCards`, `PlayerScopes`, `SequenceEvents`, `DelayedIdentity`,
`CopiesAndEmpty` and `Invalid`. The complete real records for Demonic Attorney
and Contract from Below run for all six reprints and both players. No source
record changed. Ante payments, outside-game admission and ownership exchange
are outside this contract.

## Typed resolution ante payments

`AnteTopCost() Cost` pays with the payer's current library top. The shared
payment transaction locks each successive top on its validation game. It checks
all locked payments on a separate game before spending live mana or other
resources. Empty libraries, foreign-owned cards, tokens, disabled ante and
settled games cannot pay. Affordability queries do not move cards or offer choices.
Direct payment and transactional payment use `AnteLibraryTops` for movement.

`PayPermanentAnteOrElse(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef, paid, unpaid
ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect` offers a payment with one exact permanent.
`AntePermanentOrElse` has the same signature and performs a mandatory payment
without a may choice. The permanent is captured before an optional offer.
The payer must own it, but need not control it (CR 407.4). Phased or departed
subjects cannot pay. A returned card cannot replace the captured incarnation
(CR 400.7). The transaction uses `MoveToAnte`, with existing departure/LKI,
attachment and zone-event behavior. This is neither destruction nor sacrifice;
regeneration and graveyard-destination replacements do not apply.

Each result is local to its invocation and selects exactly one branch after
payment (CR 118.3, 118.10–12). Missing players perform no branch. A nil branch
performs no action; two nil branches are invalid. Definitions validate typed
players, subjects and non-nil branch declarations. Delayed queries enumerate
explicit source operands and bodies without resolving them or offering payment.
Pending copies use their own payer, saved source and frame; clones keep separate
zone storage and delayed lifetimes.

RON supports `MayCost(AnteTopCardOfLibrary)` and
`PlayerMayCost(playerRef, AnteTopCardOfLibrary)`; `MayCost`, `PlayerMayCost` and
`MustCost` support `AnteAPermanent(SinglePermanent(permanentRef))`. These forms
require an adjacent `If`, `Unless` or `IfElse` on bare `CostWasPaid` or
`CostWasntPaid`, with nonempty action lists. Existing resolving spell, activation,
trigger and delayed contexts use the same adapter. Per-factory references retain
lexical bindings. No result is available outside its continuation. Activation
costs, entry/static operations, mandatory top payments, arbitrary permanent
collections and `EachPlayerMayCost` are not supported by this adapter.

Evidence: native `TestAntePayment*` covers owner/control distinctions, token,
phasing, return, offer-time return, disabled/settled games, exact physical IDs,
transaction rollback and stale preflight. `TestRONAntePayment*` covers actual
casting and activation, branch-local nested results, explicit target payers,
permanent subjects, clone/copy behavior, delayed identity and invalid contexts.
Jeweled Bird's retained payment subrule uses a draw continuation. Its complete
record and ante movement now have separate `TestRONAnteMovement*` coverage.
Rebirth's complete record still rejects paid-player collection dispatch. These
are prerequisite mappings, not complete-card gameplay claims.

## Exact ante card targets

`DeclareAnteCardTarget(name string) *CardTargetBinding` declares exactly one
card in the shared, public ante zone. It has no ownership restriction. The
existing `CardRef` and target declaration validation supply typed reads and
per-instance identity. Disabled or settled ante games supply no candidates.

Each ante arrival has a separate visit. `SetAnte` keeps visits of cards that
remain in the zone, including copy-on-write ownership changes. Removing a card
ends its visit; adding that physical card again creates a new visit. Existing
initial ante, `MoveToAnte` and `AnteLibraryTops` use this same storage. Clones
keep visits and separate subsequent mutations.

Casting and activation save ante targets before payment. The existing stack,
resolution and copy services retain the saved zone and visit. An absent or
returned target is illegal (CR 400.7 and 608.2b). No LKI makes it available.
An ownership change alone keeps it legal. Copies without new target choices
retain the old visit. A legal new choice can select the current visit of the
same physical card. Queries do not move cards, make choices or consume RNG.

RON supports `TargetAnteCard(AnyCard)` in the existing singular `Targeted`
spell, activation and trigger contexts. It declares local `Ref_TargetAnteCard`
as a typed card reference with a fresh binding per factory instance. Other
filter shapes and incompatible permanent/player/graveyard reads reject at
compilation. Inventory descends into the still-unsupported exchange action.
Targeting alone does not supply movement or ownership exchange. The movement
contract below establishes a separate ante-to-graveyard operation.

Native `TestAnteReference*` covers visits, current ownership, typed reads,
prepayment capture, zone changes during payment, clone isolation, copies,
legal retargeting and all existing ante arrival paths. `TestRONAnteReference*`
covers casting, failed payment, return illegality, independent activations,
entry triggers, invalid declarations and semantic inventory. Darkpact's actual
target subrule runs with a test-only life continuation; all six complete
records still reject their exchange action. This is prerequisite gameplay
coverage, not complete Darkpact coverage. Complete Jeweled Bird coverage is
recorded in the ante-to-graveyard movement contract below.


## Typed ante-to-graveyard movement

`AnteCardsOwnedBy(owner PlayerRef) AnteCardSet` selects exact current ante
visits with that current owner, across both players' storage. Selection is pure.
`OtherAnteCards(subjects AnteCardSet) AnteCardSet` excludes the physical source
card after payment moves it to ante (CR 400.7j).
`PutAnteCardsInGraveyards(subjects AnteCardSet) ResolvingEffect` saves the
selection once, removes duplicate visits, and moves each available card to its
current owner's graveyard. Ownership changes do not replace a visit. Departure
and return do. Disabled or settled ante games and missing owners move nothing.

Owner-controlled graveyard order uses the existing card-choice service and the
same helper as milling. Choices follow APNAP order (CR 101.4), use card copies,
and precede all movement. Invalid answers use the first remaining card. The
operation preserves prior graveyard order (CR 400.5 and 404.3). Exact visits and
ownership are checked again after choices. All moves finish before zone events;
events identify the destination owner. New graveyard visits use existing player
storage. This is neither a death nor milling; battlefield-departure replacements
and mill modifiers do not apply. No general zone replacement contract is added.
Clones retain separate zone storage. No absent-card LKI enables movement.

RON action shape: `PutEachCardFromAnteInGraveyard(OwnedByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(playerRef)))`.
The owner uses existing typed player references in resolving spell, activation
and trigger action contexts. `Other(OwnedByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(playerRef)))`
is supported only in the paid branch of an adjacent source-permanent ante
payment and its immediate nested actions. It is rejected outside that branch,
on unpaid paths and in delayed bodies. Entry, cost and static contexts reject.
Other filter shapes, invalid arity and unbound/incompatible references reject
at compilation. Inventory classifies the operands as ante card filters, player
filters and player references, including descendants of rejected declarations.

Jeweled Bird's full ARN record uses explicit `Other(...)` to preserve Oracle's
“all other cards.” `TestRONAnteMovementJeweledBird` covers payment, source
exclusion, ownership/control distinctions, departed/returned/phased sources,
clones, ability copies, empty other-card sets and drawing. `BirdSequenceAndOrder`
covers deck preparation, tap payment, owner order, simultaneous movement and
payment-before-movement-before-draw. `ExplicitPlayerAndInventory`, `Declarations`
and `SourceScope` cover typed owners, reporting and invalid declarations.
Native `TestAnteMovement*` covers saved visits, ownership changes, duplicates,
multiple owners, APNAP decisions, invalid choices, return during a decision,
clone storage and invalid definitions. Existing mill-order tests protect the
shared helper's callers. Darkpact still rejects its ownership/exchange operation;
