the exact ante-departure helper is available for that later atomic operation.


## Typed ante ownership and library exchange

`AcquireCardOwnership(card CardRef, owner PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect` changes
ownership through `Game.ChangeOwner`. It requires a present nontoken card and
an existing player in an enabled, unsettled ante game (CR 407.3). It does not
move the card, change its visit or alter a controller. Copy-on-write replacement
keeps game clones separate and preserves original-owner settlement history.
Graveyard replacement now keeps the selected and neighboring cards' visits;
`SetGraveyard` retains its existing whole-zone replacement behavior.
Hand, exile and ante replacement retain their existing visit preservation.
Saved card references supply no LKI permission to act on departed objects.

`ExchangeAnteCardWithLibraryTop(card CardRef, player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`
requires a current exact ante visit owned by the selected player. A nonempty
library must have a nontoken top owned by that same player (CR 701.12a/d).
The action reads the top at resolution. It moves the ante card to the top of
that library and the former top to ante, with both moves complete before zone
events. An empty library receives the ante card (CR 701.12d). The library tail
keeps its order. Ante departure ends its visit; the incoming top gets a fresh
ante visit (CR 400.7). An invalid operand prevents the entire exchange.
This operation does not acquire ownership. A preceding ownership instruction
still succeeds if a foreign-owned or token library top prevents exchange.
No draw, reveal, shuffle, payment or battlefield event is added.

RON shapes are `AcquireOwnershipOfCard(anteCardRef, playerRef)` and
`ExchangeAnteCardWithTopCardOfPlayersLibrary(anteCardRef, playerRef)` in resolving
spell, activation and trigger actions. `anteCardRef` must be the bound
`Ref_TargetAnteCard` from `TargetAnteCard(AnyCard)`. Player operands use the
existing typed player grammar and per-instance bindings. Wrong arity, kind,
zone, unbound references and cost, entry or static uses reject at compilation.
Semantic inventory classifies both operands as card/player references.
Explicit source reads in the player operand are declared to waiting delayed
queries; the queries do not resolve operands or change ownership or zones.

All six Darkpact records now contain the missing independent Oracle ownership
instruction before exchange. Local `data/LEA.json` supplies the Oracle evidence.
`TestRONAnteExchangeDarkpact` covers every reprint, payment rollback, timing,
foreign ante ownership, empty and foreign-owned libraries, target departure and
return, spell copies, clone isolation and the spell's final graveyard move.
`TestRONAnteExchangeContextsAndInstances` covers independent activations,
triggers, source phasing and source return; declaration/role tests reject invalid
forms. `TestAnteExchange*` covers native atomic events, exact visits, current
tops, disabled/settled games, missing players, token tops, independent ownership,
other nonbattlefield zones, settlement and definition validation.

This contract does not implement two-card ownership exchange, result-bound exile
or reveal adapters, paid-player collections or general zone replacements.
Bronze Tablet and Tempest Efreet remain rejected; Rebirth needs paid-player
collection dispatch. Go definitions and the legacy DSL remain until the runtime
and removal gates pass.

### Oracle card name catalog and resolution choice (CR 201.4)

`OracleCardNameCatalog` is separate from the card factory registry. It supplies
all nontoken English names in the retained Scryfall catalog snapshot, including
cards outside the game's format and executable collection. CR 201.4 prohibits
token-only names. CR 201.4b–f permits individual split, flip, double-faced, meld
and adventure names. Combined ` // ` names are split and not offered as choices.
The canonical embedded asset contains 35,919 unique sorted face names from
35,137 source entries. The interchangeable-name supplement below adds 31
original English names, for 35,950 choices. Source URIs, retrieval times and
hashes are retained beside the assets. Runtime choice does not make a network
request or load Go card definitions.
Source: https://scryfall.com/docs/api/catalogs/card-names.

`ChooseCardName(PlayerRef, *CardNameCatalog, *CardNameBinding) ResolvingEffect`
performs a required choice during resolution, using the resolved explicit player.
Announcement, affordability and static/waiting queries do not choose names.
The decision receives separate list storage through existing `Player.ChooseMode`.
An invalid response uses the first legal entry, consistent with other required
choice recovery. An absent chooser clears the result without a decision.
Definition validation rejects nil operands, empty catalogs and unnamed bindings.
Results have per-binding, per-resolution storage; frame cleanup clears them,
clones copy them, nested applications restore outer results, and loops isolate
member choices. Pending stack copies make their own choices. No zone operation,
replacement ordering or simultaneous operation is part of choosing a name.

The chooser declares explicit source reads for waiting delayed references.
Queries do not choose names. Existing permanent references and LKI keep the
original chooser after source departure/return, and phasing keeps the reference.
Choice inside a delayed body is supported; capture of a prior name result by a
delayed consumer is not established here. No chosen-name characteristic or
interchangeable-name matching contract is claimed by this operation.

Evidence: native `TestCardNameChoiceCatalog`, `Bindings`, `Declarations`,
`WaitingSource`, `LoopIsolation`; RON `TestRONCardNameChoiceGameplay`,
`Declarations`, `PendingSource`, `PaymentAndCopy`, `Inventory`,
`RealDeclarations`. The last test executes the name-choice AST from the complete
Nebuchadnezzar and Petra Sphinx records as subrule evidence. Both complete cards
remain rejected because other adapters are missing.

### Typed name-result reads

`FromCardName(*CardNameBinding) CardNameRef` declares a pure read of a saved
English name. `CardNameRef.Resolve(*EffectContext) (string, bool)` reads the
current resolution frame, without a card lookup, decision or mutation. Missing
results remain absent. The operand declares its binding read to definition
validation; a nil binding, an unnamed binding or a read before its producer is
invalid. The declaration plan inspector traverses that binding normally.

The existing name-result map owns values. Clone, clear, nested resolution and
loop-frame services remain the single storage and lifetime contract. A name
has no zone or incarnation identity. Source departure or phasing does not erase
a pending choice/read sequence. An absent chooser clears the result, so a read
cannot reuse a prior choice. The read does not infer a waiting object reference.

Native evidence: `TestCardNameRefContract`, `Declarations`, `Frames`,
`PendingResolution`; existing `TestCardNameChoice*` contracts remain applicable.
RON evidence: `TestRONCardNameScope*` establishes operand type, instance identity,
unconditional PlayerActions export, independent subsequent choices and branch
boundaries. The real Nebuchadnezzar and Petra Sphinx operands are covered only
as subrules; both full records remain rejected. CR 201.3/201.4g name equivalence is
established below; reveal-result consumers remain separate prerequisites.

### Typed chosen-name matching and hand discard (CR 201.2a, 201.3, 201.4g)

`OracleNamesInterchangeable(first, second string) bool` is a pure English-name
comparison. Equal nonempty names match. Distinct names match only in the same
retained interchangeable-name group. Empty names never match. Artwork flavor
titles are not aliases (CR 201.6). The snapshot covers the 30 Universes Within
printings, with 31 distinct face pairs; Themberchaud has the same English name
on both printings and needs no pair. Double-faced pairs are matched by face
index, not across faces. The retained source metadata records each Oracle
identity, print-query URI, response hash, English names, retrieval time and
asset hash. Scryfall canonicalizes these printings and puts original names in
English `printed_name`, including face-local fields. The name catalog now
includes both members of every pair. Runtime matching has no network or registry
lookup. This snapshot must be updated when new interchangeable names appear.
Evidence: [Wizards' indicator explanation](https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/announcements/whats-new-on-the-list-for-wilds-of-eldraine),
[Scryfall SLX printings](https://api.scryfall.com/cards/search?q=set%3Aslx&unique=prints),
and the per-identity URLs in `oracle_name_equivalences_source.json`.

`MatchesChosenCardName(CardNameRef) CardNameMatcher` supplies
`Match(names []string, ctx *EffectContext) bool`. It checks whether any supplied
characteristic name matches the saved choice. The caller owns current/LKI
selection, object identity and visibility. The matcher does not resolve objects,
reveal cards, move cards, make decisions or mutate either input. Missing/cleared
choices and empty/nameless sets return false. Native declaration inspection
traverses the name operand, so a nil operand or an undominated binding rejects.
Existing per-frame choice storage supplies nested, loop and clone isolation.

`DiscardHandMatchingName(PlayerRef, CardNameMatcher) ResolvingEffect` checks the
selected player's current hand names at resolution, then uses the same
`discardMatchingHandEffect` and `discardActionsTogetherWithEvents` batch as the
legacy filtered discard. All replacements see the initial hand; all moves finish
before discard events. A redirected discard still sends a discard event;
a prevented discard sends none. An absent player or name result discards nothing.
This uses the engine's current single-name hand-card characteristic. Additional
object-name representations and reveal-result movement are separate services.

RON supports `DiscardCards(IsNamed(TheChosenName))` in `PlayerAction` and
`PlayerActions` resolving bodies. The name requires a dominating lexical choice.
`IsNamed` has exactly one positional operand; incompatible operands, unbound
results and other shapes reject. The private `compileResolvingCardNameFilter`
factory is also ready for reveal consumers. Cost/static/entry use and nested
boolean name filters remain unsupported. `actionOptions` supplies the ordered
RON action list through `mage.Sequence`, so native definition validation sees
producer-before-read order across the list; targets remain on the outer action.

Native evidence: `TestCardNameMatchEquivalence`, `Contract`, `Declarations`,
`PendingAndFrames`, `DiscardBatch`, `Snapshot`. RON evidence:
`TestRONCardNameMatchDeclarations`, `InvalidConsumers`, `RealOperands`,
`Gameplay`, `ScopedGameplay`. Actual Nebuchadnezzar/Petra Sphinx choice/filter
ASTs execute through native choice and matcher services; their complete records
still reject. Synthetic RON activation/spell gameplay covers explicit players,
failed payment, source departure/return/phasing, nested choice export and cloning.
No full-card gameplay mapping or collection compilation gain is claimed.

## Random hand reveal with an exact card result

`RevealRandomHandCardInto(player PlayerRef, result *CardBinding) ResolvingEffect`
selects one current hand card uniformly through the game's random service,
records a public reveal snapshot, and saves its exact hand visit. It makes no
player choice and moves no card. An absent player or empty hand clears the
binding without using randomness. A present selected card without an engine
hand-visit identity returns an explicit error before publication. The binding belongs to the existing resolution
frame. `FromCard(result)` can act only on the original still-present visit;
departure and return invalidate it. Revealed facts remain in copied public
history, which supplies no action permission or current visibility for a later
visit. New reveals can reveal the same present card again.

`DiscardCardFromHandFor(player PlayerRef, card CardRef) ResolvingEffect` first
requires current membership in the explicit player's hand. It passes the exact
card to `Game.PlayerDiscardByEffect`, preserving prevention, destination
redirection and discard events. Prevented discards send no discard event;
redirected discards still send that event. It makes no second choice or random
selection. The action cannot follow an absent or returned saved card.

Definitions validate non-nil players/results/references, binding names and
producer-before-read order. Each factory build keeps its own declarations.
Clones, nested effects and permanent-loop iterations keep separate singular
card maps. Permanent-loop execution now restores the outer singular-card map
also on error; this closes an isolation gap exposed by the reveal tests.

Both native operations declare explicit source reads in typed player operands
to waiting delayed queries. Those queries do not resolve the player, reveal,
select a card, discard or consume randomness. The same existing source and LKI
services support pending resolution after source departure or phasing; no LKI
makes an absent hand card available for an action.

Evidence: `TestRandomHandRevealIdentity`, `Declarations`, `Frames`,
`Replacements`, `AbsentAndWaiting`, `MissingIdentity`; `TestRONRandomHandRevealGameplay`, `Invalid`,
`RealOperands`, `References`, `DistinctProducers`. Rules: local CR 400.2, 400.7,
608.2c and 701.20a–c. Singular hand production and exact discard are established;
reveal-result property snapshots/predicates, plural reveals, library visits and
ownership exchange need separate contracts. No new simultaneous-operation or
replacement-order service is introduced.

## Reveal-result history predicates

`RevealRandomHandCardInto` now saves an immutable name/card-type snapshot with
its exact card visit in the existing resolution binding. Snapshot storage is
private and is never mutated. Cloned, nested, loop and delayed frames reuse their
existing independent card maps; sharing immutable facts cannot transfer choices
or let one frame clear another's result. Empty or absent production clears both
identity and facts. Existing payment/draw/card captures without reveal facts
cannot satisfy a reveal predicate.

`RevealedCardHasType`, `RevealedCardLacksType` and `RevealedCardNamed` build typed
pure matchers. Names use `CardNameMatcher`, including interchangeable Oracle
names and missing-choice behavior. `IfRevealedCardMatches(result, matcher,
matched, unmatched)` checks the saved reveal once and executes one branch.
No result always selects the unmatched branch, even for a negative type.
A nil branch makes no change; at least one branch is required. Definition
validation checks binding dominance, matcher/type validity, name-result dominance
and each declared body. Branch writes do not become unconditional producers.

These predicates inspect the historical reveal operation (local CR 608.2i),
not current characteristics or generic object LKI. Departure, return, or a later
characteristic change cannot rewrite the saved event facts. This does not
establish current mana-value reads or general characteristic queries (608.2h).
The exact `FromCard` visit remains required for an action on the card (400.7).
Public revelation itself moves nothing (701.20a–c). No zone, payment, replacement
ordering or simultaneous batch service is changed.

Both bodies declare explicit source reads to waiting delayed queries. Queries
never evaluate the matcher, choose a body, read hidden cards, consume randomness
or execute either body. Captured reveal results survive delay creation and are
retained by game clones; they do not expose another hand visit.

Native evidence: `TestRevealResultSnapshots`, `Declarations`,
`WaitingAndFrames`; neighboring `TestRandomHandReveal*` retains exact identity,
clearing, replacements and frame contracts. RON evidence: `TestRONRevealResult*`
covers invalid shapes/scope, stack timing, failed activation payments, explicit
players, source departure/return/phasing, independent clones and producers,
spell/trigger/delayed contexts, interchangeable names and real Wand land-payment
outcomes. Complete inventory-card coverage is unchanged. Library/drawn/plural
producers, generic boolean reveal filters and dynamic life payment remain gaps.

## Saved drawn-card reveal and result dispatch

`RevealHandCardInto(card CardRef, result *CardBinding) ResolvingEffect` reveals
only a currently valid hand card. It records public history and saves an exact
hand visit with immutable name/type facts in a separate result. It moves no
card and makes no choice or random selection. Missing input, an invalidated
visit, or an input outside a hand clears the result without publication.
Definitions require valid input/result declarations and producer dominance.
A historical matcher can still inspect saved facts after departure; `FromCard`
cannot act on a returned visit. Separate clone and nested-resolution maps retain
independent results. The existing reveal API remains available.

RON resolving action lists lower `DrawACard` (also
`PlayerAction(player, DrawACard)`) to existing `DrawFor(player, Fixed(1),
DrawCardInto(binding))`. `RevealTheCardDrawnThisWay` reads that lexical draw
binding and writes a separate lexical reveal binding for existing predicates.
`DiscardTheCardDrawnThisWay`, optionally in `PlayerAction`, uses the draw
binding with `DiscardCardFromHandFor`. Branches and delays retain their input
bindings; a conditional producer cannot escape its body. Separate producers
shadow only their continuations. PlayerActions does not export draw results.
Plural draws, costs, static declarations, entry/replacement bodies and library
reveal producers remain separate contexts. Explicit-player reveal wrappers
remain rejected; the supported reveal operand is the singular drawn result.

The native draw service retains CR 121.6c: a replaced draw supplies no original
result, including when its replacement draws a card. This adapter does not use
the turn's last-drawn slot. Shared discard prevention, destination replacement
and events remain in force. CR 121.1–6, 400.7 and 701.20a–c establish the draw,
visit and reveal boundaries. No replacement priority or simultaneous operation
contract changes.

Evidence: `TestSavedHandRevealIdentityAndHistory`, `Declarations`,
`ReplacementDraw`, `NestedFrames`; existing `TestDrawCardResult*`,
`TestRevealSavedHandCard*`, `TestRandomHandRevealReplacements`.
`TestRONDrawnCardRevealSindbad` executes the complete repository record with
land/nonland/empty/replaced draws, summoning sickness, source departure/return/
phasing and cloned stacks. `Contexts`, `DistinctProducers` and `Invalid` cover
spell/trigger/delayed resolution, explicit players, saved historical facts,
returned-visit rejection, lexical shadowing and independent factories/clones.
Sindbad gains complete RON gameplay evidence; Petra Sphinx remains blocked by
its library producer and movements, and Wand by dynamic life payment.

## Library-top reveal results and library visits

`RevealLibraryTopInto(player PlayerRef, result *CardBinding) ResolvingEffect`
reveals the selected player's current library top at resolution. It saves an
immutable name/type snapshot and an exact library visit in the existing card
frame, and records copied public history. It makes no choice, uses no randomness,
and moves no card. Empty libraries and absent players clear the result. A
nonempty library without engine visit identities returns an error before reveal.
Definition validation checks player/result declarations and producer dominance.

`BasePlayer` owns library visits. Additions create fresh visits; draw and
SetLibrary removal end departed visits. SetLibrary compares retained order, so
insertion or removal alone preserves retained visits. Reordered regions receive
fresh visits, including unchanged indices inside a changed region; untouched
prefixes and suffixes keep their visits. Shuffle renews every current visit,
including a one-card library. The existing continuous visibility service also
ends a retained top's visit when that card stops being the public top, or when
the final visibility rule ends (CR 401.6). Source phasing and ability removal
use that same layer-pass transition. Multiple active visibility rules preserve
the visit when one rule ends. Player extraction, SearchPlayer and game clones
retain visits with separate storage on mutation. Existing callers remain valid.
The repository mutation audit found BasePlayer mutations and SetLibrary callers.
Some retained Go callers change the returned library slice before SetLibrary.
An independent saved ID order lets SetLibrary detect those changes without
changing the public slice APIs or the card implementations.

`FromCard(result)` now resolves the original library visit, even when another
card's removal changes its index. Departure, return, shuffle and reordering end
that permission. `IfRevealedCardMatches` keeps historical reveal facts after the
visit ends. This separation follows local CR 400.7, 608.2i and 701.20a–e;
701.20d explicitly makes reordered revealed cards new objects. The operation
supplies no permission to draw, move, exile, or inspect another card.

RON supports bare `RevealTopCardOfLibrary`, explicit `PlayerAction(player,
RevealTopCardOfLibrary)`, and unconditional nested `PlayerActions` production in
resolving action lists. A scoped producer can supply its lexical result to the
outer continuation without changing the outer player. Existing `If`, `Unless`
and `IfElse(ACardWasRevealedThisWay(filter), ...)` use the current reveal's saved
facts and existing type/name matchers. Library results cannot supply a hand
reveal discard. Branch-local production cannot supply an outer result. Tuples,
arguments, unbound players, costs, static rules, entry and replacement operations
remain rejected. Spell, activation, trigger and delayed action lists share the
same adapter. Factories allocate separate result bindings; saved resolution and
delayed frames reuse existing clone/capture behavior.

The typed player's explicit source reads participate in waiting delayed-source
queries. Queries do not reveal or inspect the library. Source departure uses its
saved controller information; returned sources cannot replace the incarnation.
This introduces no replacement candidate or simultaneous movement. Payment
rollback and target legality use existing announcement services.

Evidence: native `TestLibraryTopRevealVisits`, `RemovalAndClone`,
`ReorderRegion`, `Declarations`, `WaitingAndFrames`, `MissingIdentity`,
`ContinuousVisibility`, `MutableCallerOrder`; RON
`TestRONLibraryTopRevealGameplay`, `Contexts`, `DistinctResults`, `Invalid`,
`PetraPrerequisite`. The Petra test extracts the actual scoped producer and name
predicate from its complete LEG record and executes them on the native stack.
That test retains prerequisite coverage. Complete Petra now has native RON
movement coverage in `TestRONLibraryTopMovePetra`. Knowledge Vault still needs
linked face-down exile; Aladdin's Lamp needs draw replacement and library
selection.


## Resolving library-top movement without draw or mill

`PutLibraryTopInHand(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect` and
`PutLibraryTopInGraveyard(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect` use one shared engine
implementation. A typed player resolves at action execution. The action selects
the current top, checks the destination owner, removes the card with SetLibrary,
and inserts it with AddToHand or AddToGraveyard. One EvtZoneChange follows all
movement, with the physical card ID, destination owner, ZoneLibrary and the
correct destination. There is no battlefield departure or death. An absent
player or empty library has no effect. Invalid owner state returns an error
before movement. Nil player declarations fail definition validation.

CR 400.3 routes the destination to the owner; CR 400.7 ends the library visit.
Retained suffix visits do not change. Destination services create their own
visits. Reveal history remains immutable after departure. Clones use existing
independent player zone/visit storage. The actions keep no mutable saved top.
The top is read at resolution, even for delayed effects and changed library order.

CR 121.5 separates hand movement from drawing. These actions do not use DrawCard,
the draw action pipeline, last-drawn state or empty-library draw state. Petra's
local Oracle text in data/LEG.json uses a graveyard movement instruction rather
than the mill keyword. CR 701.17 defines mill as its own keyword action.
Wizards' [Ravnica Remastered release notes](https://media.wizards.com/2023/downloads/RVR_Release_Notes_XrN0zlJaFn/EN_MTGRVR_ReleaseNotes_20231120.pdf)
state that Bruvac does not apply when a graveyard instruction lacks that keyword.
The graveyard service therefore bypasses mill modifiers; it does not change the
existing mill service. Generic library-zone replacement declarations are not
established by this slice.

Both effects declare explicit source reads in typed players to the existing
waiting delayed-source query. Queries do not resolve players, inspect tops or
move cards. Saved source control uses exact LKI; a returned source cannot
replace that incarnation. The same engine implementation covers both
constructors. RON owns spelling and context checks, and lowers only bare symbols
in resolving lists, explicit PlayerAction and nested PlayerActions bodies.
Spell, activation, trigger and delayed contexts use the existing frame services.
No action-result binding is produced or required. A reveal predicate in Petra
uses its independently saved facts before its selected movement branch executes.

Evidence: native `TestLibraryTopMoveHand` covers owner routing, completed-event
state, retained/departed visits, current tops, clone isolation, empty/absent
subjects and invalid declarations. `TestLibraryTopMoveGraveyard` proves zone
events and exclusion of doubling mill rules, draw events and death events.
`TestLibraryTopMoveWaiting` covers pure waiting queries, departure/return LKI,
independent delayed execution and clones. RON `TestRONLibraryTopMovePetra`
covers the complete LEG record, matching/nonmatching names, target player
choice, source departure/return/phasing, empty libraries and resolution timing.
`Scopes`, `Contexts` and `Invalid` cover player nesting, failed payment, cloned
stack execution, spell/trigger/delayed timing, current resolution tops and
rejected declaration shapes/contexts.

## Random hand reveal with matching discard

`RevealRandomHandAndDiscardMatchingName(PlayerRef, ResolutionValue,
CardNameMatcher) ResolvingEffect` reads the player, amount and current hand at
resolution. It selects distinct random cards before testing the saved name.
Only matching selected cards are discarded. A short hand limits selection;
nonpositive amounts and absent players make no reveal or random selection.
`RevealHandAndDiscardRandomMatching(PlayerRef, CardFilter) ResolvingEffect`
reveals the complete current hand and selects one random matching card. An empty
matching set uses no randomness, even when other hand cards are revealed.

Both operations share the random selection service with `DiscardAtRandom`.
Each selected card consumes one random value, including a sole candidate.
All public reveal snapshots precede the shared effect-caused discard replacement
batch. Replacements are prepared before movement; all moves precede discard
events. Prevention does not cause reselection. The selected cards are local to
one synchronous operation, with no saved card result or extended hand visit.
Graveyard destinations use the existing owner-order choice service after
replacement preparation. Players choose in active-player order, and all order
choices precede movement. Hidden destinations offer no graveyard-order choice.
Neither operation draws or targets hand cards. Existing player targeting,
payment transactions, source LKI and clone services retain their contracts.

Delayed step and permanent-event bodies save a separate chosen-name map at
creation. Execution uses a copy of that map and restores the outer map, including
on error. This permits a saved name to drive a later resolving action without
reading a later choice. Typed player and amount source reads remain available to
waiting queries without hand inspection, name selection, reveal or RNG use.

Rules: CR 101.3, 201.2, 404.3, 608.2c, 701.9 and 701.20. Evidence:
`TestRandomHandDiscard*` and `TestRONRandomHandDiscard*`; complete RON records
for Nebuchadnezzar and Rag Man cover their activation, target and timing rules.

## Linked exile producer identity and transport (CR 406.3, 406.6–7, 607.2a)

`NewExileLink() *ExileLink` declares one immutable ability group.
`ExilePermanentLinked(PermanentRef, *ExileLink) ResolvingEffect` uses the existing
battlefield departure, LKI, copied-card restoration and zone-event services.
The subject must be its current unphased incarnation. Tokens leave but do not
supply a linked card. `ExileLibraryTopLinked(PlayerRef, *ExileLink, bool)
ResolvingEffect` reads the current library top, removes it through the library
service and creates a new exact exile visit. A missing player or empty library
makes no change. No draw, mill, reveal, randomness or choice occurs.

Both save the declaration and original source incarnation before the zone event.
An announced source remains usable after departure, phasing or control changes;
a returned source cannot supply the earlier incarnation. Repeated instructions
with the same native link accumulate visits. Different declarations on the same
source remain separate, and legacy ExiledBy values cannot establish a link.

`CardsExiledWith(*ExileLink, PermanentRef) ExiledCardSet` selects only current visits
with the matching declaration and source identity. Departure and re-exile end
membership even when physical card IDs are unchanged. The set can supply native
transport of face-down cards without granting inspection to any player. The separate
ExiledCardSet type cannot feed a general CardSet chooser or characteristic filter. Standard
visibility and damage-source queries remain unchanged. The declaration has no
mutable resolution state. Clones copy cards, visits, link metadata and visibility
storage while retaining the immutable declaration identity.

`CountExiledCards(ExiledCardSet) ResolutionValue` counts selected exact visits
without characteristics or inspection.

Delayed producer queries declare the original source without reading a library
or moving a card. CountExiledCards of a linked set retains direct source reads as well.
Nil links and typed operands fail declaration validation. The hand and graveyard
consumer extension is specified below. Linked acquisition/copy adaptation, plural
exile, replacement exile and token zone persistence remain separate contracts.

RON lowering supports `Exile([TheTopCardOfLibrary], [])`, the same form with one
symbol `ExilesFaceDown`, and linked `Exile([Permanent(ref)], [])` in resolving
permanent bodies. Unassociated producers get separate declarations. Invalid
arity, tuple spellings for symbols, duplicate or unknown modifiers, unbound
subjects and unsupported cost/static/entry/spell-source contexts reject before
execution. Ordinary spell exile and existing cost services retain their callers.

Evidence: TestLinkedExileIdentity, PermanentAndEvents, Declarations, Waiting and
RepeatedAndTokens; TestRONLinkedExileProducers, Contexts and Invalid. The producer
mapping uses the first actual rule from complete Knowledge Vault and Safe Haven
records. These producer-only tests do not establish complete-card gameplay
support. The consumer extension below supplies Knowledge Vault coverage.


## Mandatory payment of one typed permanent

`IfRequiredSacrificePaid(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef, body ResolvingEffect)`
and `UnlessRequiredSacrificePaid(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef, body ResolvingEffect)`
use the exact-subject sacrifice service with mandatory payment. The payer must
control the present, unphased incarnation. A saved reference cannot select a
returned card. Ownership controls the destination, not permission to sacrifice.
An absent payer runs no body. Declaration validation rejects nil operands,
nil bodies and unbound subjects.

The service reads the subject once, then uses the existing exact-incarnation
filter and matching sacrifice transaction. It makes no optional payment offer.
The shared replacement pipeline can change or prevent movement after payment
starts; this does not undo success (CR 118.11–12). Regeneration and indestructible
cannot prevent sacrifice (CR 701.21a). Each invocation selects its own body;
nested payments, stack copies and game clones do not share payment results.
Waiting delayed queries retain explicit source reads in the subject, player and
body without resolving operands, testing affordability or making payment.
No new replacement order, zone storage or simultaneous-operation rule is added.

RON supports `MustCost(SacrificePermanent(ref))` followed immediately by
`If` or `Unless` with symbol `CostWasPaid` or `CostWasntPaid` and a nonempty
action list. `ref` uses the existing typed permanent scope: source, declared
target, event, choice or Aura host where available. Activated, triggered and
delayed resolving bodies use their existing identity and legality rules.
An unbound reference, invalid symbol/arity, separated continuation, empty body,
static or entry operation rejects. Two-branch `IfElse` remains unsupported.
Optional typed sacrifice and required matching sacrifice keep their contracts.

Evidence: `TestRequiredTypedSacrificeIdentity`, `Definition` and
`ReplacementOrdering` and `Rollback` cover legality, owner destination, phasing, return,
control, native declaration errors, movement prevention, competing replacements,
sacrifice LKI triggers, death exclusion and invalid-choice rollback. `TestRONRequiredTypedSacrifice*`
covers Knowledge Vault's real payment rule with an observable test continuation,
announcement/resolution timing, changed-controller copies, cloned pending
resolution, branch polarity, independent nested results, resolving contexts,
waiting-source queries and target legality. This is payment-rule evidence;
Knowledge Vault uses the linked-exile consumer contract for complete-record gameplay.


## Linked exile hand and graveyard transport

`ReturnExiledCardsToOwnersHands(ExiledCardSet) ResolvingEffect` and
`PutExiledCardsInOwnersGraveyards(ExiledCardSet) ResolvingEffect` use the existing
exact-visit exile selection. CR 406.6 and 607.2a restrict each consumer to its
producer declaration and source incarnation. CR 400.7 and 406.7 prevent returned
sources and later exile visits from inheriting that association.

Selection occurs once at resolution. Duplicate visits move once. Current owners
supply destinations. Graveyard order choices use the existing ordering service
in active-player order before movement. Each saved visit and owner is checked
again after choices. All moves finish before zone-change events (CR 608.2f).
Transport is neither a draw, discard, mill nor a death. Face-down cards can move
without an inspection permission; the public graveyard destination permits its
owner to order the arriving cards. Existing destination services create visits.
Clones keep separate exile and destination storage. Nil sets or invalid linked
references fail definition validation.

The effect declares direct source reads in its linked set to waiting delayed
queries. Queries do not select cards, make choices or move cards. Saved source
incarnations survive departure and phasing. Actions on exile cards still require
the saved visits; source LKI never permits movement of a returned exile card.

RON supports one unambiguous exile producer with source-local hand/graveyard
consumers in activated, triggered and delayed resolving bodies. Knowledge Vault's
complete record proves discard-before-return, successful sacrifice despite an
exile replacement, failed sacrifice, copied activations, independent sources,
source departure and pending clone isolation. Its sacrifice queues a departure
trigger; that trigger sees no linked cards after the resolving activation returns
them. Separate departure instead sends linked cards to owners' graveyards.
Safe Haven now has complete-record gameplay evidence through owner-controlled entry.
Multiple producer groups and other source references remain unsupported.


## Linked exile battlefield entry

`PutExiledCardsOntoBattlefieldUnderOwnersControl(ExiledCardSet) ResolvingEffect`
uses linked selection (CR 406.6, 607.2a), exact exile visits and independent
prepared definitions (CR 400.7). Selection deduplicates physical cards. Each
current owner controls the new permanent; the resolving controller is the actor.
Unknown owners, tokens and nonpermanent cards cannot enter (CR 400.4a, 111.8).

The shared battlefield preparation pipeline applies entry copies and replacements,
then tapped status, counters and entry choices (CR 614.12, 616.1). Preparation
keeps cards in exile until choices finish in active-player order (CR 101.4, 608.2f).
The enclosing announced X does not enter this operation; X and cast colors are
zero for these uncast cards (CR 107.3g). Preparation restores the caller's X.
Each owner can order their simultaneous entry choices (CR 101.4c) through the
shared sanitized card-order choice service. The existing failure-to-graveyard
entry contract remains: failed preparations
report their destination for the batch instead of moving immediately. Legacy
single-entry callers still receive their immediate graveyard behavior. Owner
graveyard ordering precedes movement.

Aura entry chooses a legal existing permanent without targeting (CR 303.4f–g).
The shared attachment service checks enchant limits, protection and creature-Aura
restrictions. A phased or returned host cannot qualify. Aura hosts entering in
the same batch are not yet on the battlefield and cannot qualify. Exile visits,
owners, hosts and entry prohibitions are checked after all choices. Ineligible
subjects retain their exact exile visits; valid entry-operation failures move to
the graveyard. Every successful permanent is registered before attachment or
zone-change events. Entry zone events report exile as their origin.

The linked set retains source identity through departure, phasing and delayed
resolution. Waiting queries retain explicit source reads without running entry.
Clones keep independent exile, battlefield and pending resolution state. New
entries acquire fresh counters and tapped/copy rules rather than old battlefield
state. Physical identity and printed departure definitions remain.

Evidence: `TestLinkedExileEntryBatch`, `VisitsAndProhibition`, `Aura`,
`ChoiceRechecks`, `ChoiceOrder`, `DoesNotCast`, `Definition`; `TestRONLinkedExileEntrySafeHaven`, `Contexts`,
`CopyReplacement`, `Invalid`. Full Safe Haven tests use its unchanged RON record
and cover successful/declined sacrifice, control loss, departure/return, phasing,
stack copies, independent sources, illegal targets, tokens and pending clones.
The complete Coffin record remains unsupported; no counter-note or explicit
attachment semantics are inferred from this entry service.

## Saved reveal mana value and typed resolution life payment

`RevealedCardManaValue(result *CardBinding) ResolutionValue` reads immutable
mana-value facts saved by `RevealRandomHandCardInto`, `RevealHandCardInto` and
`RevealLibraryTopInto`. The producers use the shared mana-cost value with X zero
for these nonstack zones. A missing result or a card capture without reveal facts
supplies zero. Definition validation requires a named result and a dominating
producer. The numeric read is historical information, not a live card reference
or action permission. Departure, return and later characteristic changes cannot
change the snapshot; `FromCard` still checks its exact visit. Clearing a result,
nested resolution and clone execution cannot clear another frame's facts.

`IfLifePaid(player PlayerRef, amount ResolutionValue, effect ResolvingEffect)
ResolvingEffect` and `UnlessLifePaid` read the amount once before the choice,
clamp nonpositive amounts to zero, then use `LifePayCost` and the existing
`unlessPaidEffect` payment transaction. Insufficient resources cause no offer
and run only the unpaid body. Acceptance triggers a fresh affordability check;
a failed transaction spends no life. Exact available life can be paid. Zero
payment requires acceptance, including at nonpositive life. An absent payer runs
no body. Each payment controls only its own continuation. Nil payer, amount or
body and undominated reveal reads fail definition validation.

The typed payer, amount and body declare explicit source reads to waiting delayed
queries. Queries do not resolve operands, evaluate amounts, select payment or
execute bodies. Saved source identity, controller LKI, phasing and delay frames
use their existing services; returned sources cannot substitute. Clones keep
independent decisions, resources and result maps. No new replacement priority,
simultaneous batch or general dynamic activation-cost contract is introduced.
Life payment is life loss through the shared service, not damage.

Rules evidence: local CR 107.1b, 118.3b/5/10/11, 202.3a/e, 400.7,
608.2c/d/h/i and 701.20a–c. The repository DRK Oracle text confirms Wand of Ith's
land payment of one life, nonland payment of mana value, exact discard and
controller-turn activation restriction; no source correction is required.

Evidence: `TestResolutionLifePayment` covers accepted, declined, short, exact,
zero and negative amounts for both branches. `FixedBeforeChoice` checks one read
and failed rechecks; `Declarations` checks invalid definitions;
`WaitingAndFrames` checks typed source declarations, LKI, phasing, delays and
clone choices; `AbsentAndIndependent` checks separate payments and nested frames.
`TestRevealedCardManaValue` checks all three producers, nonstack X, immutable facts,
returned visits, empty production and clone isolation. Existing
`TestRandomHandRevealReplacements` retains discard prevention, destination
redirection and events. RON `TestRONResolutionLifeWand` maps the complete card;
`Contexts`, `DistinctProducers` and `Invalid` map compiler scope and timing.

## Grouped permanent exile results (CR 400.7j, 406.2/5/7, 603.6, 608.2b/c)

`PermanentExileGroup{Subjects PermanentSet, Result *CardsBinding}` declares one
subject group. `ExilePermanentGroupsInto(groups ...PermanentExileGroup)
ResolvingEffect` requires at least one group, valid sets and distinct named result
bindings. Definition validation checks production before reads on every path.
The constructor copies the group list; bindings hold no game state.

All groups select before any movement. Current unphased incarnations qualify;
returned objects cannot replace saved subjects. Overlapping members move once,
but each declaring group receives that same exact exile visit. Each group's
order follows its selected set. Empty selections clear previous results. Tokens
leave and produce the shared zone event, but supply no retained exile card.

The operation uses the existing `withZoneChangeBatch`, battlefield departure,
printed-copy restoration, LKI, zone storage and exile-history services. All moves
and result writes finish before batch events. Leaving observers see the former
battlefield and completed movement. This adds no choice, payment, replacement
priority, exile replacement registration or persistent source-local exile link.
Existing singular exile and linked-exile callers retain their contracts.

`ExiledCardsFrom(binding *CardsBinding) ExiledCardSet` selects only current saved
exile visits without granting card inspection. `SingleExiledCardFrom(binding
*CardsBinding) CardRef` requires exactly one original saved visit and current
visibility. A plural result with only one remaining member is still plural.
Departure and re-exile end a reference. Source departure and control changes do
not alter saved visits. Transport uses current owners and the existing shared
hand, graveyard ordering and battlefield-entry services.

Existing resolution frames, stack/delayed captures and game cloning copy result
maps and slices. Nested execution restores the outer frame. A producer cannot
overwrite a different lexical declaration. Waiting delayed queries retain explicit
source reads in every subject set without selecting members, running filters or
moving cards. Implicit attachment references keep their existing behavior.

RON supports `Exile([Permanent(ref), ... EachPermanent(filter) ...], [])` with two
or more permanent groups in resolving action sequences, including supported
spell, activated, triggered, conditional and delayed bodies. `AttachedToPermanent`
lowers to `AttachmentsOn(SingletonPermanent(ref))`; existing intersections retain
Aura filtering. It checks the original host and attachment incarnations.

Two singular groups bind `TheFirstCardExiledThisWay` and
`TheSecondCardExiledThisWay` by declaration order, regardless of failed movement.
One singular and one collection group bind `TheSinglePermanentExiledThisWay` and
`TheOtherPermanentsExiledThisWay`. `ThisExiledCard` requires one explicit source
permanent group. Results require symbol spelling and lexical dominance. Branch
producers do not escape their branch. Every factory builds fresh bindings.

`PutExiledCardIntoOwnersGraveyard(ref)` accepts a singular grouped result.
The existing plural hand/graveyard/owner-entry adapters accept the other group;
owner entry still accepts only `[EntersUnderOwnersControl]`. Typed card-reference
lowering supplies `SingleExiledCardFrom` for future consumers, while graveyard
and ante operations reject these incompatible exile references. Unsupported
modifiers, card/library/spell groups, cost/static/entry contexts, unbound or
ambiguous results and attachment/counter return options still reject.

Evidence: native `TestGroupedExileIdentity`, `Declarations`, `Waiting`,
`OverlapAndLegality`, `SingularDoesNotPromote`, `SimultaneousEvents` and `Frames`;
RON `TestRONGroupedExileSubjects`, `Results`, `Invalid`, `CardReferences`,
`TimingAndLegality` and `Contexts`. The actual Bronze Tablet and Tawnos's Coffin
exile nodes run in test-only action probes. This evidence establishes their exile
prerequisite, not complete-card behavior. Counter notes, departure-or-untap return
subscriptions, noted-counter/attachment entry and ownership exchange remain gaps.

## Two-card ownership exchange (CR 108.3, 400.7, 407.3, 701.12a)

`ExchangeCardOwnership(first CardRef, second CardRef) ResolvingEffect` resolves
both operands before changing either owner. Missing or stale visits, tokens,
missing owners, disabled ante and settled games prevent the entire exchange.
Same-card and same-owner pairs make no change. Current owners are read at
resolution; a prior ownership change keeps a visit and changes the swap inputs.
LKI cannot authorize an action on an absent card. Source phasing and return do
not change saved nonbattlefield references. A phased permanent cannot supply a
new grouped-exile result.

Ownership changes use the existing `Game.ChangeOwner` service. No choices,
replacement callbacks or events run between its two checked updates. The service
keeps physical IDs, exact visits, zones, controllers and attachments. Ownership
change does not cause a zone event. Copy-on-write storage isolates clones, and
`AnteResult` reports both net changes. No zone movement or destination permission
is implied. Ante-library zone exchange retains its separate contract.

Existing resolution frames and delayed captures retain typed card bindings.
Waiting queries do not resolve these operands or infer a permanent source from a
saved card. Frame restoration keeps outer binding storage separate.
`TestCardOwnershipExchange*` covers hand/graveyard and exile/ante pairs, original
and current owners, same-owner/card pairs, absent and returned visits, hidden
exile, tokens, disabled/settled games, invalid owners, no zone events, retained
visits, settlement, declaration validation, delayed frames and clone isolation.
RON tests cover independent factory bindings, announcement timing, failed payment,
source phasing/return, illegal targets, supported action contexts and rejection.

Source defect: ATQ Bronze Tablet's RON unpaid branch swaps the two card owners.
Local `data/ATQ.json` instead assigns the Tablet to the targeted permanent's owner
and the other card to the ability controller. A Tablet owned by someone other
than its controller distinguishes these instructions. This slice leaves that
source correction and its owner/controller evidence to the independent assignment
adapter; it does not claim Oracle fidelity for the complete card. No RON assets
or vocabulary source hashes changed.

## RON nontoken permanent selection

`IsNonToken` is a symbol in permanent-filter roles and uses the existing
`Not(IsToken)` predicate. CR 111.1 and 111.6 distinguish tokens from physical
cards; copying characteristics does not transfer token status (CR 707.2).
The shared adapter now supplies supported permanent targets, resolving
collections, fixed matching sacrifice payments, static selections and resolving
property conditions. Static condition selection retains the same behavior.

The predicate does not select a zone or authorize an absent action. Target
services retain announcement identity and legality rechecks (CR 608.2b).
Collections omit phased permanents and read membership when the action resolves.
Static selections read membership each pass. Property conditions use current
or retained information for the original incarnation (CR 608.2h).

`TestRONNontokenFilterCardTargets` uses real RON target nodes to check token
rejection, cost preservation, target/source departure, phase cycles, control,
clones and copies. `TestRONNontokenFilterSacrifice` checks the real Lich filter
in a fixed-count creature payment probe; its complete dynamic mandatory payment
remains unsupported. Collection and layer probes check late entries, phasing,
physical token exclusion and source LKI. `TestNontokenFilterPhysicalCopyStatus`
checks both directions of entry copying. `TestNontokenFilterSimultaneousExile`
checks that all selected objects leave before live event observation and that
leave-trigger detection retains the former battlefield. Existing batch,
identity, payment, LKI and copy mechanics are reused without new state.

## Controller sacrifice of a simultaneous selected collection

`ControllersSacrificeEach(subjects PermanentSet) ResolvingEffect` selects once
at resolution. The private `Game.controllersSacrificePermanents([]*Permanent)`
checks each current incarnation, excludes phased objects and removes duplicate
identities. Each subject's current controller performs the sacrifice (CR 701.21a),
independently of the resolving ability's controller. No subject-selection choice
is needed when the instruction requires all selected subjects.

All sacrifice replacement proposals use the existing `prepareSacrifice` pipeline
in active-player order, before movement. The source of a replacement may itself
be among the sacrificed subjects. Existing affected-controller replacement
ordering remains in force. Each owner orders their nontoken graveyard arrivals
with `orderCardsForGraveyard`, also in active-player order (CR 101.4, 404.3).
Replaced exile arrivals and tokens do not supply graveyard-order choices.
`performSacrifice` rechecks exact incarnations and executes prepared proposals
inside `withZoneChangeBatch`. All moves precede event dispatch. Sacrifice events
retain current controllers; destination ownership remains separate (CR 400.3).
Indestructible and regeneration cannot stop sacrifice. Tokens leave without a
retained graveyard card. Leave triggers retain source LKI and the former
battlefield; state-trigger checks cannot observe partial movement.

`refersToSourcePermanent` delegates to the existing typed set declaration walker.
Waiting delayed queries do not select subjects, apply replacements or make
choices. Frames and game clones retain existing independent storage. This action
adds no result binding or cost transaction. Stale subjects have no action permission
from LKI (CR 400.7); target legality stays with the original target declarations.

Evidence: `TestControllersSacrificeBatch`, `IdentityAndDefinition`, `Replacement`,
`DepartingReplacementSource`, `PreparationOrderAndCancellation`, `WaitingPurity`,
`TokenAndSourceTriggers`, and
`TestRONControllersSacrificeGameplay`, `Targets`, `RollbackAndWaiting`,
`Declarations`, `AtomicRoles`. RON probes retain Golgothian Sylex's exact activation
cost and action; only the unsupported original-printing predicate is replaced by
a supported test collection. City in a Bottle remains rejected and has no new
complete-card coverage claim.

## Fixed original-printing names

CR 206.3 replaces expansion-symbol tests with original-printing English-name
membership. `OriginalPrintingNameCatalog(string) (*CardNameCatalog, error)`
supplies immutable embedded ARN and ATQ lists from CR 206.3a/b. The local lists
were compared with the official rules effective September 25, 2026:
[Wizards Comprehensive Rules](https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020260925.txt).
The snapshots retain all 77 and 85 names. Mountain is not in the ARN list.
Unsupported codes fail at declaration time. No runtime catalog initialization
or registry lookup supplies membership. `PrintedInSet` and the legacy expansion
casting blocks remain unchanged for their current callers.

`CardNameCatalog.Matches([]string) bool` accepts any matching supplied name,
uses existing CR 201.3 interchangeable-name groups, and excludes absent names.
`HasNameIn(*CardNameCatalog) PermanentFilter` reads the supplied permanent's
current characteristic name and excludes face-down subjects (CR 708.2).
The filter does not exclude tokens; Sylex's separate `IsNonToken` does that.
The existing engine models one current name per permanent. The catalog matcher
can also consume a supplied multiple-name list without a new object model.

Presence, incarnations, phasing and target legality belong to existing consumer
services. Collections select at resolution and can include new incarnations.
Targets retain their original incarnations and recheck current names.
Information conditions can use exact departure snapshots without authorizing an
absent action (CR 400.7, 608.2b, 608.2h). Entry copies use copied characteristic
names; departure restores the physical definition for the next entry.

The new static-name recheck test exposed a layer reset gap: face-down subjects
kept computed P/T effects from a prior name. `Permanent.resetComputedPT()` now
clears computed bonuses, CDAs and switching for each layer pass, including
face-down subjects. Their base overrides remain fixed. Copy-on-write isolates
clones. This correction is required for the shared name-filter layer context.

Evidence: `TestOriginalPrintingNamesRules`, `CurrentCharacteristics`,
`EntryCopy`, `FaceDownLayerRecheck`; `TestRONOriginalPrintingNamesSylex`,
`SylexCast`, `SylexSimultaneous`, `BottleFilter`, `Targets`, `SharedContexts`,
`Declarations`. Sylex uses its unmodified complete RON record and a real Revised
Ornithopter reprint. Bottle uses its exact nested nontoken/name conjunction in a
synthetic resolving probe and remains rejected as a complete record. Existing
controller-sacrifice native tests retain replacement ordering, departing
replacement sources and graveyard-order evidence. No new movement, cost, LKI,
result binding or replacement pipeline was introduced.

## Source-counter X in activation mana payments

`WithActivationManaXFromSourceCounters(core.CounterType)` is an `ActionOption`
for an activated `ActionDefinition` with an X mana payment. Definition validation
requires one declaration, a valid counter kind and an X mana cost. The live,
unphased source supplies the counter count before target validation and payment
(CR 107.3a/c/k, 602.1b, 602.2b). The player cannot choose a different payment X.
`CanActivate` uses that count for affordability without changing the resolution
frame. Activation scopes the count through the existing announcement pipeline
and restores the outer X on success and failure.

All X symbols use the same count. The shared cost transaction substitutes X
before activation reductions and locks the amount before counter removal or
source sacrifice. Stack copies retain the announced payment X and pay no new
costs. Games and separate source instances retain separate counters and pending
objects. Phasing or departure prevents a new announcement.

This service defines mana announcement, not a dynamic resolving `ValueX`.
Resolving source-counter instructions use `CountersOnWithLKI(This, counter)`;
they read current counters or departure information for the exact original
incarnation. A returned source cannot replace it. CR 107.3c permits a defined
value to change while pending, so the RON adapter rejects `ValueX` reads in its
body and target declarations until that distinct dynamic-X contract is ready.

RON supports `XIs(TheTotalNumberOfCountersOfTypeAmongPermanents(counter,
SinglePermanent(ThisPermanent)))` as one activation modifier, including a member
of `And([...])`. An X mana payment is required. Other source subjects, plural
collections, arithmetic, target-derived values, duplicate definitions and wrong
roles remain errors. `activation_x_value` distinguishes the semantic inventory
from resolving counter information.

`TestActivationDefinedXPayment`, `TestActivationDefinedXDeclarations`,
`TestActivationDefinedXLockedCostAndClones` and
`TestActivationDefinedXReductionAndSacrifice` supply native contract evidence.
`TestRONActivationDefinedXDoll`, `TestRONActivationDefinedXDollTriggers` and
`TestRONActivationDefinedXDollCastAndRollback` execute the complete Voodoo Doll
RON record, including all triggers, casting, damage prevention, target legality,
LKI, source return/phasing, destruction failure, payment rollback and native
upkeep/end-step execution. Declaration and inventory tests cover atomic rejection
and announcement-value roles. Reflecting Mirror remains unsupported.

## Temporary player mana payments at instant timing

`PlayerManaPaymentThisTurn(player PlayerRef, mana core.ManaCost, body ResolvingEffect)
ResolvingEffect` installs a repeatable payment permission when its resolving
instruction executes. It saves the selected payer, original controller, exact
source incarnation, target visits, X, event context and typed lexical bindings.
An absent payer installs nothing. The permission is independent of source
presence, control, phasing and ability removal (CR 611.2a). Cleanup removes all
these permissions with the other end-of-turn effects (CR 514.2).

`Game.GetPlayerPayments(player uuid.UUID) []PlayerPaymentInfo` lists affordable
permissions without choices, payment, tapping or body execution. Each result
has a stable `ID`, `SourceID` and `Description`. `Game.TakePlayerPayment(player,
id uuid.UUID) error` requires that payer and a current permission. It checks and
commits through the existing action payment transaction, including automatic
mana production. Failure leaves resources and the body unchanged. These are
special actions under CR 116.2c, not activations on permanents: they create no
stack object and no ability-activation event. Activation cost modifiers do not
apply. No additional target is announced or selected when taking a payment.

The caller must supply a time when the player could cast an instant (CR 117.1a).
Both methods reject use while a stack object is resolving. The priority handler
supports `PriorityTakePlayerPayment` with `PriorityAction.PlayerPaymentID`.
The priority coordinator retains the acting player after a successful action
(CR 116.3, 117.3c), and starts with the active player after stack resolution
(CR 117.3b). This fixes its previous unconditional active-player restart.
Each successful payment executes the body immediately in a fresh copy of the
saved frame, then restores the ambient frame. A body result cannot escape into
its installer or alter another payment. Saved references cannot follow a
returned object; phasing and LKI follow the existing typed-reference services.
Game clones share only immutable permission snapshots and have separate lists,
resources and body execution frames. Copies of the installing spell independently
save their controllers and references. A spell with all illegal targets cannot
install its permission.

Definition validation requires a non-nil player and body, fixed nonnegative
ordinary mana, valid target declarations and producer-before-consumer binding
paths. X and hybrid payments are outside this contract. Bodies have isolated
result scopes, but can consume dominated outer bindings. Source reads participate
in the existing waiting-delayed-source query without installation or payment.

RON lowers `CreatePlayerEffectUntil(playerRef,
[MayPayManaAnyTimeTheyCouldCastAnInstant(manaList, actionList), ...], UntilEndOfTurn)`
in resolving spell, activation and trigger bodies. Each operation installs a
separate permission. Empty operation/body lists, unsupported operations, X,
invalid mana, wrong kinds/arity, other durations and unbound references reject
at compilation. Nested bodies use existing resolving actions and instance
bindings. Semantic inventory reports player references, temporary player
operations, mana metadata, actions and duration separately.

Complete Guardian Angel records in LEA, LEB, 2ED, 3ED, CED and CEI execute their
initial X shield and repeated paid shields through the existing prevention
pipeline (CR 615.4, 615.7). The local `data/LEA.json` Oracle text matches these
records; no source correction was needed. Channel and North Star retain explicit
rejections for their nested life-to-mana and one-use casting operations. This
contract supplies their player-owned permission/lifetime prerequisite, not those
operations or their timing rules.

Evidence: `TestPlayerPaymentLifetime`, `Declarations`, `FramesAndRollback`,
`PriorityAndTiming`, `RetainsPriority`, `ManaSources` and
`SourceLKIAndIndependentInstallations`;
`TestRONPlayerPaymentGuardian`, `TargetIdentity`, `CopiesAndExpiry`,
`IllegalAndRollback`, `ResolvingContexts`, `Invalid`, `Inventory` and
`MultipleOperations`. Shared
prevention and mana suites retain replacement-order and simultaneous-damage
coverage; this capability adds no new replacement order or damage-batch service.

## Exact source-card payment results (CR 400.7j, 118.11, 603.6c, 701.13, 701.21)

`SacrificeSourceCostWithCard(result *CardBinding) Cost` and
`ExileSourceCostWithCard(result *CardBinding) Cost` supply an activated ability's
source card in its first new public-zone visit. The shared transaction locks the
source incarnation before mana payment. It preflights the full payment again
before spending live resources. Departure/return and phasing invalidate either locked payment. Control changes
invalidate a locked sacrifice payment. An exile payment keeps the ability's
permission for another player to act; exile does not require control of the
source. Queries do not move cards or make choices.

Payment uses the existing sacrifice replacement and exile services inside the
shared zone batch. Capture occurs after movement and before zone events, so an
event cannot substitute a later visit. Sacrifice replaced by exile saves that
exile visit. Prevented departure cannot pay. Tokens pay but supply an empty card
result. `FromCard` retains its ordinary visit and visibility checks. LKI does
not authorize an action on a missing card. No physical-ID lookup follows future
zone moves. Costs have no mutable result state; the transaction and stack frame
own results. Copies, delayed frames and clones use existing card-binding storage.

Definition validation requires a nonempty result declaration, rejects duplicate
result producers, and permits the producer only as an activated ability cost.
The same source payment without a card consumer retains its existing callers.
No new simultaneous multi-permanent operation or replacement ordering exists.

RON accepts the symbol `ThisPermanent` as an ownership-exchange card operand in
an activation with exactly one unconditional source sacrifice/exile payment,
or after a grouped exile with one unambiguous singular source group. The latter
uses `SingleExiledCardFrom` and changes no exile mechanics. The binding belongs
to each ability factory; branches and delays read the retained lexical result.
An unpaid source, ambiguous source producers, `ThisPermanent()` and `ThisCard`
remain declaration errors. Static, entry and cost-role ownership operations
remain unsupported. This contract does not implement source transport from
anywhere, hand transfer, or independent ownership assignments.

Evidence: `TestSourceCardPayment*` covers both payments, exact visit loss/return,
tokens, copy/clone isolation, replacement destinations, stale-payment rollback,
invalid declarations and capture before event-induced return. `TestRONSourceCard*`
covers fresh instances, delayed frames, synthetic paid-source exchanges and a
Tempest Efreet requirement fragment with its actual tap/sacrifice, life payment,
random reveal and ownership exchange. Its two later unsupported transports are
omitted only in that explicitly partial test; the complete record still rejects.
Bronze Tablet's existing ownership-assignment source defect remains unresolved.

### Resolution text-word pairs

`ChooseColorWordPair(PlayerRef, *ColorWordPairBinding) ResolvingEffect` and
`ChooseBasicLandWordPair(PlayerRef, *BasicLandWordPairBinding) ResolvingEffect`
make two required decisions in order at resolution (CR 608.2c–d). The first
options are White, Blue, Black, Red, Green or Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain,
Forest (CR 105.1, 305.6). The second options omit the first answer: the local
Oracle text of Sleight of Mind and Magical Hack requires replacement “with
another.” No occurrence of the chosen word on a subject is required to choose
it. These operations select words; they do not change a subject's text.

`BindColorWordPair(string)` and `BindBasicLandWordPair(string)` declare typed
results. `FirstColorWord`/`SecondColorWord` return `ColorWordRef`, whose
`Resolve(*EffectContext) (core.Color, bool)` reads the saved result.
`FirstBasicLandWord`/`SecondBasicLandWord` return `BasicLandWordRef`, whose
`Resolve(*EffectContext) (core.BasicLandType, bool)` keeps land words separate
from colors. Missing results return zero and false. Both decisions finish
before the pair is published. An absent chooser clears a prior result without
making decisions. Invalid responses select the first remaining legal option.
Decision lists have separate storage, so player code cannot change the domain.

The resolution subsystem owns one per-binding map of immutable integer pairs.
Clear, clone, nested application, permanent/card/damage-result loops and saved
delayed bodies follow the existing frame contracts. Copies decide separately
with their own controller. Source departure or phasing does not cancel a
pending choice. Typed chooser source reads remain available to waiting delayed
queries without making decisions; exact source LKI cannot follow a return.
Definition validation rejects nil players/results, empty names, duplicate pair
producers on one path, and reads without a producer on every path. Distinct
color and land reference interfaces prevent a consumer from mixing domains.

RON supports the exact symbols `ChooseTwoColorWords` and
`ChooseTwoBasicLandTypes` in resolving action sequences and player action
bodies. Tuple, cost, entry and static declarations reject. The compiler retains
separate lexical color and land plans and lowers the exact first/second symbols
to typed references. A producer in a nested player scope stays in that scope;
this slice does not export its pair to an outer action sequence. Branches and
modes retain their own plans. Actual text-effect consumers remain unsupported.

Evidence: native `TestTextWordChoiceResults`, `Declarations`, `ReadDeclarations`,
`SavedFrames`, `WaitingSource`; RON `TestRONTextWordChoiceGameplay`,
`Declarations`, `RealOperands`, `RealGameplay`, `CopyPaymentAndSource`,
`TargetLegality`.
RealOperands executes the choice and both saved operands from both complete
records' spell/permanent branches. RealGameplay casts each selected real targeted
branch through the engine with its text consumer omitted. The full target-union
wrapper is also omitted because `Targeted_Modal` only accepts Lace color actions. This is prerequisite evidence, not complete
Magical Hack or Sleight of Mind gameplay validation. No replacement ordering,
zone transport, layer installation or simultaneous object action is introduced.

## Union target resolving bodies

`ResolveObjectTarget` uses the captured category of one
`SpellOrPermanentTargetBinding`. Its spell and permanent projections share the
same target declaration, so announcement saves one choice before payment.
Resolution requires a current spell with that stack object ID or a phased-in
permanent with that incarnation (CR 608.2b). It runs only the matching body and
makes no mode choice. A returned permanent or later cast cannot replace the
saved object. The spell projection does not use physical source-ID fallback.

After body execution starts, existing typed LKI readers can read the departed
object's information for later instructions (CR 608.2h). A target need not remain
present for those information reads. Action references still require presence.
Each branch's result producers stay local during definition validation. Each
factory builds separate declarations; copies and clones use the existing target
frames. Cross-category retargeting selects the new category's body. Both bodies
retain explicit source reads for waiting queries without running an instruction.
The body uses existing movement, replacement, batch and payment services.

Evidence: native `TestObjectTargetBodyDeclarations`, `SavedIdentity`,
`ProjectionIdentity`, `BranchBindings`; RON `TestRONObjectTargetBodyGameplay`,
`Invalid`, `RealChoices`, `LegalityAndPayment`, `RetargetCopy`,
`DepartureInformation`; and unchanged `TestRONLace*` coverage.

## Private hand inspection

`LookAtHand(viewer, player PlayerRef)` reads both players and the current hand at
resolution (CR 402.3, 701.20e, 608.2c). The entire hand is saved before observer
delivery. Only the viewer receives `HandLookObserver` notifications. Observers,
`Game.HandLooks(viewerID)` callers and game clones receive independent card and
type storage. Historical observations retain the facts seen at inspection;
subsequent hand changes do not update them. HumanPlayer shows these private cards
through the existing choice channel.

Inspection leaves hand visits, card ownership, order, zones, public reveal
history and continuous hand visibility unchanged. It sends no reveal or zone
change event and uses no randomness. Empty hands and missing players do nothing.
Nil, unbound or undeclared player references fail definition validation. A queued
activation keeps its action controller as viewer after source control changes,
phasing, departure or return. Retargeted copies have separate target declarations
and use the copy controller as viewer.

Both player operands declare source reads to waiting delayed queries without
reading a hand or sending observer notifications. Existing typed player reads
supply current or exact source LKI as specified by the reference; returned
sources cannot replace saved incarnations. Inspection itself creates no card
binding, lasting inspection permission, controlled-play permission, cost,
replacement, simultaneous movement or new LKI rule.

Evidence: `TestHandInspectionPrivacyAndVisits`,
`TestHandInspectionInvalidAndMissingPlayers`, `TestHumanHandInspection`, and RON
`TestRONHandInspectionGlasses`, `Casting`, `InvalidAndReprints`,
`InstancesAndRetarget`, `DelayedReads`, and `SpellAndTrigger`. Glasses of Urza's
six complete records are covered. Word of Command remains rejected; this service
is a prerequisite for its inspection step, not evidence for controlled play.

### Text definition ability correspondence prerequisite

`WithDefinitionAbilityGroup` retains definition-local declaration identity as a
nonnegative group and member. RON uses top-level rule position plus one, with
zero reserved for combined count CDAs. Keywords that add no Ability still retain
their group. Each factory builds independent key storage and fresh abilities.
Grouped declaration validation rejects duplicate, nil, negative and stale keys.
Existing callers can still add ungrouped abilities. Revision construction rejects
a definition with any ungrouped ability; it does not silently include that ability
in printed text. Existing definitions without groups retain their validation.

`BuildTextDefinitionRevision` uses `BuildTextChangedDefinition` and checks an
exact group/member and ability-category correspondence before returning a
changed prototype. `TextDefinitionRevision.ReplacementAbility` supplies the fresh
Ability for an original ability UUID. The changed definition does not inherit
physical identity, owner, controller, source or saved choices. The map does not
change the original ability ID. Successive transformations use the immediate
input definition. Card copies have separate key maps; token copies remap fresh
ability IDs to the same declaration keys. Legacy rule replacement clears keys.
Retained-color copy exceptions remove omitted color-definition keys and preserve
the other member numbers.

CR 612.1–3 and 613.1c require text changes on the correct semantic words and in
layer 3; CR 113.7a keeps a queued ability independent of its source. This slice
prepares correspondence only. It does not implement live timestamps, layer
installation, granted-ability exclusion, activation-history migration, source
incarnation replacement, spell-entry continuation or departure restoration.
There is no new payment, LKI, replacement-order or simultaneous-operation rule.
Those existing services remain unchanged.

Evidence: `TestRONTextAbilityCorrespondence` executes changed Black Knight
protection and repeated transformations. `QueuedActivation` executes original
and changed synthetic targeted activations, rejects the old target color and
resolves cloned queues independently. `LandAndTrigger` executes changed Lifetap
and an ability-free Tropical Island prototype, and checks that all twelve full
Magical Hack/Sleight records still reject. Native `Contracts`, `InvalidGroups`
and `MembersAndCopy` check group validity, context isolation and copy storage.
`CountDefinition` covers combined Keldon Warlord CDAs; native
`CopyOmissionsAndTokens` covers copy omissions and token ID remapping.
No complete-card or collection acceptance gain is claimed.


### Printed activated-action state under text revision

`Game.RevisePrintedActivatedAbility(source *Permanent, abilityID uuid.UUID,
changes ...TextChange) error` establishes the bounded activated-action part of
active text installation. `WithTextRevisionActivationState` opts declarations
into this service; it is invalid on a spell action. RON adds it on its ordinary
and modal ActionDefinition activation path. Separate conditional mana actions
and other ability categories remain outside the supported context.

Before movement of runtime state, the service checks the source incarnation,
face-up presence, printed group/member correspondence and active action. It
reuses `BuildTextDefinitionRevision` and the retained semantic AST builder.
Unknown, removed, granted and unmarked declarations reject. Invalid words,
missing provenance, incompatible history contracts and failed builders leave
the live runtime slice unchanged. Phased sources cannot be revised; a phase
cycle keeps an existing revision. Leave-and-return cannot inherit it.

The active ability UUID, source, current controller, activation limits and paid
activation counts remain. A history binding has a fresh lineage UUID on ordinary
construction. Only a checked runtime revision gives its new declaration the old
lineage. Tracker keys combine that UUID with the source incarnation. Pending
old bodies therefore retain history reads without sharing new targets or result
bindings. Countered activations count; copies do not add counts. Cost payments,
clone isolation and cleanup use the existing shared services. Two declarations
with identical history names cannot share counts.

CR 602.2a fixes a queued activation's text; CR 602.5b keeps restrictions through
control changes. CR 612.3 excludes granted abilities. This service handles one
printed activated action, not a complete continuous text effect. It does not
modify the physical card's printed/copiable rules, static registration, layer
order, expiry or spell entry. The activated-action layer service below now owns reapplication after
layer-driven ability restoration. There is no new replacement, LKI, simultaneous
movement or cost transaction contract.

Evidence: RON `TestRONTextActivationStateHistory` executes all rules of Dragon
Whelp, Nalathni Dragon, Farrelite Priest and Initiates of the Ebon Hand with a
runtime revision before the fourth activation. `QueuedAndRepeated` covers changed
target filters, successive transformations, pending bodies and cloned resolution.
`LimitsAndIdentity` covers failed payments, once/max limits, control changes,
cleanup, phasing and returned sources. `HistoryQueueAndClone` covers countered
activations, copies and queued history. `IndependentHistoriesAndCleanup` covers
separate declarations and cleanup of a surviving revised source. `Eligibility`
and native `Declaration`, `MissingSource`, `ContractMismatch` establish rejection.
`CopiedDefinitionAndResults` checks independent entry-copy rules, draw/reveal/
discard results and printed-origin restoration after departure. Complete Magical
Hack/Sleight of Mind loading remains unsupported. `Modal` executes independently
queued mode targets and choices across a checked runtime revision.

### Printed battlefield spell-cast trigger text revision

`GenericTriggered.WithSpellCastTextRevision() *GenericTriggered` and
`Game.RevisePrintedSpellCastTrigger(source *Permanent, abilityID uuid.UUID,
changes ...TextChange) error` establish checked runtime installation for one
printed typed battlefield spell-cast trigger. Declaration validation rejects
other event types, state triggers and non-battlefield or additional source zones.
RON opts in its existing `WhenAPlayerCastsASpell(AnyPlayer | Opponent, filter)`
path; unsupported filters and bindings still reject before factory publication.

The service checks the saved source incarnation, face-up presence, retained
builder, printed declaration group/member and active opt-in. It rebuilds and
validates correspondence before replacing the runtime slice. Unknown, removed,
granted, unmarked, absent, phased, returned and incompatible declarations reject
without live changes. Replacement keeps the active UUID, source and current
controller. Fresh event bindings, targets, choices and payment bodies belong to
that declaration. Each sibling trigger keeps its own ordered text changes.

CR 603.2 and 603.3 fix the detected ability's rules; CR 603.3a fixes its controller.
Replacement does not modify the old declaration held by pending triggers. Target
selection at placement therefore uses the earlier text even if revision occurs
between detection and placement. Stacked abilities and copies keep earlier bodies
and captured caster/spell identities. Copying with a new controller does not change
an explicitly captured payment player. The existing event capture, cost, target,
LKI, clone and stack services supply these contracts.
