after division (CR 608.2b/f/h). Returned targets cannot replace an announced visit;
phasing preserves the visit but prevents resolution actions while absent.
Spell copies retain X and can choose new targets without paying again. Game clones
keep independent payments and results. Surcharged actions do not receive the
ordinary no-cost spell-text continuation marker; that context needs a separate
checked payment contract.

Evidence: `TestActionTargetSurchargeContract`,
`TestActionTargetSurchargeRejectsActivation`,
`TestActionTargetSurchargeGroupsAndLockedCost`, existing `TestTargetSurcharge*`,
and the complete Fireball and synthetic shape cases in `TestRONTargetSurcharge*`.

## Zone-event intervening conditions and historical death cause

`PermanentMatchesFilterWithLKI` is a pure source/attachment condition for
`WithInterveningIf` (CR 603.4, 608.2h). It reuses the exact-incarnation
information service. Present objects supply current facts; phased objects supply
saved phase information; departed objects supply departure LKI. A departed
source keeps its final attachment, while a present source reads its current host.
Returned sources and hosts cannot replace saved incarnations (CR 400.7).
Information reads grant no permission to act on an absent object.

`WithDeathNotSacrificed` requires a typed permanent-death pattern, one guard,
an ordinary guarded body, and no second intervening condition. The existing battlefield-to-graveyard
zone event's sacrifice flag determines the historical fact. Detection checks
that event. Stack placement stores a separate immutable event in the guarded
body; resolution checks that same fact. Later deaths, sacrifice, source return,
control changes, trigger copies and game clones cannot change it. No global
last-action result is used. Simultaneous death detection retains the shared
former-battlefield and APNAP contracts (CR 603.6c, 603.10).

Mana payment, replacement order, phasing, trigger placement, drawing and cost
rollback use existing engine services. The RON adapter enables complete Urza's
Miter. Earthbind still requires a separate acquired-static-ability adapter.
Evidence: `TestZoneIntervening*`, `TestRONZoneInterveningMiter`,
`TestRONZoneInterveningEntry`, `TestRONZoneInterveningNativeLoadAndCast`,
`TestRONZoneInterveningInvalid` and `TestRONZoneInterveningEarthbindPrerequisite`.

Resolving Aura spells now attach through the shared spell-entry service before
entry effects and the entry event (CR 303.4, 603.6a/b). This includes spell copies.
Spell-to-permanent damage/exile replacement continuation still precedes entry
notifications. Target legality uses the existing resolved-target service.
`TestRONZoneInterveningNativeEntry` and `NativeAuraCopy` verify native casting,
entry-time host checks, copied Auras and clone isolation. `SourceEntry` checks
source keyword changes, departure, return and phasing.


## Acquired layer 6 static abilities

`AcquireStaticAbility(subject PermanentRef, rule StaticRule) ResolvingEffect`
reads one live recipient at resolution and saves its exact battlefield visit.
It accepts a `While` continuous rule with layer 6 modifications and no nested
activated or triggered grants. Declaration validation gives the acquired rule
a fresh binding scope and a battlefield source context. Unsupported rule kinds,
empty rules, missing conditions, other layers and unbound outer bindings fail
validation. Each acquisition has a separate static declaration identity.

The recipient supplies the rule's live source and controller. Its attachments
and set membership remain live. The independent acquisition effect grants the
declaration in timestamp order; the declaration's own effects use shared
dependency ordering and require that ability to remain present. An earlier
removal can be followed by acquisition; a later removal stops the static rule.
The layer scheduler retains inactive effects until an earlier grant can activate
them in the same pass. Reattachment retimestamps the acquired static effect.
Phasing suspends the rule and preserves acquisition. Departure ends that visit;
returned recipients cannot inherit it. Donor departure does not end a different
recipient's acquisition. Clones keep separate battlefield and layer state.
Acquired rules do not enter printed or copiable card definitions. Explicit This recipients are declared to
`Game.WaitingDelayedPermanentSources` without resolving them or executing the
static rule. The nested rule has its own future recipient context; its reads and
implicit attachments do not supply reads by the waiting action. Saved source
visits and cloned waiting lifetimes use the shared delayed-reference service.

RON accepts the exact resolving shape
`CreatePermanentLayerEffect(ThisPermanent, [AddAbility([PermanentLayerEffect(HostPermanent, [LosesAbility(keyword)])])])`
on an Aura, with one supported fixed keyword. The nested host is evaluated in
the acquired static context, not saved as the host at acquisition. Other subjects,
combined grants, nested rule effects and temporary acquisition remain rejected.
Earthbind uses this adapter after its existing intervening-if entry condition
and shared damage operation. Prevention does not prevent acquisition. Damage
uses source LKI after departure, but acquisition requires the original live Aura.
A copied trigger rechecks flying: an earlier resolution can make it fail.

CR 400.7, 604.2/4/7, 611.2a/c, 611.3a, 613.1f, 613.7a/b/e and 613.8a-c
supply identity, duration, live attachment, timestamp and dependency contracts.
`TestAcquiredStatic*` covers engine lifecycle, declaration isolation, recipient
context and invalid rules. `TestRONAcquiredStatic*` covers all six complete
Earthbind records, native casting and rollback, trigger/spell copies, pending
clones, prevention, entry/resolution timing, source and host returns, phasing,
control, removal, reattachment, strict loading and semantic inventory.

## Live turn damage-history rules

`CantRegenerateDealtDamageByThisTurn(source PermanentRef, filter PermanentFilter)`
and `ExileDealtDamageByThisTurn(source PermanentRef, filter PermanentFilter)`
return resolving effects. They save one exact damaging source at installation.
The filter reads current recipients. `CantRegenerateCreaturesDealtDamageByThisTurn(source PermanentRef)`
instead retains creature status at actual damage, even after type changes.
`PermanentsDealtDamageAsCreaturesByThisTurn(source DamageSourceRef, candidates PermanentSet)`
exposes that history to resolving collection consumers.

`Game.CanRegeneratePermanent(*Permanent) bool` checks present visits, existing
keyword prohibitions and live history rules. Regeneration replacement matching
uses this query before choices, without requiring a layer pass. These restrictions
change rules rather than recipient abilities (CR 611.2c). Ability removal does
not end them. Damage history records positive post-replacement damage only.

Death replacement reuses the singleton service for destruction, sacrifice and
other graveyard moves, including zero toughness. Membership is checked before
movement. Shared replacement ordering and simultaneous batches remain in use
(CR 614.8, 616.1). Indestructibility still stops destruction. Regeneration can
compete with exile when no prohibition applies.

Source departure, control changes, phasing and ability removal cannot end a
resolved rule. Original damage sources can use retained information at installation.
Recipient phasing suspends actions but preserves identity. Returned sources and
recipients have new visits (CR 400.7). Cleanup ends rules and clears both general
and creature-at-damage history. Clones copy each history map independently.
`WaitingExileSources` includes the explicit saved history source, with departure
information; it does not invent references to prospective recipients. Delayed
collection queries retain declared source reads without selecting history members.

Evidence: `TestLiveDamageHistory*` and `TestRONLiveDamageHistory*`, including the
complete corrected Runesword record. The source correction follows local
`data/DRK.json`: creature-at-damage is required for its regeneration restriction;
its death replacement requires a current creature. There is one RON printing.

### Bounded one-shot delayed steps

`AtNextThisTurn(pattern DelayedStepPattern, body ResolvingEffect,
options ...DelayedStepOption) ResolvingEffect` uses the same typed declaration,
frame capture, source/controller, target and binding services as `AtNext`.
It sets a separate cleanup lifetime on the resulting `DelayedTrigger`.
`Persistent` continues to control repeated detection. The bounded schedule is
one-shot: detection removes it before placement, and cleanup removes an unused
schedule without discarding a pending trigger. Cloning copies the lifetime.
Existing persistent turn subscriptions and ordinary next-step schedules retain
their behavior. No cost, replacement ordering or simultaneous zone service changes.

CR 603.7a and 511.2 require installation before the matching event. CR 603.7c-e
and 400.7 retain saved visits and the resolving controller. CR 514.2 ends unused
this-turn schedules at cleanup. The explicit next-event contract consumes one
match even if additional combats occur. Glyph of Doom selects live blocked
creatures at delayed resolution through `BlockedByThisTurn` and `DestroyEach`;
its declaration target is not selected again.

Evidence: `TestBoundedDelayedStepLifetime` covers creation timing, extra combat,
skipped combat, cleanup, pending triggers, countering, controller and clones.
`TestBoundedDelayedStepDeclarations` covers nil operands, missing producers and
ordinary schedule compatibility. `TestRONBoundedDelayedStepGlyphOfDoom` covers
the complete card, payment rollback, target legality, saved Wall and attacker
visits, phasing, control, regeneration, copies and clones. `NativeAndBindings`
uses a strict full-record registry and independent targets; `LiveHistory` covers
resolution-time membership and indestructibility; `Invalid` rejects malformed
events, bodies and references. All RON names have prefix
`TestRONBoundedDelayedStep`. Runtime collection cutover remains gated.

### Indefinite captured base P/T and departed damage recipients

`PermanentsThatDealtDamageToThisTurn(recipient PermanentRef, candidates PermanentSet) PermanentSet`
uses the existing typed information-reference identity for sources, attachments,
saved permanents and singular targets. It does not require the recipient to
remain present or retain LKI. A returned visit cannot replace the saved visit.
Candidates must remain present and unphased and must match the current supplied
set. Only actual positive damage contributes; prevention supplies no history.
Direct departure self-trigger checks now fill missing event incarnation from
the saved departure, as `FireEvent` already does. Source death RON declarations
use `PermanentDies().WithCard(card).WithPermanent(permanent)` with separate
per-instance bindings. Other movement and event contracts stay in shared services.

`Until(Indefinite, SetEachBasePowerToughness(subjects, power, toughness))`
captures members and values at resolution (CR 611.2c-d). Layer 7b applies the
base values before bonuses and counters in layer 7c; later base-setting effects
use timestamp order (CR 613.4b-c, 613.7b). No stated duration lasts through
cleanup (CR 611.2a). Control, type or ability changes do not change captured
membership. Phasing keeps the visit and resumes its effect; zone return cannot
inherit it (CR 400.7, 702.26). Clones retain independent registrations.

`TestCapturedBasePTDepartedBinding` covers identity after departure, cleared LKI
and return. `TestCapturedBasePTLayersAndMembership` covers layer order, counters,
later base settings, expiry, new members and clones. `TestRONCapturedBasePT*`
covers full Brine Hag gameplay, death paths, prevention, regeneration, exile,
ability removal, current creature membership, phasing, return, control, pending
clones, independent simultaneous deaths, copied triggers, spell targets, strict
loading, payment rollback and declaration errors.

Reverse turn-damage collections also declare explicit source reads to the shared
waiting-delay query. That query does not select members or resolve the effect.
`TestCapturedBasePTDelayedSource` checks the declaration and saved departure.


## Heads-or-tails damage rounds

`RepeatHeadsOrTailsDamage(source DamageSourceRef, amount ResolutionValue,
players ...PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect` captures the selected player identities
once at resolution. It excludes duplicate and absent players, preserves operand
order for deterministic random scripts, and does nothing for an empty result.
Each round obtains every coin outcome before any damage. These are raw heads
or tails (CR 705.2), with no winner, loser, or call decision. The existing
`Game.FlipCoin` random queue supplies the outcomes without win/loss branches.

A round with all heads ends the process. Otherwise the amount and exact damage
source are read once for that round, and each tails player receives that amount
in one `DealSimultaneousDamage` batch. Nonpositive amounts, an absent source,
prevention and redirection do not change the coin-based repeat decision. No
arbitrary round limit is imposed. Damage replacements, affected-player ordering,
source keywords, current source facts and departure LKI retain their shared
contracts (CR 608.2c/e/f/h). State-based loss does not interrupt spell resolution
between damage packets or rounds (CR 704.4).

The effect retains immutable player, amount and source declarations. Round
outcomes are local variables in `Apply`, not resolution-frame slots. Separate
invocations and nested callers cannot overwrite one another. Factories retain
independent target declarations; stack copies retain or retarget those groups;
clones retain independent random queues and game actions. Definition validation
rejects empty participant declarations, nil operands and unbound references.
Explicit source reads also remain visible to the existing delayed-source query.

RON accepts exactly three instructions in `RepeatableActions([producer, damage,
continuation])` in an ordinary spell action context: `EachPlayerAction` with a
nonempty `Or([SinglePlayer(reference), ...])` and bare `FlipACoin`;
`SpellDealsDamage(ThisSpell, Integer(n), EachPlayer(CoinCameUpTails))`; and
`Unless(AllCoinsCameUpHeads, [RepeatThisProcess])`. Reference scope is validated
before the factory builds. Coin consumers outside that complete shape reject.
Activated, modal, delayed and replacement bodies, dynamic amounts and additional
round operations remain unsupported. Existing spell targeting checks prevent
an all-illegal spell from consuming randomness (CR 608.2b). No card-name dispatch
or Go factory fallback is used.

Evidence: `TestCoinRound*` for batches, duplicate/absent participants, frame
isolation, definition rejection, nonpositive damage, 1,001 rounds, lethal damage,
source departure/return/control/phasing, clones and replacement ordering;
`TestRONCoinRound*` for the unchanged complete Mana Clash record, all four
outcome pairs, casting payment rollback, illegal targets, prevention, repetition,
retargeted copies, illegal copied targets, clone randomness, independent factories,
atomic loading, malformed declarations and nested inventory roles. Local
`data/DRK.json` confirms the source record. No RON source correction is needed.

## Current active player in control restrictions

`TargetControlledBy(player PlayerRef) PermanentTargetOption` now also accepts
`ActivePlayer`. `PermanentsControlledBy(controller PlayerRef, filter
PermanentFilter) PermanentSet` already executes this reference. The active
player is the player whose turn it is (CR 102.1), independent of the action,
source or copy controller. Target selection and resolution read current turn
control (CR 601.2c, 608.2b). Collections select current battlefield members at
resolution (CR 608.2h). A delayed body does not save an earlier active player.

Targets retain their original incarnation and ordinary legality. Departure and
return cannot restore an old target. Phasing makes that target unavailable;
a phase cycle keeps its identity. Collections can include new and returned
members at resolution but exclude phased objects. Source departure does not
cancel a pending action. Copies keep independent target declarations; changing
a copy controller does not change the active-player restriction. Clones read
their own turn state. Target queries do not mutate game state or consume RNG.
Shared announcement and payment transactions retain failed-payment rollback.

RON supplies the exact `ControlledByPlayer(TheActivePlayer)` spelling for
singular targets and resolving collections, including nested intersections
and resolving unions. It rejects malformed operands and unsupported reference
contexts before gameplay. No control-history or activation-window semantics
are established here. No replacement or simultaneous-operation service changes.

Evidence: `TestTargetActivePlayerContract` and `TestRONActivePlayerControl*`.
Nettling Imp now uses the typed activation windows documented below. Siren's Call has complete
record gameplay evidence in the control-history and saved-player sections below.

## Continuous control since the current turn began

`ControlledSinceCurrentTurnStart` is a `PermanentFilter`. It reads the current
controller's most recent acquisition turn against `Game.CurrentTurn()`. Entry,
control loss and regain during the current turn fail the check. A new turn,
including an extra turn for either player, can make the check true. This differs
from `Permanent.ControlledSinceTurnStart(GameReader) bool`, which compares
against the controller's most recent own turn for CR 302.6.

The filter uses shared entry/control-layer history and clone storage. Phasing
excludes selection without erasing history (CR 702.26b/d). Return has new history
(CR 400.7). Target legality reads history at announcement and resolution
(CR 608.2b); resolving collections read current members (CR 608.2h). No LKI can
restore an absent action subject. Queries make no choices and consume no RNG.
Shared destruction batches retain simultaneous movement and regeneration.

RON supports the positive and negative symbol forms in singular TargetPermanent
filters and resolving collections. Collections additionally accept exactly
`ExceptFor(NotControlledSinceBeginningOfTurn)`. General exclusion forms,
static contexts and activation timing remain separate. Malformed declarations
reject before execution. Same-turn Siren's Call uses existing casting windows, live
attack requirements and saved end-step triggers with this exclusion. Local
Oracle evidence is `data/LEA.json` and `data/catalog/2ED.json`. The full record
now saves the earlier active player before delay creation. The saved binding
keeps that player if the next end step occurs on another player's turn.
Current membership and current-turn history remain live at delayed resolution.

Evidence: `TestCurrentTurnControlHistory`, `TestRONCurrentTurnControlTargets`,
`Collections`, `Invalid`, `Native`, `ImpClauses`, and `Siren` (all six reprints).

## Saved active-player scope across delayed execution

Existing signatures establish this contract without a new engine export:
`SnapshotPlayer(subject PlayerRef, binding *PlayerBinding) ResolvingEffect`,
`FromPlayer(binding *PlayerBinding) PlayerRef`,
`AtNext(pattern DelayedStepPattern, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect`, and
`PermanentsControlledBy(controller PlayerRef, filter PermanentFilter) PermanentSet`.

A snapshot reads the active player once during resolution. Delay creation saves
that resolution frame, so later writes to the same binding in a separate
resolution cannot change an earlier delay. Source departure or return does not
change the saved player (CR 603.7d). One-shot detection uses the next actual event,
even across cleanup or a skipped end step (CR 603.7b). Each body's completion
restores the enclosing frame. Copies and game clones keep independent maps.
Explicit ActivePlayer operands read each game's live turn state (CR 608.2h).

Controlled collections use the saved player but select present current members
at resolution. They retain the shared phasing, control history, destruction,
regeneration and simultaneous zone movement contracts. Waiting queries do not
read players or infer a permanent reference from a saved player alone.
Announcement and cost failure install no snapshot or delay.

RON permits CreateFutureTrigger in resolving PlayerActions, TheActivePlayer as
a typed resolving player operand, and ControlledByPlayer(ActionPlayer) in a
resolving collection with a dominating player scope. Unbound, escaped and
malformed reads fail compilation. RON spelling stays in the compiler; no new
engine state or parallel execution system is added.

Evidence: `TestSavedActivePlayerDelayedFrames` reuses one declaration for two
separate delays, tests source return, frame restoration, clone turn divergence,
query purity and unbound declaration rejection. `TestRONSavedActivePlayer*`
covers nested scope, copies, collection control, native atomic rejection,
payment rollback and all six corrected Siren's Call records across turns.
Existing `TestRONCurrentTurnControlSiren` retains same-turn attack requirements,
attack history, current-turn control, casting windows and regeneration evidence.


## Singular temporary attack requirements (RON migration slice)

`MustAttackThisTurn(subject PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect` resolves its typed
subject once and saves its physical ID and battlefield incarnation. Missing or
phased subjects install no rule. Definition validation rejects nil or unbound
references. The existing `turnAttackRule` gains an optional captured subject;
its collection callers keep live membership and their saved-player behavior.

The shared native and explicit attack paths require the exact subject to attack
if able in each combat before cleanup (CR 508.1d). Current control selects the
attacking player. Tapped, sick, phased and restricted subjects cannot attack.
The requirement does not force an attack payment, even when mana is available.
This is a rule, not an ability grant: ability removal cannot erase it. Source
control changes, departure and phasing do not end it. A phase cycle keeps the
subject; departure and return cannot transfer it (CR 400.7, 702.26b).

The existing continuous-effect service owns source-exit survival, cleanup and
clone isolation. Copies resolve with their own target frames. Delayed bodies
retain their saved references. Explicit `This` reads declare the original source
to `WaitingDelayedPermanentSources` without resolving it or installing a rule.
Information retained after departure cannot permit an action on an absent visit.
No damage, replacement ordering or simultaneous zone operation changes.

RON supports `CreatePermanentRuleEffectUntil(ref, [MustAttack], UntilEndOfTurn)`
with existing typed singular permanent references in resolving bodies. Numbered
target groups remain separate. Empty, mixed or malformed operation lists,
other durations and escaped references remain errors. The six full Nettling Imp
records now use the activation windows documented below. The RON tests retain
those modifiers and exercise the attack rule with its target filter, tap payment
and saved delayed destruction.

Evidence: `TestSingularAttackRuleLifetime`, `DefinitionAndAbsent` and
`DelayedSource`; `TestRONSingularAttackRuleGameplay`, `ImpClauses`,
`InvalidAndNative` and `SourceAndGroups`. Existing `TestAttackRulesThisTurn`
and RON collection-attack tests retain their separate collection contracts.

## RON activation turn/combat window contract

CR 506.7a–g applies the same combat-window rules to spells and activated
abilities. RON activation windows use the existing typed engine conditions:
`WithActivationStateCondition(StateCondition)`, `IsYourTurn`, `NotCondition`,
`AllConditions`, `IsDuringSteps` and `BeforeCombatStep(PhaseStep, bool)`.
No new engine mechanic or combat-history store is required.

The compiler validates turn operands (`You` or `Opponent`), bare before/combat
symbols and nonempty nested window conjunctions. It propagates current-combat
context across all `ActivateOnlyIf` declarations in one modifier conjunction
when any contains `IsDuringCombat`. Otherwise each before condition uses the
first combat. Order and nesting do not change meaning. Existing combat history
handles native skipped steps, extra combats, first-strike damage, turn resets
and separate clones. CR 602.1b/602.2/602.5a and 506.7g govern activation timing,
acting-player context, payment rollback and tap restrictions.

Timing gates run before announcement/payment and are pure during legality
queries. Existing permissions, sorcery timing and limits remain conjunctive.
Pending bodies and stack copies keep their announced controller, source visit
and targets and do not repeat timing checks (CR 113.7a). Shared target legality,
phasing, LKI, replacement ordering, simultaneous operations and delayed bindings
are reused. No declaration or engine service is removed.

`TestActivationWindowTypedContracts` proves engine reuse with acting-player turn,
payment preservation, source departure, pending clones and extra combats.
`TestRONActivationWindow*` covers the compiler contexts, invalid declarations,
atomic native loading, all steps and both players, native empty-combat skipping,
sorcery timing, cost failure and control changes. Complete Nettling Imp records
in LEA/LEB/2ED/3ED/CED/CEI cover target exclusions, source departure/phasing,
attack requirements, delayed destruction, regeneration, target control changes,
phasing, phase cycles, returned visits, copies and game clones.

## Required graveyard choice and battlefield return

`ReturnChosenGraveyardCard(graveyard, controller PlayerRef, filter CardFilter)
ResolvingEffect` makes a required non-target choice for the resolving effect
controller. `ReturnChosenGraveyardCardToOwner(graveyard PlayerRef, filter CardFilter)
ResolvingEffect` instead uses the selected card's owner as its entry controller.
The graveyard and explicit controller references are read once before the choice.
Candidates are current matching cards in that graveyard. Empty sets do nothing.
One candidate needs no decision; multiple candidates use `ChooseCardFromGraveyard`
without a `ChooseMayAbility` offer. Nil and foreign answers use the first eligible
candidate, as with the shared required permanent-choice contract.

Each candidate's graveyard visit is saved before the decision. The selected card
must still occupy that exact visit in the same graveyard. Departure and return
cannot supply the move. Choices are local to each operation. Shared
`returnGraveyardCardToBattlefield` retains zone replacements, entry restrictions,
entry operations, ownership and fresh battlefield identity. This is one move;
it does not change simultaneous multi-card movement or payment transactions.
Source-derived player references declare waiting reads without making a choice.
Existing capture frames retain source LKI, phasing and departed visits for delayed
bodies; copies and cloned games keep their frames separate.

RON lowers
`ReturnACardFromPlayersGraveyardToBattlefield(IsCardtype(Creature), player,
[EntersUnderOwnersControl])` or one
`EntersUnderPlayersControl(controller)` entry. Player operands use existing typed
lexical references in ordinary resolving bodies and supported nested/delayed
bodies. Other filters, entry lists and unbound operands reject at compilation.
This slice supplies the shared return action for Reincarnation and Glyph of
Reincarnation; their complete records remain unsupported. It does not supply
owner-information reads, delayed death-event bindings or death-result loops.

Evidence: `TestChosenGraveyardReturnContracts`, `Definition`, `WaitingSource`;
`TestRONChosenGraveyardReturnGameplay`, `RealClauses`, `DelayedTiming`, `InvalidAndNative`,
and `Inventory`. These cover chooser versus graveyard player, required-choice
fallback, exact visits, owners and entry controllers, current resolution
membership, delayed source LKI/phasing/departure, copies, clones, declaration
errors, nested inventory and atomic collection rejection. Rules: CR 115.10,
400.7, 603.7 and 608.2c/d/h. These are clause and engine contracts, not complete
card gameplay claims.


## Delayed death facts in saved resolution frames

`WhenDiesThisTurnWithBindings(subject PermanentRef, permanent *PermanentBinding,
owner, controller *PlayerBinding, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect` extends
the existing exact-incarnation death subscription through cleanup. Definition
validation requires all operands, different player bindings, and a producer for
any external saved subject. Event bindings are available only inside the body.
The current `WhenDiesThisTurn` signature and behavior remain available.

Detection reuses `PermanentDies().WithPermanent(...).WithOwner(...)` capture
against the existing former-battlefield observer; controller capture uses the
death event player. These immutable facts belong to each pending event. Stack
placement copies the saved frame and adds its event facts before execution.
The frame restores all outer binding maps when the body finishes. Captured
permanent identities supply the shared stack-reference query (CR 609.7a).
No new zone-change, replacement or simultaneous-movement service is introduced.

CR 400.7, 603.6c, 603.7b–e, 603.10a and 608.2h establish identity, timing and
LKI. Control changes before death affect the captured controller. Source
departure, cleanup after detection and returned physical cards cannot change
pending facts. Phasing preserves a watched visit but sends no death event.
Exile replacement does not supply a death. Clone copies of waiting, pending
and stacked triggers keep independent frames. A returned permanent cannot
receive an action intended for the captured visit.

`TestDelayedDeathCaptureFacts`, `Definition` and `IdentityAndFrames` prove
these engine contracts. `TestRONDelayedDeathCapture*` proves full Reincarnation
execution, separately saved owner/controller values, resolution-time non-target
choice, target legality, copies, simultaneous watches and native atomic loading.
Required costs, damage ordering and plural death-result loops are outside this
new event-binding contract.

## Mandatory payment by tapping a saved permanent

`RequiredTapOrElse(player PlayerRef, subject PermanentRef, paid, unpaid
ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect` reads its subject once at resolution and
saves its battlefield visit for the shared payment transaction. CR 118.3,
118.10 and 118.12 require an untapped available subject and keep each payment
result local. CR 701.26a supplies the tap operation. This written instruction
has no tap symbol, so CR 602.5a does not restrict a newly entered creature.
Control is checked by the calling declaration when required, as in Energy Tap's
target filter; tapping itself can affect a permanent controlled by another player.

The operation makes no optional offer or permanent choice. It uses the shared
transaction and `Game.TapPermanent`. Its internal cost checks the saved visit,
phasing and tap state before live resources are spent. Duplicate tap costs fail
validation on the isolated game. A later return cannot pay for a saved visit
(CR 400.7), and departure LKI cannot permit payment. The two branches use the
existing resolution frame and typed bindings. Definition validation requires
a player, a valid subject and at least one branch. Delayed queries retain
explicit source reads in both branches, payer and subject without paying or
reading state. Pending copies and cloned games keep separate outcomes.

RON Aura-host activation payments reuse `TapAttachedPermanentCost`, including
its source/host locking, stale-attachment checks and rollback. Existing source
tap-symbol costs are unchanged. The two complete cards also reuse target
legality, fixed mana production, mana-value LKI, upkeep events, counter changes,
shared sacrifice and temporary collection layers. No new tap replacement or
simultaneous operation is established by this slice.

`TestRequiredTapPaymentIdentity`, `Definition`, `Rollback` and
`WaitingAndCopies` establish the engine contract. Existing
`TestTapAttachedPermanentCost*` retains attachment, source-return and rollback
coverage. `TestRONSpecificTapPayment*` supplies native real-record gameplay,
declaration rejection, local nested outcomes, copies, clone isolation and
atomic collection rejection.

## Contextual spell filters in targets and cast events

`SpellFilter` is an immutable predicate tree. `SpellCardMatches(CardFilter)`,
`SpellControlledByYou()`, and
`SpellSharesColorWithPermanents(PermanentFilter, controlled bool)` form leaves.
`AllSpellFilters(...SpellFilter)`, `AnySpellFilter(...SpellFilter)` and
`NotSpellFilter(SpellFilter)` compose them. The zero filter, empty conjunctions
and disjunctions, and invalid children fail definition validation. Constructors
retain separate operand lists. Queries do not make choices or change game state.

`(*SpellTargetBinding).WithFilter(SpellFilter) *SpellTargetBinding` adds one
contextual filter to a singular spell declaration. A duplicate addition or an
addition to a union declaration fails validation. Existing card filters,
announced-X mana-value restrictions and controlled-permanent target restrictions
still apply. The action controller supplies `You`, independent of source or
spell ownership and subsequent source control. The spell's current controller
supplies controller matching (CR 112.2). Shared target selection and resolution
legality checks apply the same predicate (CR 601.2c, 608.2b). Target bindings keep
exact stack visits; returning or recasting the card cannot replace that visit.

`SpellCast().Matching(SpellFilter)` adds one checked filter to a typed cast
pattern. Detection resolves the event's exact stack ID and verifies its source
ID before matching. The controller of the trigger source supplies `You` at
that event. Existing caster restrictions compose with the new filter. The check
runs at detection, after completed casting (CR 601.2i, 603.2), and is not an
intervening-if condition. Later color, control or battlefield changes do not
cancel a pending trigger. Copies of spells do not emit a cast event. Copies of
triggers keep captured spell and caster bindings; clones keep independent state.
Text rebuilding uses fresh filters and preserves the existing cast context.

Color sharing reads effective spell colors and current permanent colors. It
selects current battlefield members through the supplied filter. With
`controlled=true`, only the action controller's members qualify. One common
color is sufficient for multicolor objects; two colorless objects share no
color (CR 105.1–105.3). Phased members are excluded (CR 702.26b). Departure ends
membership, but a later returned matching permanent can qualify in a new query.
No departure LKI or saved membership is used for this predicate.

RON accepts `ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))`,
`SharesAColorWithAPermanent(filter)`, and `ExceptFor(spellFilter)` with nonempty
nested `And`/`Or` in `TargetSpell` and battlefield `WhenAPlayerCastsASpell`.
The permanent member filter reuses the existing attachment-member filter
contract: supported pure permanent filters and at most one conjunctive
`ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))`; control inside a member disjunction
remains rejected. Event-bound or target-bound player reads in these declaration
filters remain rejected. Cost predicates and ability-source predicates retain
their existing pure card-filter contexts. This slice does not add the
`SinglePlayer(You)` caster adapter, ability-target exclusion, or stack-source
triggers.

Evidence: `TestContextualSpellFilter*` checks native target legality, current
membership, cloning, definition errors and union rejection.
`TestRONContextualSpellFilterTargets` checks controller scope, live target
changes, returned source and target identity, queries, copies and clones.
`TestRONContextualSpellFilterInvokePrejudice`, `InvokeLifetimeAndManaValue` and
`IndependentTriggers` execute the complete unchanged Invoke Prejudice record,
including casting the source, effective colors, phasing, ability removal,
captured caster, optional payment, insufficient payment, X and departure mana
value, source and spell return, trigger copies and independent pending payments.
`Invalid`, `NativeAndInventory` and `RemainingGoblinBlocker` check declaration
rejection, fresh factory declarations, semantic roles, strict atomic loading
and Goblin Artisans' remaining exclusion rule. Existing payment, replacement
and simultaneous-operation services are reused; none is changed by this slice.


## RON controller-cast triggers and optional drawing

`WhenAPlayerCastsASpell(SinglePlayer(You), filter)` lowers to
`SpellCast().ByController().Matching(filter).WithSpell(...).WithCaster(...)`.
The selector must contain the symbol `You`. Other singular player references
remain declaration errors. Existing AnyPlayer and Opponent contexts stay valid.
The source controller at detection supplies You (CR 603.2, 603.3a). Later source
or spell control changes do not cancel a pending trigger or change its captured
caster. Spell copies cause no cast event; failed casting causes no event.

`MayDrawCard(player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect` offers one choice to the selected
player at resolution, then uses `Game.PlayerDrawCard` if accepted. An absent
player makes no choice. An empty library still permits the choice and preserves
normal draw failure. Draw replacements and events use the existing service
(CR 121.1, 603.5). Player references retain explicit delayed source reads.
RON lowers exactly `MayAction(DrawACard)` in resolving ActionList and PlayerActions bodies;
argument-bearing DrawACard forms remain invalid. Each choice stays local and
produces no payment or drawn-card result binding.

Evidence: `TestRONControllerCastEnchantress` executes the complete unchanged
Verduran Enchantress record. `Records` validates all six reprints and strict
atomic loading. `Invalid` and `ScopedOptionalDraw` cover declaration errors and
independent player scope. Native `TestControllerCastDetectionAndBindings`,
`Declarations` and `OptionalDraw` cover composition, saved event identities,
copies, clones, typed validation, accept/decline, absence and draw replacement.
Stack-source Mana Vortex uses the self-cast contract below; general optional action lists remain unsupported.

### RON controller permanent-presence state trigger

`WhenAPlayerControlsAPermanent(SinglePlayer(You), filter)` uses the existing
`Controls(filter) StateCondition` and `WhenState(condition, body, options...)`
services. No new engine execution API is needed. `CheckStateTriggers` reads
current controller, subtype layers and unphased battlefield membership.
Tokens and a matching source qualify. The source must have its active ability
on the battlefield. There is no event-member capture or intervening-if check.

Each declaration and source incarnation has one pending or active trigger
(CR 603.8). Countering or resolving it permits another check. Detection saves
controller and exact source incarnation (CR 603.3a, 113.7a). A false condition,
source ability removal or departure cannot cancel that saved body. Phasing
prevents sacrifice while preserving identity; return supplies a different visit
(CR 702.26, 400.7). Copies use their own controller's sacrifice permission.
Clones keep separate arming, pending frames and zone storage.

The body uses shared sacrifice replacements and owner destinations
(CR 701.21a). Indestructible and regeneration do not prevent sacrifice.
Cancellation permits rearming; exile replacement changes the destination.
Batched departure of matching permanents cannot cancel pending bodies.
RON rejects malformed selectors, empty nested filter groups and unbound event
reads at compilation. Strict collection loading stays atomic.

Evidence: `TestRONControllerPresenceDetection`, `Pending`, `PhaseRestoration`,
`FilterComposition`, `Targets`, `Invalid`, `Records` and `Inventory`. Complete Goblins of
the Flarg also has `CastingAndMountainwalk`, which verifies payment, printed
characteristics and defending-player Mountainwalk (CR 702.14c). Native
`TestControllerPresenceStateBatchAndReplacement` checks canceled sacrifices,
indestructible, regeneration, exile, matching-member batch departure and clones.
Captured battlefield-member events and other player selectors remain separate.

## Stack abilities that target a spell

`SpellNotTargetedByPermanentAbility(filter PermanentFilter, excludeSource bool)
SpellFilter` composes with the existing immutable spell predicates. Each query
checks current stack objects marked as abilities and their exact spell target
IDs. Spells, resolved abilities, pending triggers not yet on the stack and
missing source visits do not qualify. A target remains a reference even if it
has become illegal (CR 115.9b). The candidate spell must still be on the stack.
Copies retain their original ability source (CR 707.10b).

Permanent source characteristics come from the original battlefield visit:
current information when present, retained departure or phase information
otherwise (CR 113.7, 113.7a, 400.7, 702.26). Source control, name and card-type
changes apply when read. Return cannot supply new characteristics for the old
source. An optional source exclusion compares both physical ID and incarnation.
Announcement uses the live source; resolution uses the shared target-source
information view so departure and return keep the original exclusion identity.

The existing target selection and resolution pipeline checks the predicate
at announcement and resolution (CR 602.2, 601.2c, 608.2b). Full illegality stops
all instructions, including flips and winning draws. Failed activation preserves
payment and random state. Each declaration and resolution frame remains separate.
Shared stack copy, cloning, draw replacement and counter services are unchanged.
No new payment, replacement ordering or simultaneous-operation service is added.

RON supports this shape only in permanent activated spell targets. It reuses
validated context-free permanent filters, fixed names and conjunctive source
exclusion. Controller-dependent filters and other declaration contexts remain
errors. `TestSpellAbilityExclusionIdentity` checks current and retained source
information, phasing, missing visits, resolved objects and clone separation.
`TestRONSpellAbilityExclusionGameplay`, `CastingAndInstances` and `SourceVisit`
execute all Goblin Artisans rules, coin outcomes, legality rechecks, copies,
clones, tap payment, sickness, multiple sources and exact return identity.
`Invalid`, `Contexts` and `Records` check declaration rejection, fresh factories,
semantic inventory and atomic collection loading. Local `data/ATQ.json` Oracle
text requires another creature with the fixed name; the RON omission is corrected.

### RON global battlefield-absence state trigger

`WhenNoPermanentsAreOnTheBattlefield(filter)` uses the existing typed
`BattlefieldHasNone(PermanentFilter) StateCondition` and
`WhenState(StateCondition, ResolvingEffect, ...TriggerOption) TriggeredAbility`
contracts. The pure query includes both players, tokens and the source when
they match. Membership uses current layers and excludes phased permanents.
No player or permanent event result is produced.

CR 603.8 requires one pending or stacked instance per source incarnation and
declaration. Countering or resolution permits another detection while the state
holds. This is not an intervening-if clause: later matching permanents do not
cancel a pending trigger. Source departure, phasing and ability removal stop
new detection but do not remove pending bodies (CR 113.7a, 603.3a). Detection
saves the controller and source visit; a return cannot supply that visit
(CR 400.7). A controller change can prevent the old controller from sacrificing
the source, then permit a new trigger under the current controller.

Target announcement occurs at stack placement; legality is checked again at
resolution (CR 603.3d, 608.2b). No legal target removes that instance and permits
later detection. Phasing preserves the visit but prevents sacrifice while
phased (CR 702.26). Copies keep the saved source; their controller must have
permission to sacrifice it. Clones retain independent state and pending bodies.
The existing zone batch defers state checks until all simultaneous moves finish.
Sacrifice retains replacement choices and owner destinations; indestructible
and regeneration cannot stop it (CR 701.21).

Evidence: `TestRONBattlefieldAbsenceRealRules`, `Pending`, `Targets`,
`PhaseAndLayers`, `Invalid`, `RecordsAndInventory`, and native
`TestBattlefieldAbsenceBatchAndReplacement`. No cost, replacement-order or
zone service is added. Complete Mana Vortex and Drop of Honey gameplay remains
blocked by their other rules.

## Stack-source self-cast triggers

`SourceSpellCast() spellCastPattern` uses the stack as its source zone and
matches only the exact source spell visit identified by the cast event.
`WithSpell` and `WithCaster` keep the existing typed captures. Stack detection
now saves those captures before queuing, using the same service as battlefield
triggers. Copies on the stack cannot inherit another visit's cast event. Real
spell copies and failed casting do not emit a cast event. Pending bodies keep
the detected controller, caster and spell identity after source departure or
control changes. Re-casting a physical card cannot replace the saved stack visit.
The normal APNAP, counter, clone and resolution-payment services remain shared
(CR 113.6k, 113.7a, 400.7, 601.2i, 603.2/3a, 707.10).

RON accepts exactly
`FromStack(TriggerA(WhenAPlayerCastsASpell(SinglePlayer(You), SingleSpell(ThisSpell)), actions))`
on a permanent card definition. Every constructor has its exact tuple arity;
`You` and `ThisSpell` must be symbols. This context supplies only the existing
cast spell/caster bindings, not a battlefield source or Aura host. Bodies use
the existing validated action compiler and fresh per-factory declarations.
Other source-zone events, instant/sorcery declarations and other self-spell
reference consumers remain separate. RON owns spelling and scope validation;
the engine owns exact-visit matching, capture timing and execution.

Evidence: `TestRONStackSelfCastManaVortex` executes the complete real record for
payment, decline, absent payment, failed casting, copies, departure and controller
changes. `ManaVortexBattlefield` covers both upkeep players, phasing and global
absence. `CloneAndRecast` uses an explicit later stack visit to prove old captures
cannot follow the physical card, and clone execution leaves original choices
unchanged. `RecordsAndInventory` checks fresh declarations, semantic reference
roles and strict atomic loading; `Invalid` checks malformed and foreign contexts.
Native `TestStackSelfCastExactVisit` places a copy beside the cast visit before
an event check, then verifies the captured counter removes only the cast visit.
Optional sacrifice transactions and replacement ordering retain the existing
`TestRONOptionalSacrifice*` and native cost/zone-batch contracts.

### Minimum-power comparison and required destruction choice

`PowerEqualToLeastOf(subjects, compared PermanentSet) PermanentSet` reads the
comparison set at resolution through `LowestPower`, then keeps subjects with
that current power in subject order. Sets can differ. Empty comparison sets
supply no value and select nothing; zero and negative power are ordinary values.
Current layers, counters, control and phasing determine membership and power.
The selector has no mutable choice state. Definition checks traverse both sets,
including target and binding dependencies. Waiting queries retain explicit source
reads from either set without selecting members or reading power.

RON `PowerIs(EqualTo(TheLeastPowerAmongPermanents(collection)))` lowers this
selector only in resolving collections. `DestroyAPermanentNoRegen(collection)`
composes the existing required non-target `ChoosePermanent` and
`DestroyWithoutRegeneration` services with a fresh private binding. The scoped
player chooses during resolution (CR 115.10, 608.2d). Shroud permits the choice.
Indestructibility does not exclude a least-power creature or permit destruction
of a different creature. Regeneration cannot replace this destruction, while
other zone replacements still apply (CR 701.8). Empty choices do not stop later
instructions. Saved choices keep exact visits through control and phasing;
returned objects cannot replace them (CR 400.7, 702.26). Copies and clones keep
separate resolution choices. Failed activation payment makes no choice.

Drop of Honey's complete RON factory uses both rules. Controller upkeep queues
its choice without targets; pending bodies keep their controller after source
control changes, departure, phasing or ability removal. The independent absence
state trigger uses the existing `BattlefieldHasNone`/`WhenState` contract
(CR 603.8), including pending sacrifice after a later creature entry.

Evidence: `TestLeastPowerComparisonSelection`, `Declaration`, `WaitingSource`,
`ChoiceIdentity`; `TestRONLeastPowerChoiceDropOfHoney`, `Absence`,
`CopiesAndClones`, `PlayerScope`, `ActivationAndEmpty`, `Invalid`,
`RecordsAndInventory`. Existing destruction, sacrifice, replacement and state
trigger tests retain batch ordering and exact departure contracts.

## Typed permanent-control exchange (CR 400.7, 701.12a/b, 702.26)

`ExchangePermanentControl(first, second PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect` reads both
present exact visits at resolution. An absent or phased visit, identical subjects,
equal controllers or either subject's control-change prohibition prevents the
entire exchange. The existing `Game.ExchangeControl` service snapshots current
controllers, creates two indefinite layer 2 effects and applies them together.
Later timestamps and continuous-control history use the shared layer service.
Exchange-created effects now capture each target incarnation and explicitly
survive source exit. Other control effects retain their existing lifetimes.
Source departure does not end these unconditional effects. Phasing keeps the
subjects' visits and effects; a return starts a new visit. LKI does not supply an
absent exchange subject. An unsuccessful exchange does not stop later actions.

Definition inspection traverses both references. Waiting-source queries report
explicit source reads on either side without executing the exchange. Factory
bindings, target legality, copy retargeting, saved choices, delayed frames and
clone state retain the existing typed services. This adapter neither implements
replacement ordering nor creates new payments or parallel control mechanics.

RON accepts `ExchangeControl` with exactly two singular permanent references in
resolving contexts. The original API produces no changed-control result.
The saved-result API below adds a typed historical outcome and its consumer.
Player-keyed choices and contextual type comparisons have their own contracts.
Gauntlets of Chaos now has complete-record gameplay evidence.

Evidence: `TestReferencedControlExchangeIdentity`, `Declaration`, `WaitingSource`,
`NativeDuration`;
`TestRONControlExchangeGameplay`, `Invalid`, `GauntletsProjection`,
`ActivationAndCopies`, `ChoiceAndRoles`, `TriggerAndDelay`, `Duration`. Existing
`TestExchangeControlIsAtomicAndUsesSnapshotControllers` retains simultaneous
layer application, control history, later timestamps and clone isolation.


## Player-keyed permanent choice history

`ChoosePermanentForPlayer(PlayerRef, PermanentSet, *PermanentChoiceBinding)`
uses `SnapshotPlayer` followed by `ChoosePermanent`. The shared choice service
selects current eligible members at resolution and keeps exact incarnations.
No target is declared. Required choice fallback and empty-set behavior stay the
same. Choices follow instruction order (CR 608.2c-d); this service does not add
an all-player simultaneous choice operation.

`PermanentChosenByPlayer(PlayerRef, ...*PermanentChoiceBinding) PermanentRef`
reads the latest preceding result whose saved chooser matches the referenced
player. An empty latest choice stops the search. Two reference expressions that
resolve to the same player share that player's history. Different players keep
separate results. A missing player or result supplies no permanent.
`PermanentChosenIn` reads one exact choice independently of player history.

Existing player and permanent binding maps own all state. Factory declarations
are fresh. Resolution frame cloning, delayed capture and stack copies retain
separate values. Current controllers do not replace saved choosers. Phasing stops
actions while retaining identity; a zone return cannot inherit the visit (CR
400.7, 702.26). Information and damage-source reads use exact departure LKI.
Definition inspection checks every chooser and permanent binding for preceding
writes, including nil results and reads in another ability. Waiting queries
retain explicit player-source dependencies without making choices.

RON accepts the one-argument tuple reference in resolving permanent-reference
contexts following an unscoped `ChooseAPermanent` or direct `PlayerAction`
choice in that sequence. Branches and abilities cannot export local producers.
The existing unkeyed `TheChosenPermanent` scope is unchanged. `PlayerActions`
list choice producers and required payment choices need separate adapters.

Evidence: native `TestPlayerPermanentChoiceHistory` and
`TestPlayerPermanentChoiceIdentityAndDeclarations`; RON
`TestRONPlayerPermanentChoiceJuxtapose`, `MixedTypes`, `AliasAndCopies`, `Delay`
and `Invalid`. Existing `TestRONPermanentChoice*` verifies caller preservation.
Juxtapose record execution covers both highest-mana-value exchange rounds,
including ties, empty rounds, same-player targeting and control prohibitions.
The grouped-choice contract below corrects the record's former caster-first
tie choices. Sequential choice instructions retain their declared order.

## Grouped permanent choices in APNAP order

`ChoosePermanentsAPNAP(...PermanentChoiceRequest) ResolvingEffect` saves all
choosers before the first choice. Requests contain `Player PlayerRef`,
`Subjects PermanentSet` and `Result *PermanentChoiceBinding`. Required choices
use `ChoosePermanent` in active-player, then nonactive-player order (CR 101.4).
Requests for the same player retain declaration order (CR 101.4c). Later player prompts
show each earlier chooser, permanent name and ID, including automatic singleton
choices and empty results (CR 101.4b). Candidate collections are read at each
choice; the group itself does not move objects or exchange control.

All old permanent results are cleared before choices. An absent player or empty
set supplies no permanent. Results use the existing frame maps and exact visits.
Phasing prevents actions and retains the visit; return cannot inherit it.
Information reads retain departure LKI. Copies, clones and delayed bodies use
existing frame isolation. Waiting queries retain player and collection source
reads without making a choice. Definition validation rejects empty groups, nil
inputs, repeated result declarations and reads of another request's output
within the group. Results become declared reads after the whole group.

RON accepts `SimultaneousPermanentChoices([PlayerAction(playerRef,
ChooseAPermanent(collection)), ...])` in resolving action sequences. Each
factory creates fresh results. The group exports keyed history to its following
instructions, without changing `TheChosenPermanent`. Branch results stay local.
Costs, static declarations, arbitrary grouped actions and implicit reordering of
sequential choices remain unsupported.

The Juxtapose RON record now groups each exchange round's choices explicitly.
Local `data/LEG.json` Oracle text requires a shared exchange and controller tie
choices. CR 101.4 supplies APNAP ordering; CR 701.12a-b supplies atomic exchange.
This corrects the previously recorded caster-first source defect. No other
collection record has this name. Creature and artifact rounds remain separate,
so the artifact round reads control after the creature exchange.

Evidence: `TestAPNAPPermanentChoices`, `Declarations`, `EmptyAndAliases`;
`TestRONAPNAPPermanentChoices`, `Juxtapose`, `Invalid`, `DelayAndCopies`;
existing `TestRONPlayerPermanentChoiceJuxtapose` and `MixedTypes` retain real
RON payment, targets, empty rounds, ties, self-targeting, phasing, prohibited
exchange, fresh factories and artifact-creature behavior.


## Required permanent cardinality choices and simultaneous sacrifice

`SacrificeAllButEach(players PlayerSet, subjects PermanentSet,
keep ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect` reads the kept count once and saves all
present candidates by controller before choices. Counts below zero keep zero;
counts above available members keep all. Each selected player chooses the
permanents to **keep**, in APNAP order, with prior players' kept names and IDs
visible in the prompt. Selection uses distinct exact visits. Invalid chooser
responses receive a legal required-choice fallback. No choice moves a subject.

`LeastControlledPermanentCount(players PlayerSet, subjects PermanentSet)
ResolutionValue` supplies the minimum count, including zero-member players.
Absent and duplicate player IDs are excluded. Empty player sets supply zero.
Duplicate permanent visits, phased subjects and old incarnations cannot count.
The private `choosePermanentSubset` helper uses the existing `ChoosePermanent`
decision API for an exact bounded count; it can also supply future optional
count adapters once those adapters choose and save their own count/results.

Unkept visits still controlled by the choosing player enter the existing
`controllersSacrificePermanents` batch. Replacement choices and owner graveyard
ordering precede all moves. Indestructible and regeneration do not stop sacrifice.
Cancellation and exile replacement do not cause new choices. Shared zone events
retain departure LKI and the former battlefield. CR 101.4, 101.4b, 608.2d and
701.21a supply the choice, ordering and sacrifice contracts. No persistent choice
or last-action state is added. Copies, clones and delays use their own current
resolution context. Waiting queries inspect declarations without making choices.

RON accepts `EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer,
SacrificeAllPermanentsExceptForNum(collection, count))` in resolving action lists.
`count` is `Integer(n)` with n >= 0, or
`TheLowestNumberOfPermanentsControlledAmongPlayers(collection, AnyPlayer)`.
Collections use existing typed resolving adapters, including saved singular
targets. Target selection and resolution legality remain with their declarations.
Other player sets, cost/static contexts, hand equalization, optional selections,
and saved plural choice results remain unsupported. The least-count spelling
is supported in this count context only.

Evidence: `TestPermanentCardinalityChoicesAndBatch`, `LeastAndDeclaration`,
`BoundsIdentityAndFallback`, `ReplacementsAndWaiting`; RON
`TestRONPermanentCardinalityBalanceInstructions`, `Invalid`,
`TargetsCopiesAndDelay`, `RolesAndInventory`. All six Balance reprints supply
unchanged land and creature instructions. The full card remains rejected at
`DiscardAllButNumberCards`; instruction coverage is not full-card gameplay.

## Required hand cardinality choices and simultaneous discard

`LeastHandSize(players PlayerSet) ResolutionValue` reads the minimum current
hand size of the selected present players. Empty hands count as zero. Duplicate
and absent IDs are excluded; an empty set supplies zero. The query does not
make choices, reveal cards, run replacements or change game state.

`DiscardAllButEach(players PlayerSet, keep ResolutionValue) ResolvingEffect`
reads the kept count once, then snapshots each selected hand and its exact visits
before any choice. Negative kept counts mean zero; counts above hand size cause
no discard. Each player chooses the required number of cards to **discard**, in
APNAP order. Hidden card names are not added to later prompts (CR 101.4a).
Selections must belong to the saved hand and be distinct. Invalid, duplicate,
nil or short answers receive distinct fallback cards in saved hand order.

The private `snapshotHandGroup` and `chooseHandDiscards` helpers also serve the
existing `DiscardUpToEach` operation. That operation retains its optional count
choice and per-player actual-result binding. Both operations preserve visits
before card choice. A changed or returned hand visit cannot replace a selection.
No persistent choice binding or global action result is added.

All choices precede the existing `discardActionsTogether` service. Replacement
preparation and owner graveyard ordering precede movement; all moves precede
discard events. Cancellation or a changed destination does not repeat selection
or recalculate the minimum. Independent later instructions still run. This is an
effect, not a cost; existing payment transactions retain their contracts.
CR 101.4/101.4a, 400.7, 608.2c–f/608.2h and 701.9a–c establish these boundaries.

RON accepts `EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer, DiscardAllButNumberCards(count))` in
resolving spell, activation, trigger and delayed action lists. `count` is
`Integer(n)` with n >= 0 or
`TheLowestNumberOfCardsInHandAmongPlayers(AnyPlayer)`. The latter spelling is
local to this count context. Other RON player sets, dynamic count expressions,
singular player actions, costs and static declarations remain rejected.

Evidence: `TestHandCardinalityChoicesAndBatch`, `BoundsLeastAndDeclarations`,
`ReplacementsAndVisits`, `ReadsOnceAndWaiting`, `ChoiceVisitsAndSnapshot`;
`TestRONHandCardinalityBalance`, `Invalid`, `CopiesClonesAndDelay`,
`InventoryAndAtomicLoad`. Complete unchanged Balance records from LEA, LEB,
2ED, 3ED, CED and CEI execute land sacrifice, simultaneous hand discard and
creature sacrifice in their declared order. Existing permanent-cardinality and
optional-discard result tests retain their identity, phasing, LKI, replacement,
payment and frame evidence.

## Optional per-player tap selection and actual results

`TapAnyNumberEach(players PlayerSet, subjects PermanentSet,
result *PlayerNumbersBinding) ResolvingEffect` saves each selected player's actual
tap count. The subjects are restricted to present untapped permanents controlled
by that player. Duplicate or absent player IDs and duplicate, phased or old
permanent visits do not add subjects. The entire candidate collection is read
once, and both players' candidate groups are saved before any choice.

Each player chooses a count from zero to their candidate count, then distinct
permanents through the shared bounded subset selector. Choices use APNAP order;
later players receive the previous players' public selections, including an empty
selection (CR 101.4, 101.4b, 608.2d–f). Malformed counts are clamped. Malformed
permanent responses use distinct saved candidates. All choices precede taps.
Summoning sickness does not restrict this effect; it is not a tap-symbol cost.

Each selected subject must retain its exact battlefield visit, remain untapped
and present, and remain controlled by its chooser before tapping. Only these
actual transitions supply counts (CR 400.7, 701.26a). The shared
`tapPermanentsTogether` service sets every state before any tap event. Counts are
saved before event detection. There is no new tap replacement pipeline or cost
transaction: this operation is a resolution effect. Existing costs and tap-cost
callers retain their behavior. Every invocation clears both result members,
including absent players and zero choices. Later untapping, control changes and
departure cannot change the saved counts (CR 608.2i).

`PlayerNumber` reads these same typed result frames. Definition validation checks
nil operands and producer dominance. Factory declarations, stack copies, game
clones and delayed bodies retain separate values. Explicit typed source reads in
players and subjects supply waiting delayed references without selecting members,
asking questions, or tapping. Phasing and departure retain those references;
returned sources cannot supply their earlier visits.

Evidence: `TestPlayerTapResultsChoicesAndBatch`, `VisitsAndActualTransitions`,
`BoundsResetAndDeclarations`, and `SnapshotAndWaiting`, plus the RON tests below.


## Repeated optional permanent choices and saved exclusions

`ChooseUpToPermanentsEach(players PlayerSet, subjects PermanentSet,
limit ResolutionValue, repetitions *PlayerNumbersBinding,
result *PermanentSetBinding) ResolvingEffect` reads the limit, candidate visits
and each selected player's saved count before choices. It makes that many
separate bounded choices per player, in APNAP order. Each choice offers zero
through the smaller of the limit and present candidate count. Negative limits
and repetition counts mean zero. Distinct members are required within one
choice; repeated choices and different players can select the same visit.
Subjects do not need to be controlled by the chooser. Later players receive
earlier players' public selections. The existing subset selector supplies legal
fallbacks for malformed answers. Choices do not move or tap subjects.

`BindPermanentSet(name string) *PermanentSetBinding` declares the union result.
Each invocation clears the old result, including empty choices. The saved union
contains exact visits, with no duplicate visit. `FromPermanentSet` reads surviving,
unphased visits. `WithoutPermanents(subjects, excluded PermanentSet) PermanentSet`
reads both sets at resolution and excludes matching visits. Control changes and
phase cycles retain identity; departure and return cannot supply an old choice.
Existing simultaneous destruction, regeneration and replacements apply later.

`CreatedTokensBinding` is a compatibility alias for `PermanentSetBinding`.
Token entry and choice producers retain separate named declarations. Both use
the existing exact-visit result maps, definition dominance validation, resolution
frames, deep cloning, delayed captures and waiting/stack source queries.
No new action-result storage or token behavior is introduced.

RON supports the complete resolving shape
`EachPlayerAction(AnyPlayer, ChooseUptoNumberPermanentsForEach(Integer(n),
filter, NumberOfPermanentsTappedThisWayByPlayer(EachablePlayer)))` with n >= 0
and a preceding local tap producer. `EachablePlayer` is permitted only in that
count position. `NotChosenThisWay` is a symbol in later contextual permanent
collections. Branch results remain local, later producers use fresh declarations,
and delayed bodies retain saved choices. Other player sets, repetition forms,
costs, targets and static predicates remain unsupported.

CR 101.4/101.4b/101.4c, 400.7 and 608.2d–f establish choice order, exact identity
and resolution timing. Local `data/FEM.json` confirms that Raiding Party permits
any player's Plains and one up-to-two choice for each tapped creature.
Evidence: `TestPermanentSetChoiceRepeatedAPNAPAndOverlap`,
`VisitsResetCloneAndDelay`, `InvalidDefinitions`, `BoundsDistinctVisitsAndWaiting`;
`TestRONPermanentSetChoiceRaidingParty`, `Invalid`,
`CopiesClonesDelayAndScope`, `InventoryAndAtomicLoad`, and
`TestRONAbilityTargetRestrictionRaidingParty` with the complete factory.

## Static land play restrictions

`PreventLandPlays(filter CardFilter) StaticRule` prevents all players from
playing matching land cards while its source rule is active. A zero filter is
invalid; an explicit all-card filter supplies the unconditional form.
`Game.IsLandPlayProhibited(card Card) bool` is a pure restriction query, separate
from timing, zone permission and land-play limits. It also retains the existing
global and legacy expansion restrictions. Nonlands and nil cards return false.

The typed static effect uses the existing printed declaration and source-visit
lifecycle. Queries read active effects directly so phasing immediately stops the
rule without a new layer cycle. Departure, face-down status and ability removal
stop it; tapping and control changes do not. A phase cycle restores the same
visit. Return installs a fresh rule. Effect cloning keeps source lifetimes
independent; no per-game mutable predicate result is shared.

`PlayLand` checks a hand card or permitted library top before removing it.
Rejected plays preserve zone order, land-play history and the battlefield.
`GetPlayableLands` uses the same restriction for its existing hand enumeration.
Extra and unlimited land-play permissions cannot override a prohibition
(CR 101.2, 305.1–4). Direct battlefield entry does not use this rule (CR 305.4).
Source identity, abilities and phasing use CR 400.7, 613.11 and 702.26b–d.

Evidence: `TestLandPlayRestrictionLifecycle`, `LibraryAndOverlap`, `Invalid`,
`HandOrderAndPermissions`; `TestRONLandPlayRestrictionRealRules`, `Invalid`,
`InventoryAndAtomicLoad`. Real-card probes retain the exact land subrules from
City in a Bottle and Worms of the Earth, not their unsupported sibling rules.
These probes do not establish complete gameplay support for either card.


## Filtered static casting restrictions

`PreventSpellCasts(filter CardFilter) StaticRule` prohibits all players from
casting matching nonland cards while its source ability is active. A zero
filter fails definition validation. `Game.IsSpellCastProhibited(playerID
uuid.UUID, card Card) bool` is a pure query that also retains the existing
player-level and legacy expansion restrictions. Nil and land cards return false.
The filter supplies reusable policy; the engine does not select card names.

The shared cast precheck enforces the rule in hand casting, free and alternate
zone casting, cast copies, and hand castability queries before modes, targets,
zone removal or payment. Rejection preserves hand/graveyard order, mana, stack
and life. Casting permission or an alternate cost cannot override prohibition
(CR 101.2, 601.2e). A stack copy is not cast, and existing spells still resolve.
Direct battlefield entry and land plays use separate rules.

Active printed effects retain source-visit and ability-removal contracts.
Departure, face-down status, phasing and removal stop the rule; tapping and
controller changes do not. Phasing stops it without a new layer cycle. Return
creates a new source visit. Overlapping sources and cloned games retain separate
lifetimes (CR 400.7, 613.11, 702.26b–d). No result binding, LKI action, replacement
ordering or simultaneous operation is added by this pure legality query.

Evidence: `TestSpellCastRestrictionLifecycle`, `PathsAndRollback`,
`StackCopyAndOverlap`, `Invalid`; RON evidence is mapped in the DSL reference.

## Captured permanent-set state triggers

`WhenPermanentsPresent(subjects PermanentSet, result *PermanentSetBinding,
body ResolvingEffect) TriggeredAbility` uses `WhenState` and the existing
CR 603.8 lifecycle. Definition validation requires a battlefield source,
a nonnil subject set, a named nonnil result and a valid body. The condition
is the binding producer; another rule cannot inherit its result. The engine
selects the subjects once at detection, rejects absent or phased visits and
deduplicates exact permanent identities. No player choice occurs at detection.

The pending trigger retains an immutable set of physical IDs and battlefield
incarnations before stack placement. Its capture enters the normal resolution
frame before the body. `FromPermanentSet` returns only present, unphased saved
visits. Later entries cannot join; return cannot inherit the old visit
(CR 400.7). A phase cycle preserves it (CR 702.26). Later characteristics do
not alter detection membership. No LKI can permit an action on an absent visit.

The existing source/controller capture, APNAP placement and state suppression
remain shared. Countering or resolution permits a fresh detection. Departure,
phasing and ability removal stop new detection while pending bodies survive
(CR 113.7a). Stack copies and cloned games retain the saved set in independent
resolution frames. Delayed bodies use the existing frame capture service.

`ControllersSacrificeEach` reads current controllers for the saved visits,
then uses the shared simultaneous sacrifice batch and owner destinations
(CR 701.21). Indestructible and regeneration cannot stop sacrifice. Cancellation
and exile replacements retain their existing order and can permit later state
triggers. No new payment, damage or replacement service is introduced.

Evidence: `TestStatePermanentSetCapture`, `TestStatePermanentSetInvalid`,
`TestStatePermanentSetLifecycleAndReplacement` and `TestRONStatePermanentSet*`.

## Eligible-player optional resolution payment

`PayAnyOrElse(players PlayerSet, costs CostGroup, paid, unpaid ResolvingEffect)`
reads eligibility once, excludes absent players and duplicates, and offers the
cost in active-player order (CR 101.4, 608.2d). Each eligible player receives at
most one offer. The first complete payment stops further offers and runs `paid`.
Decline, lack of resources or transaction failure lets the next eligible player
try. If no payment succeeds, including an empty set, `unpaid` runs once. Either
body may be nil; declaration validation requires at least one body.

The private `tryResolutionCostPayment` helper also serves existing `IfPaid`,
`UnlessPaid`, `PayOrElse` and mandatory payment callers. It retains their pure
affordability checks and shared action payment transaction. Costs must be paid
in full (CR 118.3); combined-cost failure does not commit partial resources.
Fixed mana can use mana abilities during resolution (CR 118.2, 608.2g).
Zero costs still require acceptance (CR 118.5). Existing resolution cost group
validation remains in force. This adds no replacement-order or simultaneous
movement service.

Both bodies keep the resolving object's controller, source, saved visits and
targets. The payment payer does not become the effect controller. The result
is a local variable; nested pairs, copies and clones cannot overwrite it.
Declaration checks isolate branch assignments. No payer result is exported.
Delayed source enumeration declares typed reads in the player set and both
bodies without evaluating eligibility or making offers. Current controller
reads and exact departure LKI keep their existing timing and identity contracts
(CR 113.7a, 400.7, 608.2h). Simulation clones retain their existing policy of
declining optional payments.

RON supports `AnyPlayerMayCost(Opponent|AnyPlayer, PayMana([...]))` in ordinary
resolving sequences with an adjacent `If`, `Unless` or `IfElse` and symbolic
`CostWasPaid`/`CostWasntPaid`. Each required list must be nonempty. Other sets,
costs, entry and draw replacement bodies remain rejected.
The payer-scope contract below supplies a local `ActionPlayer` on paid paths.
Fixed costs and bodies are built afresh per card factory.

Evidence: native `TestEligiblePlayerPaymentOrderAndResult`,
`TestEligiblePlayerPaymentRecheckAndNested`,
`TestEligiblePlayerPaymentDelayedIdentity`, `TestEligiblePlayerPaymentInvalid`,
and RON `TestRONEligiblePlayerPayment*`. The real Scarwood payment node has
gameplay evidence. Its complete record also has coverage in
`TestRONSourcePresenceDurationScarwood`.
The existing `UntilSourceLeaves` duration survives phasing and is not an exact
adapter for Oracle's "for as long as" wording (CR 611.2b, 702.26f). The separate
source-presence contract below supplies that duration.


## Captured source-presence duration

`UntilSourcePresent(This, modifications ...ContinuousModification) ResolvingEffect`
requires a permanent source and at least one valid modification. It captures
subjects, values and player references at resolution through the shared composed
layer service (CR 611.2c–d). Control modifications are permitted with this
lifetime; existing `Until` and `UntilSourceLeaves` validation stays unchanged.

The exact source incarnation must be present and phased in when the duration
starts. Departure LKI, a returned source and a phased source cannot start it
(CR 400.7, 611.2b). A phase cycle completed before resolution permits a new
duration to start. Later source departure or phasing ends all installed layers
permanently (CR 702.26f). The phase-out hook expires all layers before phase-in
can occur and reconciles their removal. Untapping, source control changes,
ability removal and cleanup do not end this duration. `UntilSourceLeaves`
continues through phasing and remains a distinct contract.

Each subject retains its captured incarnation. Target phasing suspends
application; phase-in restores it if the source duration remains active.
A returned target cannot receive an old effect. Later collection members are
excluded. Control uses the resolving controller, layer 2 timestamp order and
the shared prohibition on changing control. Expiration reveals older effects
or base control. Cloned games keep independent expiration state. Delayed bodies
retain their original frames; source enumeration declares the source read
without installing effects or changing state.

RON accepts `GainControlOfPermanentUntil(subject,
UntilPermanentLeavesBattlefield(ThisPermanent))` in ordinary resolving
permanent bodies, including local payment branches, triggers and delays.
The subject is an existing typed singular permanent reference. Only the source
endpoint is supported. Static, entry, cost, draw replacement, spell-source and
layer-duration contexts gain no adapter. Identical endpoint spelling in other
roles does not imply identical phasing rules. Scarwood Bandits uses Oracle's
“for as long as” wording (`data/DRK.json`). Gaea's Liege's layer effect instead
uses “until … leaves” (`data/LEA.json`) and needs its separate adapter. Oubliette
uses a phasing lifecycle, and Quarum Trench Gnomes already uses a distinct
subject-bound mana replacement service.

Evidence: `TestUntilSourcePresentLifetime`, `StartAndValidation`, `ControlOrder`,
and `TestRONSourcePresenceDurationScarwood`, `Contexts`, `InvalidAndLoading`,
`CastingAndBoundary`. Scarwood's complete unchanged RON record is tested for
forestwalk, casting, activation costs and rollback, artifact target legality,
opponent payment, resolution timing, control lifetime, source/target identity,
phasing, ability removal, independent instances, stack copies and game clones.
No new cost, replacement-order or simultaneous movement contract is introduced.


## Eligible-player payer scope

`PayAnyOrElseWithPayer(players PlayerSet, costs CostGroup, payer *PlayerBinding,
paid, unpaid ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect` retains `PayAnyOrElse` eligibility,
active-player ordering, affordability and total-cost transaction behavior
(CR 101.4, 118.3, 118.5, 608.2d–g). It assigns each eligible candidate before
checking affordability or offering payment. Costs can read that candidate
through `FromPlayer(payer)` in the live and isolated payment games. A failed
payment clears the candidate before the next offer. The paid body reads the
successful payer; the unpaid body has no candidate. Both bodies retain the
original effect controller, source and targets. Zero-cost payment still needs
acceptance. The old `PayAnyOrElse` signature and behavior remain available.

The binding is local to this operation. Definition validation accepts reads
only in its costs and paid body. It rejects nil or unnamed bindings, an already
produced payer binding, unpaid reads and reads after the operation. Assignments
made inside either branch retain their existing isolation. Runtime exit removes
the local value and restores a prior value if one exists. Nested operations use
separate declarations. Delayed bodies created inside a paid branch capture the
payer in their existing saved frame; ending the local scope does not erase
