that delayed snapshot. Copies use separate resolution frames. Game clones
keep their existing optional-payment policy; clones of an already created
delayed body retain its saved payer. Waiting queries enumerate source reads
without making offers or executing paid bodies (CR 113.7a, 400.7).

RON accepts `ActionPlayer` only on the successful branch of the existing
`AnyPlayerMayCost(Opponent|AnyPlayer, PayMana([...]))` pair. This includes
`If(CostWasPaid)`, `Unless(CostWasntPaid)` and either paid `IfElse` branch.
An enclosing action player is shadowed on the paid path and unavailable on the
unpaid path. After the pair the enclosing lexical scope is unchanged. Implicit
player actions keep their prior context; an explicit player reference selects
the payer. Each factory creates a fresh binding. Payment cost alternatives,
action payments and repeated subject offers keep separate compiler contracts.
No RON card record changes, replacement rules or simultaneous actions are added.

Evidence: `TestEligiblePayerScopeOffersAndRollback`,
`TestEligiblePayerScopeCostBinding`, `TestEligiblePayerScopeNestedAndDelayed`,
`TestEligiblePayerScopeInvalid`, and `TestRONEligiblePayerScope*`.
Existing `TestEligiblePlayerPayment*`, `TestRONEligiblePlayerPayment*` and
`TestRONSourcePresenceDuration*` preserve caller and real-card coverage.

## Per-permanent eligible-player payments

`OfferCostForEachPermanent(subjects PermanentSet, players PlayerSet,
costs CostGroup, unpaid *PermanentSetBinding) ResolvingEffect` saves the exact
present, unphased visits at resolution and reads player eligibility once.
Duplicate subjects and absent players cannot supply additional offers.
Subjects are grouped by their controllers in turn order. The effect controller
chooses the relative order within each group (CR 608.2f). Each subject's offer
names that subject. Eligible players receive offers in active-player order;
the first complete payment ends that subject's offers (CR 101.4, 118.3).
Each subject needs a separate payment. A zero cost still needs acceptance.

The shared eligible-player offer loop and action payment transaction own
payment, affordability rechecks and rollback. Failure or decline continues to
the next player. The result contains unpaid exact visits, including an empty
result that clears older values. All offers finish before the next effect.
`FromPermanentSet(unpaid)` reads current present, unphased saved visits.
A control change or phase cycle keeps identity; departure and return cannot
replace a visit. Later entries do not enter the result. Existing resolution
frames keep factory instances, stack copies, game clones and delayed captures
separate. Waiting queries declare source reads without running offers.

RON supports `ForEachPermanentAnyPlayerMayCost(collection, AnyPlayer,
PayLife(Integer(n)))` for nonnegative fixed life in ordinary resolving action
sequences. `CostWasntPaidForIt` is a plural collection read from the latest
preceding producer in that lexical sequence. Nested branches keep their own
producer; a branch cannot export one. Entry and draw replacement bodies,
other player sets, other payment forms and dynamic amounts remain rejected.
No per-subject permanent or payer binding is exported by this shape.

Cleansing's complete DRK record uses this producer followed by
`DestroyEachPermanent(CostWasntPaidForIt)`. The shared destruction batch retains
simultaneous departure information, owner destinations, regeneration,
indestructibility and replacement ordering (CR 608.2f, 701.8).
The local `data/DRK.json` Oracle text confirms its source shape; no RON correction
was required. Native `TestPermanentPayment*` and RON
`TestRONPermanentPayment*` establish this contract and full Cleansing gameplay.

## Eligible-player alternative resolution payments

`PayAnyAlternativeOrElseWithPayer(PlayerSet, []ResolutionPaymentOption,
*PlayerBinding, ResolvingEffect, ResolvingEffect)` offers each eligible player
complete alternatives in turn order. The first complete payment selects the
paid body. Otherwise the unpaid body runs once. Both bodies keep the original
effect controller. The payer binding is local to offers, options and the paid
body; the shared definition validator rejects unpaid and escaped reads.

`CostPaymentOption(CostGroup)` uses the existing affordability checks and action
payment transaction. Acceptance precedes one mode choice among available
options; a single available option needs no mode choice. Invalid mode selection,
failed rechecks or transaction failure allow the next eligible player to pay.
Failed transactions do not commit partial resources. Sacrifice payments use the
existing simultaneous batch and departure information.

`ActionPaymentOption(ResolutionActionPayment)` reuses action-payment preparation
and execution. It saves amounts, source information and recipient visits before
the offer and rechecks availability afterward. An accepted damage instruction
pays even when all damage is prevented (CR 118.11–12). Damage replacements,
lifelink and events use the shared damage service. Phasing prevents action on a
recipient; a phase cycle preserves its visit, and a return cannot replace it.
The declaration stores no payment result or prepared game state. Copies, clones
and delays use their separate resolution frames and source capture.

Missing players, bindings, options, action inputs or both branches fail definition
validation. Existing PayAnyOrElse, PayAnyOrElseWithPayer and PayActionOrElse
remain available. This service does not combine action instructions with ordinary
costs in one option. Each option is either a complete transactional cost group or
one action payment.

Tests: TestEligibleAlternativePayment, OrderAndRecheck, Invalid, Declarations,
SacrificeBatch; TestRONEligibleAlternativePaymentWorms, Frames and Invalid.
Existing eligible-payer and action-payment tests retain their contracts.

## Static land-entry prohibition

`PreventLandEntry() StaticRule` prevents lands from entering while its battlefield
source ability is active. `Game.IsLandEntryProhibited(card Card) bool` is a pure
query; nil and nonland cards return false. It retains the legacy global flag.
The typed rule reads active printed declarations directly, so phasing suspends
it without a layer pass. Departure, face-down status and ability removal stop
it; tapping and control changes do not. Return installs a new source visit.
Overlapping sources and cloned games have independent lifetimes.

Entry preparation checks land type before replacements and after copy changes.
The shared replacement loop stops when a copy makes the entering object a land,
before another entry replacement can apply. Prohibition produces no entry,
entry counters or entry event. Token batches retain only permitted members.
Existing entry-copy priorities, builders and printed departure rules remain in
use. This is a prohibition, not an entry replacement (CR 101.2, 614.17).

Hand and graveyard entry prepare the object before removing its saved zone
visit. Prohibited copies keep that visit. Graveyard entry rechecks the saved
visit after entry choices. Library search retains a prohibited card and still
shuffles. Delayed exile return retains a prohibited card in exile and consumes
the delay. Linked exile batches use the same query and entry preparation.
A land play with prohibited entry fails before zone removal or turn history;
playable-land queries exclude it. Ordinary cast copies and token creation use
shared preparation. Existing land-play restrictions remain independent.

RON accepts `CardsCantEnterTheBattlefield(IsCardtype(Land))` as an ordinary
permanent rule. Other filters, malformed arguments and resolving action contexts
reject during compilation. Each factory builds independent declarations.

Evidence: `TestLandEntryRestrictionLifecycle`, `ZoneRetention`, `Batch`,
`CopyRecheck`, `Play`; `TestRONLandEntryRestrictionWorms`, `Invalid`, `AtomicLoad`,
`RealEntryPaths`. Worms of the Earth uses its complete unchanged DRK record.
Its land-play, entry and upkeep payment rules all have gameplay evidence.
Gaea's Touch and Untamed Wilds retain their complete RON entry regression tests.

## Saved instruction damage outcomes (RON execution)

`DamageOutcomesInto(*DamageResultsBinding) DamageResultOption` extends singular
`DealDamageFrom` with the same immutable outcome storage used by simultaneous
`DamageResultsInto`. It clears the output before resolving the source, recipient
and amount. An absent source, illegal recipient, nonpositive amount or fully
prevented instruction supplies no positive outcome. The final source identity,
recipient and actual amount come from the shared replacement and damage services
(CR 120.4b–d). Life loss is not the damage amount.

`IfDamageDealtToPlayer(results *DamageResultsBinding, source DamageSourceRef,
player PlayerRef, body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect` executes its body once
if a positive saved outcome has that exact source and player. `SameObject`
requires the source's exact battlefield or zone visit. Departure retains facts;
a returned object cannot stand for the former source. Player and source operands
are read when the condition resolves. The output must have a preceding producer.
Nil declarations and duplicate singular outputs fail definition validation.

`PlayerDamageRecipients(PlayerSet) DamageRecipientSet` selects distinct present
players before one shared simultaneous batch. The amount and source are read
once by `DealDamageEach`. Prevention, redirection, lifelink, damage events and
replacement choices use the existing batch. Typed player-set operands supply
explicit waiting source reads without selecting players or executing damage.

Existing resolution frames save numbers and immutable outcomes for delayed
bodies, stack copies and game clones. A branch producer stays in its branch;
no global last-damage slot is used. The new condition declares explicit source
reads in its source, player and body for waiting queries. Queries make no damage
or condition checks. Existing replacement ordering and cost transactions are
unchanged.

Contract evidence: `TestDamageOutcomeCondition`, `Definition`, `Waiting` and
`Batch`; RON `TestRONDamageOutcomeSyphonSoul`, `WarMachine`, `Scopes`, `Invalid`
and `InventoryAndAtomicLoad`.

## RON temporary singular control

`GainControlOfPermanentUntil(subject, UntilEndOfTurn)` lowers an ordinary
resolving body to `Until(core.EndOfTurn, ChangeController(subject, You))`.
`GainControlOfPermanentUntil(subject,
ForAsLongAsPermanentRemainsTapped(ThisPermanent))` requires a permanent source
and lowers to `UntilSourceUntaps(This, ChangeController(subject, You))`.
Entry and draw-replacement bodies reject both forms. Other endpoints retain
their existing support boundaries. The engine now validates layer 2 control
modifications under `UntilSourceUntaps`; no separate control system is added.

CR 611.2a–c locks the subjects, controller and duration at resolution. Shared
layer 2 timestamps apply control effects. End-of-turn control ends at cleanup
(CR 514.2). A tapped source must be present, phased in, tapped and still on its
original visit at resolution. Untapping, departure and source phasing end the
installed effect permanently (CR 702.26f). A stun replacement preserves it.
Source control changes and ability removal do not end it. Target phasing keeps
identity; target return cannot inherit it. Simultaneous source untaps restore
all affected controllers before the first untap notification. Waiting queries
retain explicit source reads without executing control or reading tap state.

Engine evidence: `TestTemporaryControlDuration`, `Start` and
`SimultaneousUntap`, plus retained `TestUntilSourceUntaps*` contracts.
RON evidence: `TestRONTemporaryControlPreacher`, `PreacherCastingAndUntap`,
`Disharmony`, `ContextsAndCopies`, `Delayed` and `Invalid`. These cover both
complete unchanged card records, opponent choice, spell/activation payments,
combat window and removal, exact visits, phasing, source control changes,
ability removal, optional untap, stun, copies, delayed frames and clones.
Plural control and other declaration contexts need separate adapters.

## Resolving permanent card-type comparison

`PermanentsSharingCardTypes(reference PermanentRef, subjects PermanentSet,
types ...core.CardType) PermanentSet` selects current subjects with at least one
card type shared with the reference. An omitted list permits every engine card
type; a supplied list restricts the intersection. The constructor copies the
list. Definition validation rejects invalid or duplicate types, missing operands,
unsupported information references and reads without a local producer/declaration.
Supertypes, subtypes and colors do not supply card types.

The existing exact-incarnation information service supplies current layered
types or departure/phase information (CR 400.7, 608.2h, 702.26b). A return cannot
replace a saved source, target or choice. The reference supplies information only;
subjects must be present, unphased, current visits. Selection keeps input order
and removes duplicate subjects. Face-down references and subjects use their
current face-down types. Empty type intersections select nothing. Control and
shroud do not restrict an untargeted collection unless its other operands do so.

Target legality remains with the enclosing ability (CR 608.2b). Illegal target
bindings cannot supply resolving comparison information. Source departure can
supply LKI. Attachment references use the existing current-or-retained exact-host
contract; they do not follow a returned host. All members are selected before the
shared action batch. No new zone, replacement, layer or payment system is added.

Waiting delayed queries retain explicit source reads from both the reference and
subject set without reading types or running filters. Existing frames keep saved
choices, targets, copied bodies, delayed bodies and cloned games separate.
Evidence: `TestPermanentTypeComparison`, `Declarations`, `SavedAndWaiting` and
`TestRONPermanentTypeComparison*`. These tests establish the resolving service.
Dependent singular announcement card-type targets now have the service below.
Other dependent targets, static declarations, entry operations and replacement
bodies require separate adapters. Resolving attachment movement now
uses this service as described in Required attachment host choice below.


## Exact attachment host references

`HostOfPermanent(attachment PermanentRef) PermanentRef` reads the host of an
exact information-capable attachment reference: source, singular target, saved
permanent or another information reference. Definition validation rejects nil,
undeclared targets and unbound saved references. The constructor stores no
game state. The host uses the existing current attachment incarnation and
`departedAttachments` records. `AttachedPermanent` shares its information
identity implementation and retains its existing action behavior.

A present attachment reads its current host. Detachment clears that read; a
host departure detaches a still-present Equipment. A departed attachment reads
its last saved host. Returning either object cannot replace the saved visit.
Information consumers can read that host's exact departure or phase LKI;
action and damage-recipient consumers require the exact present, unphased host.
Control changes do not change attachment identity (CR 303.4b/e, 400.7, 608.2h,
702.26). Target consumers use only legal target bindings (CR 608.2b).

Per-instance target bindings and shared delayed frames, stack copies,
retargeting and game cloning preserve separate reads. Waiting comparison
queries traverse the attachment operand for explicit source reads without
executing the comparison or making choices. This API creates no attachment,
replacement, payment or simultaneous-operation service.

Evidence: `TestPermanentHost`, `Declarations`, `ReferencesAndWaiting`, the
existing `TestPermanentInformation*` regressions and `TestRONTargetHost*`.

## Required attachment host choice

`AttachPermanentToChoice(player PlayerRef, attachment PermanentRef, hosts
PermanentSet) ResolvingEffect` makes a required, non-targeted choice at resolution.
It uses `ChoosePermanent` with a typed legal-host collection and then `Game.Attach`.
The current host, the attachment itself, absent visits, phased visits and illegal
hosts cannot be chosen. Invalid or nil answers use the shared required-choice
fallback. One legal host needs no decision call; zero legal hosts cause no move.

The attachment visit is saved before the choice. The selected host keeps its
exact visit in a private per-instance binding in the resolution frame. After the
choice, both objects must be present, unphased and have the saved incarnations.
Host collection membership and attachment legality are checked again. Returned
objects cannot replace either visit. The Aura's current controller supplies its
enchant restriction, while the explicit player supplies the choice. Shroud and
hexproof do not restrict the host choice; protection and enchant limits do
(CR 303.4e/j, 701.3a/b). This action does not target the destination.

Successful movement uses both host links, static layer application, attachment
timestamp order and the existing attach event (CR 701.3c). It does not change
ownership or control, create a zone move, offer payment or run a replacement
operation. Each action instance has its own result declaration. Copies, clones
and delayed bodies keep separate resolution frames. Waiting source queries
traverse explicit attachment, player and collection reads without evaluating
filters, making choices or changing state.

RON accepts `AttachPermanentToAPermanent` with exactly two positional arguments:
a bound singular attachment reference and a supported resolving host collection.
Ordinary resolving action sequences, direct scoped player bodies and delays are
supported. Entry and draw replacement contexts reject the declaration. No
`TheChosenPermanent` result escapes this action.

Evidence: `TestAttachmentMove`, `TestAttachmentMoveDeclarations`,
`TestAttachmentMoveKindsAndTimestamp`, `TestAttachmentMoveWaiting`,
`TestRONAttachmentMoveAlteration`, `TestRONAttachmentMoveInvalid`,
`TestRONAttachmentMoveScopesAndDelay`, `TestRONAttachmentMovePlayerScope` and
`TestRONAttachmentMoveKudzuPrerequisite`. Enchantment Alteration has complete RON
casting and gameplay evidence; Kudzu has only movement prerequisite evidence.


## Dependent singular permanent target queries

`TargetSharesCardTypeWith(reference *PermanentTargetBinding, types
...core.CardType) PermanentTargetOption` requires a shared current card type
with an earlier singular permanent target. The supplied type list is copied;
omission permits all card types. Definition validation rejects nil, undeclared,
self or forward references, invalid/duplicate types, and lists that combine this
option with nonsingular or nonpermanent declarations. RON's restricted spelling
also rejects an empty list. Both resolving collections and target comparisons
reuse `sharesPermanentCardType`; only collections permit their documented LKI.

`Game.PossibleTargetGroup(controller uuid.UUID, card Card, specs []Target,
group int, chosen []uuid.UUID, x int) []uuid.UUID` queries fixed singular groups.
The earlier prefix must be legal and have one choice per earlier declaration.
The query excludes candidates with no complete later selection. It keeps X and
typed target captures in a separate shallow query game with separate binding
storage. It makes no choices, payments or random calls and does not replace live
resolution bindings. Pure activation/spell availability and modal legality use
complete-selection checks. Explicit announcements, prompted and forced choices,
opponent choices and trigger placement share the context. Existing optional and
plural target group boundaries retain their original validation.

At resolution all targeting restrictions use the saved exact visits and current
characteristics before any effects run (CR 608.2b). A present earlier target can
supply the targeting relation even if shroud makes its own slot illegal. Its
return or phasing cannot supply a present reference; no departure LKI restores
this relation (CR 400.7, 702.26b). Illegal resolving slots remain absent from
effect bindings. Source departure, control, protection and LKI keep the existing
target-source service. Factory instances and cloned games have separate captures.

Copy retargeting reads each newly selected earlier group for later candidates.
It permits unchanged illegal targets (CR 707.10c). Explicit legal rechoices save
current battlefield incarnations, including returned cards with the same physical
ID. Cancellation retains old captures. Copies do not alter the original's
choices or captures. Costs and replacements retain the shared transaction;
Gauntlets' exact activation prefix proves failed pairs cannot spend mana or
sacrifice the source. Trigger APNAP and removal use the existing placement service
(CR 602.2b, 603.3c-d); the new query adds no event or payment subsystem.

Evidence: `TestTargetDependency` (legality, type changes, absence, phasing, copies
and clones), `Declarations`, `Query` (complete-selection pruning, forced choices,
list immutability and purity), `CopyAndPrompt`, `CopyReturnedChoice` (failing-first
returned-visit regression), and `Triggers`; `TestRONTargetDependency*` adds
spell/activation rollback, mode/event/opponent scope, independent factories and
the exact Gauntlets prefix. Complete Gauntlets gameplay remains blocked by its
exchange-result consumer and the recorded Aura-only source defect.

## Integer counter capacity

Counters use `int` throughout live permanent arrays, exact departure snapshots
and interactive raw snapshots. Fixed entry RON amounts above 255 lower to
`EntersWithNCounters(counter, n)` with the existing nonnegative literal contract.
No byte conversion can change entry placement, ordinary addition/removal,
loyalty damage or saved departure counts. The shared replacement service retains
affected-controller choices and replacement rechecks (CR 122.6, 614.1c, 616.1).
The array representation retains value-copy clone isolation. Phasing retains
counts; zone return starts fresh counters for a new visit (CR 122.2, 400.7,
702.26d). Typed byte-array callers require mechanical integer-array updates.

Evidence: `TestCounterCapacity` covers 255, 256, 300 and 65,536 counters at entry,
addition across the old bound, failed and successful removal, clone isolation,
phase cycles, exact departure snapshots and fresh return.
`TestRONCounterCapacity` casts synthetic RON cards with those fixed counts, checks
entry timing and factory isolation. `TestRONCounterCapacityTriskelion` executes
the complete ATQ record with seven counter doublers, 384 entry counters, rejected
target announcement without payment, and a paid damage activation.
`TestRONCounterCapacityReplacementOrder` checks 606 versus 306 counters from
add-then-double versus double-then-add and the entering controller's decision.
Existing fixed-entry rejection tests retain every invalid form except the former
256 storage rejection, which is now a positive gameplay case.

This service is a prerequisite for Rock Hydra's announced-X entry and
Frankenstein's Monster's entry-result counter distribution. It does not add X
entry scope, payments, result bindings or complete gameplay for those cards.
The separate bounded-counter declaration context retains its 0–255 limit.
Counts use machine integers, as do the engine's damage and other numeric values.


## Announced X for battlefield entry

The private `battlefieldEntryContext` contains separate `announcedX` and
`castColorsSpent` integer fields. Permanent spell resolution supplies its own
`StackObject.XValue`; every direct entry wrapper supplies zero X. The proposed
`battlefieldEntryAction` retains these values through copy replacements. No
ambient resolution value or permanent counter count supplies X (CR 107.3a,
107.3g, 107.3m, 400.7d). A copied permanent spell retains its copied X; its
payment-color count remains zero. The context does not survive battlefield entry.
Phasing retains counters; a returned object starts new counters and receives zero
entry X unless a new resolving spell supplies it (CR 400.7, 702.26d).

`AnnouncedXForEnteringPermanent() EntryCounterValue` and
`EntersWithCounters(counter, amount)` use that context before entry events.
The retained `EntersWithXCounters` API uses the same context. Counter placement
uses the shared replacement service and affected-controller ordering
(CR 122.6, 614.1c, 614.12, 616.1). With zero native X, external entry additions
still run through the existing synthesized placement proposal; doubling alone
does not invent counters. Entry copying acquires the new definition's entry rule
but keeps the entering spell's X, separate from the donor's existing counters.
Clones retain independent stack objects, entry ability identities and counters.

Evidence: `TestEntryAnnouncedXDirect`, `SpellAndReturn`, `Context`,
`AcquiredCopyRules` and `Definition`; RON `TestRONEntryAnnouncedX`,
`Declarations`, `ReplacementOrder`, `Observer` and `HydraRecord`.
Payment rollback leaves hand, mana and stack unchanged; entry observers see
counters only after resolution. Replacement tests distinguish add-then-double
from double-then-add and verify that only the entering controller chooses.
The RON adapter accepts one source entry counter operation with the `ValueX`
symbol. Entry exile payments, entry result bindings and counter distribution
remain separate contracts. No complete-card acceptance gain is claimed.


## Saved permanent-control exchange outcomes

`BindControlExchangeResult(name string) *ControlExchangeResultBinding` declares
one typed outcome. `ExchangePermanentControlInto(first, second PermanentRef,
result *ControlExchangeResultBinding) ResolvingEffect` writes success or failure
on every call. `IfControlExchanged(result *ControlExchangeResultBinding,
body ResolvingEffect) ResolvingEffect` runs its body only for saved success.

The producer reuses `Game.ExchangeControl` and its simultaneous layer 2 pass
(CR 701.12a-b). It adds no control mechanics. Missing, returned, phased,
identical, same-controller or prohibited subjects save failure. Exact references
and resolution target legality retain their existing contracts. Failure replaces
older success. Later control changes and departures do not change the saved
historical result. Definition validation requires a producer on every read path
and rejects nil references, results and bodies.

The typed binding stores its private value in the shared number frame. Copies,
clones, delayed bodies and factory instances use the existing frame services;
there is no global result slot. Waiting queries traverse the producer references
and conditional body without executing an exchange.

RON supports `If(PermanentsChangedControlThisWay, [actions...])` after the latest
local `ExchangeControl(permanentRef, permanentRef)` in ordinary resolving
sequences. The condition must be a symbol and the body must be nonempty.
Branches keep local producers; an outer result can be captured by a delayed
body. Entry, replacement, static, cost and other conditional forms remain
unsupported. Both existing exchange callers and the result-free API remain.

Gauntlets of Chaos now executes its complete LEG RON record. Local
`data/LEG.json` Oracle text requires destruction of Auras attached to the
exchanged subjects. Its RON collection now intersects `IsEnchantmentType(Aura)`
with the two attachment sets. Equipment remains on the battlefield. There is
only one record for this name; no reprint correction is needed.

Evidence: `TestControlExchangeResult*` checks historical success, repeated failure,
identity, phasing and declaration validation. `TestRONControlExchangeResult*`
checks full Gauntlets gameplay, mana/sacrifice rollback and timing, failed exchanges,
Aura-only destruction, copies, instances, clone isolation, local producer
selection and delayed frames. `TestRONTargetDependencyGauntletsPrerequisite`
now runs the full record with all prior target legality and payment assertions.
Existing native atomic-exchange and duration tests remain in validation.

## Static per-point counter-removal prevention

`PreventDamageToSourceByRemovingCounters(counterType) ContinuousEffect` retains
its public signature and live source/declaration checks. Positive damage removes
`min(damage, matching counters)` counters and prevents the same amount. Empty
counters cannot match. The damage source and combat status remain on any residual
packet. Damage assignment precedes replacement, so combat power is fixed before
counter removal. State actions follow damage; zero toughness cannot regenerate.

CR 615.12 requires counter removal even when damage cannot be prevented. Both
single-action and simultaneous pipelines now admit an additional-effect rule
through the private `appliesToUnpreventableDamage() bool` contract. The counter
rule removes counters and returns the unchanged damage packet in this context.
Each rule applies once per packet (CR 615.12a). Existing finite shields retain
capacity. The combined prevention/redirection prohibition keeps excluding other
rules; this slice does not define new unpreventable-damage syntax.

Shared replacement choices use the affected controller and APNAP batch order
(CR 616.1). Redirection first can remove the original recipient from the counter
rule; counter prevention first can eliminate the redirect event. Depletion is
checked for each packet. Rules from different source visits and declarations stay
separate. Phasing and ability removal stop static prevention; phase-in and ability
restoration can resume it. Departure ends it, and return needs a new registration.
Waiting queries retain exact active subjects without consuming counters. Clones
keep separate rules and counters (CR 400.7, 702.26).

RON accepts this exact static shape on a permanent:

```text
PreventDamage(EachDamageWouldBeDealtToRecipient(Permanent(ThisPermanent)),
 [If(PermanentPassesFilter(ThisPermanent,HasACounterOfType(counter)),
  [RemoveCounters([ACounterOfTypeFromPermanent(counter,ThisPermanent)]),
   PreventThatDamage])])
```

All three references must be the source and both counter declarations must match.
The shared permanent-counter parser validates counter kinds. Other recipients,
conditions, removal quantities, operation order and resolving contexts reject at
compilation. Each factory creates a fresh static rule ID. The adapter does not
execute arbitrary resolving actions inside a replacement.

Evidence: native `TestCounterPointPreventionUnpreventable` and retained
`TestWaitingCounterPreventionReferences`/`Boundaries`; RON
`TestRONCounterPointPrevention`, `Invalid`, `Ordering`, `BatchAndCombat`,
`Hydra`, `HydraShieldLifetime`, `HydraZeroToughness`, `Inventory` and
`RasputinSourceCorrection`. Full Hydra records exercise X casting, both mana
activations, upkeep legality and rollback. Rasputin's test covers only the entry,
mana and corrected shield prerequisite; the later turn-start contract adds
history evidence. Counter-cap support remains open. Resolved finite shields reuse their existing lifetime contract.


## Matching plural graveyard exile payments

`ExileMatchingCardsFromSingleGraveyardCost(amount int, filter CardFilter,
players PlayerSet) Cost` extends the existing plural graveyard exile payment.
Definition validation requires a nonnegative count, nonzero card filter and
nonnull typed player set. The payer chooses from eligible graveyards that each
contain enough matching cards. The first card chooses the graveyard; remaining
choices are distinct members of that same graveyard. Only the payer chooses,
even when the cards belong to another player (CR 602.1a, 602.2b, 118.3).
The player set reads the payment source and controller context. Queries do not
choose cards, move cards, spend resources or use randomness. Zero payments need
no card choices; an absent payer or empty eligible player set cannot pay.

The shared `costPaymentTransaction` copies and locks the cost, then validates
all costs on a cloned game. Choices save the visits present when offered.
Before payment, each card must retain that exact graveyard visit and match the
filter; a returned card cannot pay (CR 400.7). Invalid, duplicate, cross-graveyard,
absent and changed-type choices fail. Overlapping costs cannot reuse a card.
Failure retains live mana, life, zones and stack. `EitherCost` uses the same
locked payment. Declarations retain no chosen state between activations.

The native batch removes all selected cards and places them in face-up exile
with their original owners and the paying ability's source attribution. It then
sends each `EvtZoneChange` with the graveyard holder as `PlayerID`, followed by
one `EvtCardsLeftGraveyard` with the full count (CR 701.13a, 406.3, 603.10).
Observers see the completed zone batch. This uses existing player removal,
exile storage, exact-visit and event services. It does not create a separate
replacement system. Existing own-graveyard plural and singular cost callers
retain their behavior. The new service does not write a global last-action slot.

Night Soil pays at announcement and creates its token at resolution. Countering
the activation does not undo payment. Pending bodies keep their controller after
source departure, control change or phasing. Copies create tokens for their own
controller without another payment. Factory instances, repeated activations and
game clones remain independent. Source return cannot alter paid graveyard visits.

Evidence: native `TestSingleGraveyardExileCostSelection`, `Rollback`, `Batch`,
`DefinitionAndZero`, `ChoiceVisit`, `PlayerSetAndAlternative`; retained
`TestGraveyardExileCost*` and `TestExileDamageSourceStackBindings`. RON evidence:
`TestRONSingleGraveyardExileCostNightSoil`, `Rollback`, `IndependentActivations`,
`Invalid`, `Inventory`. The adapter supports fixed counts with AnyPlayer only.
Entry transactions, dynamic counts, entry results and failed-entry continuations
remain separate contracts. No complete Frankenstein's Monster claim is made.

## Entry color choice

`ChooseColorAsEnters() AsEntersBattlefieldAbility` saves a color on the entering
permanent before battlefield registration (CR 614.1c, 614.12, 614.12a). It uses
the entry controller, including when the owner is another player. The choice
uses `ChooseManaColor` once. Only white, blue, black, red and green are legal
(CR 105.1, 105.4); invalid answers and absent choosers use white. The typed
`core.Color` field belongs to the permanent visit, not the card definition.

The shared entry pipeline applies copy replacements first. Acquired color
choice declarations run once and choose independently of the donor's saved
color. Shared batches prepare all choices before battlefield registration and
zone events. This operation creates no stack object and makes no payment.
Unpaid casting and announcement do not run it. Definition validation rejects
this battlefield-source ability on an instant or sorcery.

Control changes and phasing do not repeat entry (CR 702.26). Return creates a
new visit and repeats the choice (CR 400.7). Game clones keep separate fields.
`TestChooseColorAsEntersTimingAndIdentity` covers all five colors, illegal
answers, pre-registration timing, controller versus owner, phasing, control,
clone isolation and return. `TestChooseColorAsEntersCopyAndMissingPlayer`
covers independent copied definitions, absent choosers and invalid source zones.
`TestChooseColorAsEntersCopyReplacementAndBatch` covers copy replacement
priority, acquired declarations and complete-batch visibility to entry events.

RON `TestRONColorEntry*` covers strict lowering, invalid declarations, native
casting, failed payment, pending clones, phasing, return, semantic inventory,
atomic collection rejection and Psychic Allergy's unchanged entry declaration.
The resolving chosen-color information contract is recorded below. Combined
color/opponent entry choices are supported below. Jihad's static and state
consumers have separate contracts below.
Legacy ETB color helpers retain their current callers and behavior.

## Exact chosen-color collection information

`PermanentsOfChosenColor(reference PermanentRef, subjects PermanentSet) PermanentSet`
reads the color saved on the reference's exact visit. The shared information
reader supplies current data, exact departure LKI, or the phase snapshot
(CR 608.2h, 400.7, 702.26). Source, singular target, saved reference and attachment
host reads use the existing identity service. Unset, wildcard and invalid colors
select no members (CR 105.1, 105.4). A returned source cannot replace its old visit.

Subjects must remain present and unphased with the same visit. Their current
layered colors supply membership, including multicolor subjects (CR 105.2,
105.3). The service removes duplicate subjects. It does not restore absent
subjects or make choices, payment, randomness or events. Information reads do
not by themselves establish target legality; target actions keep the existing
resolution legality checks. Definition validation rejects missing subjects,
invalid information references and unbound target/saved declarations.

Delayed source inspection traverses both the reference and the subjects without
executing the collection. Clones keep independent live choices and frozen
snapshots. `TestChosenColorInformationIdentity` covers current and departure
facts, return, phasing, phase cycles, missing identity, invalid colors, current
color layers, multicolor members, absent members and pure queries in clones.
`TestChosenColorInformationSavedReferences` covers target, saved and host reads
across return. `TestChosenColorInformationDeclarationsAndWaiting` covers
invalid definitions, pure waiting declarations and clone choice isolation.
RON contract evidence is in `TestRONChosenColorFilter*`.


## Required entry sequences and combined choices

`RequiredEntryOperations(operations ...AsEntersBattlefieldAbility)` returns one
required entry ability. Children run in declaration order before battlefield
registration; a false child stops later children and rejects entry through the
existing failed-entry destination. This service makes no optional offer and
stores no decision. It copies the input slice. Definition validation rejects
empty bodies, nil/typed-nil children, invalid nested declarations and use on
nonpermanent cards.

The combined color/opponent operation uses `ChooseColorAsEnters` followed by
`ChooseOpponentAsEnters`. The entry controller supplies both choices, regardless
of ownership (CR 109.5, 614.12a). Color and opponent occupy separate permanent
fields. Copy replacements run first (CR 616.1c); the acquired sequence chooses
again instead of inheriting the donor's choices (CR 707.2). Shared batches finish
all choices and battlefield registrations before any entry observer runs.

Control changes and phase cycles keep both fields (CR 702.26b–d). Return starts
a new visit and repeats both operations (CR 400.7). Independent factories,
permanent spell copies and game clones keep separate choices. Announcement and
failed casting payment do not run entry operations. Existing exact source
information and chosen-player upkeep detection supply later resolving consumers;
a returned source cannot replace the pending trigger's saved color choice.

RON accepts only one ordered color/opponent pair on `ThisPermanent`, in one entry
declaration. This establishes no entry payment transaction, plural payment result,
static chosen-color membership, state trigger or joint whole-object text revision.

Evidence: `TestRequiredEntryOperationsOrderAndFailure`, `Declarations`,
`CopyReplacementAndBatch`, `ChoiceOrder`; `TestRONCombinedEntryChoiceGameplay`,
`Invalid`, `Jihad`, `Consumers`. Jihad's exact entry declaration retains separate
gameplay evidence. Its complete unchanged record now compiles, with full-card
gameplay established by the source-choice absence contract below.

## Opponent upkeep with typed event capture

`OpponentUpkeep(player *PlayerBinding) EventPattern` uses `EachUpkeep` and
`EventPlayerIsOpponent` in the two-player engine. The event compares with the
source controller at detection, as required by CR 109.5 and 603.3a. It writes
one event-local player binding through the existing turn-step capture service.
CR 503.1a and 603.2b require detection at each actual upkeep boundary; the body
runs later through normal trigger placement and resolution. A skipped upkeep
sends no boundary event. Repeated boundaries make independent pending captures.

Source control changes before detection change the opponent. Changes after
detection keep the captured upkeep player and trigger controller. Source
phasing and ability removal stop detection; they cannot cancel a pending body
(CR 113.7a). Departure and return cannot replace its saved source visit
(CR 400.7). Copies keep the event player while using their copy controller.
Delayed bodies and game clones use separate existing resolution frames.
Nil or unnamed bindings and reads from another ability fail definition checks.
This event supplies no payment, damage, replacement or text-revision service.

RON supports the bare `Opponent` selector in ordinary upkeep `TriggerA` bodies.
It retains separate boundaries for granted events, intervening-if declarations,
other steps and printed upkeep text revision. Psychic Allergy's resolving damage
uses live nontoken members and the exact source visit's chosen color. Its other
upkeep uses the existing optional two-permanent sacrifice transaction and
ordinary destruction. Local `data/DRK.json` confirms all three source rules;
no source correction was needed.

Evidence: `TestOpponentUpkeepCapture`, `SourceLifetime` and `Declarations`;
`TestRONOpponentUpkeepGameplay`, `PsychicAllergy`, `PsychicAllergyPayment`,
`Invalid` and `CollectionAndTextBoundary`. Existing color-entry, chosen-color,
optional sacrifice, upkeep text and collection inventory tests remain required.

## Live source entry choices in static membership

`PlayerControls(player PlayerRef, filter PermanentFilter) StateCondition` now
also accepts `ChosenPlayerOf(This)`. Existing controller, active-player and
saved-player callers retain their contracts. Other chosen-permanent references
are rejected during definition validation.

`PlayerControlsChosenColor(player PlayerRef, filter PermanentFilter)
StateCondition` accepts `You`, `ActivePlayer` or `ChosenPlayerOf(This)`. It
requires a present, unphased source with a valid five-color entry choice and
checks the supplied filter plus that color through `FilterBattlefield`.
`resolveStatePermanent` checks `StateContext.SourceIncarnation`; an old source
visit cannot read a returned source's choices. There is no departure LKI read.
Unbound players, nil references and chosen attachment/saved/target references
are rejected. The condition stores declarations only, with no mutable choices.

Source control changes keep the chosen player. Subject control and color changes
update membership. Phasing stops source reads and excludes subjects; phase-in
restores the same choices. Return makes new entry choices. Clones and separate
sources keep separate fields. `While` and the shared layer service reevaluate
membership, apply color/control before P/T and disable a removed source ability
(CR 611.3a–b, 613.1b/e–g, 613.4c, 400.7, 702.26b–d).

Evidence: `TestChosenStaticConditionIdentity`, `Declarations` and
`TestRONChosenStatic*`. RON gameplay covers Jihad's entry/static subrules,
casting/entry timing, both players' white recipients, nonwhite exclusion,
nontoken membership, changing color/control, late subjects, phasing, source
return, independent instances, clones and ability removal. State detection,
replacement ordering, payments and simultaneous actions gain no new contract.

## Source-choice absence conditions and state detection

`PlayerControlsNone(player PlayerRef, filter PermanentFilter) StateCondition`
checks that a known player controls no present matching permanents. It uses the
shared `resolveStatePlayer`, `PlayerControls` and `FilterBattlefield` readers.
It accepts the existing controller, active-player, bound-player and source
`ChosenPlayerOf(This)` contexts. Bound players must have a definition producer.
Missing or unknown players return false, rather than satisfying absence.

`PlayerControlsNoneOfChosenColor(player PlayerRef, filter PermanentFilter)
StateCondition` requires a live source with a valid five-color entry choice.
It accepts `You`, `ActivePlayer` or `ChosenPlayerOf(This)` and uses the supplied
filter in conjunction with that color. Definition checks reuse the positive
condition contracts; nil, attachment/saved-object chosen references and unbound
players reject. `StateContext.SourceIncarnation` prevents old queries from reading
returned choices. Source departure/phasing supplies no LKI to these conditions.

`WhenState` uses these pure declarations through the existing state-trigger
service (CR 603.8). Each source visit/rule can have one pending or active trigger.
Phasing and ability removal stop detection; restoration permits it. Subject
control and color use current layers (CR 613.1b/e). Nontoken filters exclude
physical tokens regardless of copy characteristics. Pending bodies retain source
identity and the controller at detection (CR 603.3a, 113.7a); ordinary state
triggers do not check membership again at resolution. A returned source cannot
be sacrificed by its old body (CR 400.7), and a phased source cannot be acted on
(CR 702.26b). A controller change after detection does not authorize the old
controller to sacrifice the source (CR 701.21a). New detection under the new
controller remains possible after the old trigger leaves the stack.

Native evidence: `TestPlayerAbsenceConditionIdentity` and `Declarations` cover
missing/invalid choices, exact visits, phasing, multicolor subjects, tokens,
clone isolation and definition validation. RON evidence:
`TestRONChosenStateAbsenceJihad`, `Lifecycle`, `SpellCopy`, `Filters`, `Invalid`.
Complete Jihad gameplay includes actual casting, separate entry choices for spell
copies, global white P/T and queued sacrifice after membership returns. Existing
`TestRONChosenStatic*` and `TestRONCombinedEntryChoice*` retain their subrule tests.
No new payment, replacement-order or simultaneous-operation contract is added.


## Source-card zone event lifetimes

`WithSourceCardInZone(zone core.Zone, source *CardBinding) TriggerOption`
selects one graveyard or face-up exile source zone. Use it with `WhenEvent`.
The event has no targets or modes. Definition validation
rejects invalid/nil bindings, other zones, duplicate zone options, added active
zones, state events, target declarations, modes and battlefield
source reads. Conditions and effects cannot treat this source as a permanent.

The graveyard holder controls graveyard triggers; the card owner controls exile
triggers. Valid game zones place cards in their owners' graveyards (CR 400.3).
Event detection makes a separate ability context instead of changing card-level
source/controller fields. The shared graveyard scan retains existing callers;
the exile scan ignores face-down cards, including cards visible to one player
(CR 603.2f). Ordinary upkeep events use the same pending queue and APNAP stack
placement as battlefield triggers. Distinct occurrences queue distinct bodies.

Detection saves the source's exact zone visit in a typed `CardBinding`.
`FromCard(source)` reads that visit while present. Departure does not stop a
queued body; return cannot replace the saved visit (CR 400.7, 113.7a).
The trigger controller and event player stay separate through pending placement,
stack copying and game cloning (CR 603.3a). Independent later effects still run
when a source action cannot read its departed visit. These source actions do not
use battlefield LKI. Delayed bodies save the existing resolution frame.

`ExiledCardFrom(card CardRef) ExiledCardSet` adapts one current typed card
reference to the shared exile collection service. It supplies no subject for a
missing, stale or non-exiled read. `PutExiledCardsInOwnersGraveyards` supplies
owner destinations, graveyard ordering and zone events. Graveyard-to-hand reads
use `ReturnCardToHand` and the shared graveyard movement service.

`TestSourceZoneUpkeepVisit`, `Declarations` and `Detection` cover exact visits,
owner/player separation, pre-resolution timing, wrong zones, source phasing,
hidden exile, source departure/return, immutable detection contexts, separate
copies/events, pending clones, definition rejection and APNAP order.
RON `TestRONSourceZoneUpkeep*` adds explicit registry execution, lexical scope,
atomic rejection, delayed frames and real-record prerequisite projections.


## Source-card intervening conditions and ordered graveyard reads

`WithSourceCardInZone` now supports `WithInterveningIf(StateCondition)` on a
non-state event without targets or modes. CR 603.4 requires a true condition
at detection and again at resolution. Detection supplies the source card's
current zone visit and the event player in a separate query frame. It does not
change the active resolution frame or the ability declaration. Resolution uses
the queued binding. A departed or returned source cannot supply that visit;
these conditions do not use LKI (CR 400.7). A false resolution condition stops
the whole body. Existing unguarded zone events keep their independent effects.

`GraveyardCardHasAtLeastAbove(card CardRef, player PlayerRef, minimum int,
filter CardFilter) StateCondition` requires a saved `FromCard` reference and a
nonnegative minimum. It first checks the exact saved visit and player, then
counts matching cards after that card in the existing graveyard slice. New
arrivals append at the top (CR 404.1); the source and cards below it do not count.
A minimum of zero still requires membership in the selected player's graveyard.
The shared graveyard service owns ordering and simultaneous arrival choices
(CR 404.2/3). This query does not reorder or move cards.

`CardMatchesFilter(card CardRef, filter CardFilter) StateCondition` checks the
current card at a saved visit. Both APIs reject target references because these
condition queries have no target-selection frame. Missing or unwritten bindings
fail definition validation. Source-zone declarations still reject battlefield
source reads. Face-down exile cannot arm a trigger, even when its owner can
inspect the card (CR 603.2f). Exile counter storage is outside this contract.

The existing event captures, pending queue, stack copies and clone services keep
separate visits and players. `You` remains the effect controller; a copy under
another controller checks that controller's graveyard. The event player stays
captured separately. No payment, replacement or simultaneous-movement service
changes in this slice.

Native `TestSourceZoneCondition*` covers event/resolution checks, exact returns,
zero counts, mixed card types, hidden exile, both trigger-option orders,
unchanged query frames and declarations, copied controllers, pending clones and
invalid definitions. RON `TestRONSourceZoneCondition*` adds factory isolation,
strict atomic loading, syntax rejection and six Nether Shadow condition tests.
Those record projections replace only the unsupported body with a life probe;
they do not establish complete-card gameplay.

## Restricted fixed mana production

`mage.AddRestrictedMana(productions []mage.ManaProduction, restriction
core.ManaRestriction) mage.ResolvingEffect` copies a nonempty fixed production
batch and applies the supplied spending rule to every unit. Colors must be
concrete; amounts must be positive. Any-combination production and a missing
restriction fail definition validation. Caller and metadata slices cannot
change the saved declaration.

The batch passes through `addEffectMana` as one proposed event. Type replacements
retain each unit's restriction (CR 106.6); production tracking and tapped-for-mana
events use existing services. Fixed solver metadata retains the same restrictions
as manual production. The shared spell payment context permits artifact-only or
creature-only mana for matching spells, including artifact creatures, and rejects
it for activation costs. Pure queries do not tap sources or spend resources.
Failed casting payments retain live resources. Source departure does not remove
mana already produced. Clones keep separate pools and payment state.

RON supports `AddManaWithModifiers(fixedProduction,
CanOnlySpendOnSpells(IsCardtype(Artifact|Creature)))` in resolving bodies.
`fixedProduction` is a fixed mana symbol or nested nonempty `And([...])` lists.
Any-color production, empty nested groups, unsupported filters and entry/layer
contexts reject at compilation. `AddManaRepeatedWithModifiers(AnyManaColor,
value, restriction)` reuses this restriction adapter, with its existing amount
and one-color choice contracts. This adds Artifact as a permitted spell type
there; Metamorphosis retains its existing Creature behavior. No X-spending or
as-though color-spending contract is established.

Evidence: `TestRestrictedFixedManaPaths`, `Declarations` and `Batch` cover native
manual/solver parity, replacement batching, declaration isolation and clone
payment. `TestRONRestrictedFixedManaWorkshop` executes the complete unchanged
Mishra's Workshop record for manual production, artifact casting, artifact
creatures, nonartifact rejection, activation rejection, insufficient payment,
phasing and rollback. `Registry` uses a real RON registry and separate factory
instances, tests retained restrictions after source departure, and checks
inventory roles. `SpellCopies` covers mixed colors, nested production, both
restrictions, repeated one-color production and spell copies under separate
controllers and in cloned games. `Invalid` checks compiler contexts, malformed
forms, nested empty groups and atomic registry rejection. Existing
`TestRONSacrificeManaMetamorphosis` retains full Metamorphosis coverage.

## Optional exact graveyard return

`MayReturnNonAuraCardToBattlefield(card CardRef, player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`
adds an optional normal-entry form for non-Aura permanents to the existing typed
graveyard return operation. The selected player chooses at resolution and is the entry controller
and actor. Ownership stays unchanged. A missing player, unavailable reference,
a nonpermanent, an Aura or a card outside a graveyard supplies no offer. The
graveyard visit is saved before the offer and checked again after acceptance. A departed
or returned card cannot supply entry (CR 400.7). This action does not use LKI.

An accepted offer uses `returnGraveyardCardToBattlefieldWithEntry` and the shared
entry preparation, exact-visit recheck, graveyard move, registration and entry
completion services. Entry counters and tapped-entry replacements run before
entry events (CR 603.6d, 614.1c/d). There is no payment or simultaneous batch in
this singular operation. Decline leaves the card in its graveyard and does not
stop later instructions or later event offers (CR 603.5).

Definition validation retains the existing card/player child contracts: nil
references, unwritten card/player bindings and undeclared targets reject. The
optional declaration stores no chosen state. Event frames, stack copies, delayed
frames and game clones keep saved visits separate. The existing explicit
controller-source read also serves the optional form in waiting delayed queries.
Queries do not read players or cards, make offers, move cards or change frames.
Phasing preserves that waiting reference; a returned source cannot replace it.

RON accepts exactly one normal-entry non-Aura source return inside `MayAction` in
`FromGraveyard` upkeep action lists and saved delayed lists. Aura declarations
reject because the shared return path does not supply Aura attachment choices. Source-zone trigger and intervening-condition restrictions
remain unchanged. Nether Shadow checks its own graveyard visit and three creature cards above it at detection and at
resolution (CR 603.4, 404.1). A copy under another controller checks that
controller's graveyard. Two copies cannot return the same original visit twice.
Phased battlefield cards do not acquire graveyard trigger membership.

Native `TestOptionalGraveyardReturn`, `Declarations` and `Waiting` cover offer
acceptance/decline, missing and returned visits, departure during choice,
owner/controller separation, counters and entry replacement order, wrong zones,
nonpermanents, invalid bindings, source identity, query purity and clone lifetime.
RON `TestRONOptionalGraveyardReturnNetherShadow` covers all six complete records,
ordered threshold checks, haste, factory isolation, pending and stacked clones,
copies, source phasing and entry replacements. `Frames` covers distinct events,
delays, returned delayed visits and independent continuation actions. `Invalid`
covers unsupported signatures/contexts and atomic registry rejection. The old
source-zone condition projections remain prerequisite tests; the new unchanged
record tests establish complete-card behavior.

## Controller colored mana spending

`mage.ControllerManaSpending(from, to core.Color) mage.ContinuousEffect`
permits the source controller to spend one mana color as another color.
Definition validation requires two of the five colors. It uses a battlefield
static rule; the RON adapter accepts exactly
`PlayerEffect(You, [MaySpendColoredManaAsThoughItWereAnotherColor(color, color)])`.
Other players, operation lists, colorless/any-color arguments, resolving bodies,
entry operations and instant/sorcery static declarations reject.

RON validates spelling, arguments and context, then builds a fresh static rule
for each factory. The engine reads active rules after object layers and control
restrictions. Phase changes refresh permissions without a layer pass. Ability
removal, departure and phasing stop the rule. Restoration, return and phase-in
use the current source visit and controller. Copies retain independent rules;
game clones retain independent permission arrays and pools.

The shared mana pool planner, solver demand limits, relaxed affordability bounds,
activation-payment validation and final payment use the same permission graph.
Permissions combine and can form chains or cycles. Each actual mana unit keeps
its color and restriction. A white unit spent for a red cost is recorded as white.
No mana production or replacement event occurs for this permission. Queries make
no choices and spend no resources. Failed payment retains the existing shared
transaction contract. Existing global `ManaConversion` callers and
`ManaSolverInputs.Conversions` remain supported. Restricted X uses the separate spell spending contract below.

CR 106.6 preserves spending restrictions; CR 609.4a permits combined as-though
conditions; CR 609.4b preserves costs and actual spent mana; CR 613.11 applies
game rules after object layers. Local LEA Oracle text agrees with the unchanged
six Sunglasses of Urza RON records.

Evidence: `TestRONManaSpendingSunglasses` covers all six complete records and
metadata, cast/entry, controller scope, control changes, phasing, ability
removal/restoration, return and game clones. `Automatic` covers Plains auto-payment,
actual spent colors, resolution and failed payment resource preservation.
`Copies` covers Copy Artifact, donor departure and copied ability removal.
`Invalid` and `StrictLoad` cover declaration rejection and atomic loading.
`TestColoredManaSpending`, `ActivationAndHybrid` and `Declarations` cover
competing/chained permissions, restricted mana, clone isolation, automatic mana
activation payments, hybrid costs, X bounds, separate players and invalid colors.


## Restricted X spell spending

`mage.WithXSpendingColor(color core.Color) mage.ActionOption` declares one
spending color on a spell action. Native definition validation rejects duplicate
rules, invalid colors, non-spell actions and cards without printed X.
RON accepts exactly `CastEffect(SpendOnlyColorManaOnX(color))` on an ordinary
instant or sorcery with printed X. The argument is one of the five color symbols.
Other arities, tuple-shaped colors, colorless/any-color arguments, duplicate
CastEffect declarations, permanents, modal spells and resolving declarations
reject before publication. Restricted spells do not acquire the ordinary
spell text-continuation marker; color-word revision needs a separate adapter.

`SpellContextForCard` returns a fresh context with `XSpendingRestricted` and
`XSpendingColor`. `RestrictedGeneric` saves the restricted part of a resolved
payment, not a change to the mana cost. The shared spell transaction counts
announced X in its selected mana cost and additional costs. It applies taxes,
then reductions. Reductions remove restricted X first, so the resulting payment
can use the least restrictive legal allocation. Other generic mana remains
unrestricted. Announced X and printed mana symbols retain their values.
Channel can substitute life only for the remaining unrestricted generic amount.
An alternative mana cost without X requires announced X zero and supplies no
restricted X payment. Negative X rejects before payment.

The pool planner converts the saved restricted amount into color demand only
for allocation. Solver bounds and variable production demand use that same
allocation view. The actual total cost remains generic. Existing as-though
permissions can supply the declared color, including the cast-from-zone
any-color permission. Actual spent colors and per-unit mana restrictions remain.
Mana replacements run through the existing production pipeline. Mana-ability
activation costs use their own context and do not inherit the spell restriction.
The shared transaction proves payment before changes to live resources.

`Game.MaxXValue` copies the context for each trial and counts every X symbol in
the supplied cost. It retains the existing contract: the supplied cost is the
query input; the query does not apply spell taxes, reductions or additional
costs. A caller querying a resolved cost through `CanAfford` or pool payment
supplies its remaining amount in `RestrictedGeneric`. Queries do not make
choices, produce mana or modify the supplied context. Copies retain announced X
without another payment. Separate factories and game clones retain separate
payments and pools. This declaration requires no battlefield source, LKI,
trigger timing or new simultaneous-operation contract.

Local LEA Oracle text and all six complete Drain Life records agree on its
black-only X restriction. CR 107.3a keeps announced X; CR 601.2f locks the
combined cost after increases and reductions; CR 601.2g/h supplies mana abilities
and complete payment. CR 106.6 preserves per-unit restrictions and CR 609.4a/b
supplies as-though payment without changing mana costs or actual colors.
No RON source defect or source change was needed.

Evidence: `TestRestrictedXPayment`, `Planning`, `AutomaticAndPermissions`,
`Modifiers`, `Declarations`, `AlternateAnyColor`, `MultipleSymbolsAndCosts`,
`AutomaticRollback`, `AnyColorProduction`, `AlternateWithoutX`,
`HybridAllocation` and `ReplacementsAndConversion`
cover the native contract, costs, exact color allocation, X zero, hybrid
allocation, source phasing, replacements, automatic conversions,
clone/copy isolation and rejection without resource changes.
`TestRONRestrictedXGameplay` now executes all six complete Drain Life records,
including their clamped life gain. It checks sufficient and insufficient black
mana for X, resource preservation on failed payment, targets and resolved damage.
`TestRONRestrictedXColors`, `Invalid` and `StrictLoadAndInventory` cover the five
colors, declaration contexts, atomic loading and inventory color roles.
The singular clamped-damage contract completes Drain Life gameplay support.

## Singular clamped damage values (RON execution)

`ClampedDamageAmount(results *DamageResultsBinding) ResolutionValue` reads one
positive saved outcome from `DealDamageFrom` with `DamageOutcomesInto`. Missing
or nonsingular results supply zero. Nil and unbound declarations fail definition
validation. The value never changes the damage amount.

The shared executor saves the final recipient after replacement and prevention.
It records the player's life or the planeswalker's loyalty immediately before
damage results occur (CR 120.4b–d). Actual damage, rather than life lost or
loyalty removed, supplies the upper bound. A creature's toughness is read at
value resolution from its exact current visit, departure LKI or phase snapshot
(CR 608.2h–i). Marked damage is not subtracted. A creature planeswalker applies
both limits; a negative limit supplies zero. A returned visit cannot replace the
saved recipient. This follows the local Oracle text in `data/LEA.json`: player
life and loyalty explicitly say before damage; creature toughness does not.

Existing resolution maps and outcome cloning retain independent result frames.
Both step-delayed and permanent-event-delayed bodies now save and restore the
damage-results map as well as their other bindings. Waiting queries do not run
the value. Shared damage replacement ordering, costs and simultaneous damage
execution remain unchanged; no plural RON clamping contract is introduced.

RON supports the symbol `TheClampedAmountOfDamageDealtThisWay` after the latest
local singular ordinary `SpellDealsDamage` or `PermanentDealsDamage` producer.
Typed singular recipients and union targets use the existing adapters. Branch
producers cannot export results; delays retain their producer. Collection,
entry, replacement, malformed and unbound declarations reject during compilation.

Evidence: `TestClampedDamageAmount`, `TestClampedDamageDefinition`,
`TestClampedDamageDelayed`,
`TestRONClampedDamageDrainLife`, `TestRONClampedDamageInvalid`,
`TestRONClampedDamageScopes`, `TestRONClampedDamageAtomicLoad` and the upgraded
full-record `TestRONRestrictedXGameplay`. No RON source correction was needed.

## Exact last-drawn discard payment

`mage.DiscardLastDrawnCardCost() mage.Cost` requires the payer's last successful
card draw during the current turn, still in that exact hand visit. Merely adding
a card to hand is not a draw (CR 121.1, 121.5). A later successful draw replaces
the saved identity; departure and return cannot restore it (CR 400.7). The older
draw does not become eligible when the latest draw leaves hand. Replaced and
failed draws do not overwrite history; successful draws generated by replacement
bodies do. Each card in a multi-card draw updates history separately (CR 121.2).

The existing `Player.LastDrawnCardID()` API remains. The private visit token is
saved in `BasePlayer.DrawCard`, copied by direct and wrapped-player game clones,
and cleared with the ID after final turn cleanup. Pending cleanup priority keeps
the history available. There is no shared action-result slot or card-name policy.

The cost uses the existing `discardCost` transaction, selection locking, full
payment validation and discard replacement batch. It makes no choice. Before
commit, it checks that the latest draw and hand visit still match the locked
payment. Multiple costs cannot consume the same visit. Failed affordability,
departure, return, a newer draw or cleared history leaves mana and tap costs
unpaid. Replacement destinations can pay the discard cost (CR 118.11); prevention
of the discard cannot pay it. The cost requires identity, not characteristics,
so a hidden replacement destination does not invalidate payment under CR 701.9c.
Effect-only discard replacements do not apply to this cost. Shared replacement
ordering and simultaneous batches are unchanged.

RON lowers exactly `DiscardCard(TheLastCardDrawnThisTurn)` in activation costs,
alone or in `And([...])`, to a fresh cost for each factory instance. The argument
must be a symbol. Other references, wrong arity, resolution actions, optional
resolution payments and entry operations reject. Pending abilities keep their
controller and execute their draw even if the source changes control, phases,
departs or returns. Stack copies do not repeat payment.

Evidence: native `TestLastDrawnCostIdentity`, `Transaction`, `Clone`,
`DrawReplacement`, `DiscardReplacement` and `Interleaved`; RON
`TestRONLastDrawnCostRing`, `Rollback`, `Invalid`, `AtomicLoad` and `Instances`.
Both complete unchanged Jandor's Ring records (ARN and 3ED) exercise casting,
payment and drawing. Synthetic fixtures supply replacement interaction rules.

## Fixed-color instant and sorcery copies

`CopyInstantOrSorceryWithColors(StackObjectRef, ...core.Color) ResolvingEffect`
copies a present instant or sorcery under the resolving effect controller.
The five Magic colors are valid; an empty list sets colorless. Invalid colors,
nil references and unbound declarations fail definition validation. A departed
spell or a referenced permanent spell supplies no copy. The action does not use
LKI to restore a departed stack object.

The exception modifies the copied card before optional target choices. Shared
`copyStackObjectWithCard` retains the existing copy service's identities, modes,
X, target groups, allocations, casting facts and payment bindings. Protection
uses the copy's colors during choices and resolution. Cancelled or illegal new
choices retain old targets, including illegal old targets and their saved visits.
Returned or phased targets cannot supply those visits. The copy has its own
source card and belongs to its controller. It is not cast and pays no new costs.
Instant and sorcery copies cease to exist after resolution or countering.

`CopyRetainColors`, immutable `CopiableValues.WithModifications` and the checked
text builder retain the color exception and omit color-defining abilities.
Ordinary stack color changes remain separate and are not inherited by later
copies. Game clones keep separate stack choices and ordinary color changes.
Current callers of both public stack-copy methods keep their existing behavior.
No replacement, payment or event subsystem is added.

RON accepts `CopySpellAndMayChooseNewTargetsWithEffects(ref,
[SetColor(SimpleColorList([color, ...]))])` in resolving spell bodies. The reference
must be a scoped singular target restricted to instants or sorceries. A direct
type predicate qualifies; conjunctions require a qualifying conjunct, and every
disjunction branch must qualify. Event, union, activation, delayed, replacement
and entry contexts remain unsupported. Other effects, variable colors, colorless
symbols and multiple modifications reject. The fixed color words use the existing
spell text-revision service; names, mana costs and indicators remain fixed.

Evidence: native `TestSpellCopyColorsIdentity`, `Retarget`, `Definition` and
`Exceptions`; RON `TestRONSpellCopyColorsFork`, `Hurricane`, `Shapes`, `Text`,
`Retarget`, `Modal`, `Fireball`, `Invalid` and `AtomicLoad`. All six complete Fork
records have gameplay evidence. CR 707.2, 707.9b–d and 707.10–10c establish the
copy contract; CR 400.7, 608.2b, 612.1–3 and 702.16 establish identity, resolution,
text changes and protection interactions.

## Dynamic mana colors from opponent permanents

`NewManaAbilityOfColorsOpponentPermanentsCouldProduce(filter PermanentFilter)
*ManaAbility` declares one tap-symbol mana ability. Its source's current
controller defines the opponent. Present, unphased matching permanents supply
colors from their current abilities and layers. Colorless production does not
supply an option. The amount is always one, including when the queried ability
produces several colors or several mana. An empty option set remains a mana
ability: activation pays the tap cost, produces nothing and uses no stack
(CR 605.2–3).

`Game.ManaTypesAbilityCouldProduce` retains its signature. A query-local least
fixed point starts with no colors and adds defined production outcomes. This
supports cycles with a concrete source, including colors that become defined
through repeated dependencies and type replacements. Cycles without a concrete
source stay empty (CR 106.7). It ignores costs, tapped status and activation
restrictions. Fixed unconditional production, live resolution amounts,
conditional mana declarations and dynamic production callbacks supply outcomes.
A direct saved-number amount from `RemoveAnyCountersCost` supplies a hypothetical
positive removal without testing payment. Other absent saved numbers supply
zero; the query does not use an active resolution's saved number for that read.
No query pays, chooses, uses RNG, runs a rider, moves objects or changes bindings.
Unknown legacy effect bodies do not supply invented outcomes.

The engine keeps finite color options in value metadata. Solver enumeration,
source preservation, preferred-color matching, manual production and stale-plan
rechecks use those options. Concrete selection clears option metadata before the
shared replacement event. Query replacements include all possible orders;
actual production uses the existing affected-player choice and recheck service.
A manual choice receives only legal color names through `Player.ChooseString`;
a missing or invalid answer uses the first legal color. One legal option needs
no choice. Queried spending restrictions and riders are not copied, while a
replacement on the producing source still applies to its one mana. Copies and
clones read independent source/controller facts and game state. Departed land
LKI supplies no option; a returned land is a new current subject.

RON supports exactly one ordinary
`Activated(TapPermanent(ThisPermanent), ActionList([AddMana(
AnyManaColorAPermanentCouldProduce(And([characteristicFilter,
ControlledByAPlayer(Opponent)])))]))` declaration. The conjunction has exactly
one characteristic filter and one opponent clause, in either order. The
characteristic filter uses the existing pure conditional-mana characteristic
adapter, including its conjunctions and disjunctions. Targets, scoped players,
other costs, modifiers, multiple actions, repetition, resolving spells, entry
and replacement contexts reject before factory publication. RON owns syntax;
the engine owns colors, recursion, identity, choice and mana mechanics.

Evidence: native `TestManaColorsCouldProduceOptions`, `Recursion`,
`RecursiveReplacements`, `PaymentAndReplacements`, `CounterPaymentResult`,
`Lifecycle`, `StalePlan`, `DynamicAndRiders`, and `AbsentAbility`; RON
`TestRONDynamicManaColorsFellwarStone`, `Invalid`, `ChoiceAndRegistry`,
`OpponentRecords`, and `CopyArtifact`. The sole unchanged DRK Fellwar Stone
record has complete-card cast, activation and automatic-payment evidence.
Five complete FEM storage-land records supply direct counter-payment query
interactions. City of Brass, Dwarven Ruins, Mishra's Workshop and Urza's Tower
supply existing complete-record production and replacement interactions.
Rainbow Vale and City of Shadows still reject for unrelated source-reference
and exile-payment gaps; native fixtures cover dynamic output and riders.

Local `data/DRK.json` Oracle text agrees with the unchanged RON record.
[Wizards' Commander Masters release notes](https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/feature/commander-masters-release-notes)
confirm the cost, amount, color, replacement-order and restriction contracts.
No RON source correction is needed.


## Exact exile-card counter predicates

`ExiledCard.Counters [core.NumCounters]int` belongs to one `Visit`, separate
from the physical card definition. The shared exile constructors start each
new visit with zero counters, including re-exile (CR 400.7/400.8, 122.2).
`ZoneSystem.Clone` copies the array by value. Removing another exile member or
replacing a card definition within the same visit does not change its counters.
This storage adds no placement, removal, transfer, or characteristic-changing
instruction. Future counter operations must use their own shared rules contracts.

`ExiledCardHasCounter(card CardRef, counter core.CounterType) StateCondition`
checks a positive count. `ExiledCardHasNoCounters(card CardRef, counter
core.CounterType) StateCondition` checks zero. Both require a saved `FromCard`
reference, a valid counter type, and a present face-up exile visit. Missing,
wrong-zone, departed, returned and face-down sources make both conditions false.
The zero predicate cannot infer counter absence from a failed reference. These
conditions use current counters, not departure LKI (CR 400.7, 122.1).

`WithSourceCardInZone` supplies exact event facts. `WithInterveningIf` checks at
detection and resolution (CR 603.4); `IfState` checks at its instruction during
resolution. The existing query-frame service preserves outer bindings. Queued
triggers, copies and pending clones retain the saved visit and event player.
Counter reads make no choices, pay no costs, and change no game state. Exile
cards do not phase. Battlefield phasing, counter replacement ordering and
simultaneous counter operations are outside this predicate/storage contract.

RON lowers `ExiledCardPassesFilter(ThisExiledCard,
HasACounterOfType(counter))` and `HasNoCountersOfType(counter)` in an ordinary
owner-upkeep `FromExile(TriggerI(...))` and in resolving
`If(condition, [actions])` under that zone declaration. The existing single
`IsCardtype(type)` predicate also works in the resolving branch. Counter kinds
reuse the existing checked counter parser. Conjunctions, numeric comparisons,
other card references, source zones, target predicates and alternative branches
remain unsupported. Every factory creates fresh card and event bindings.

Evidence: native `TestExileCounterConditionVisits`, `Timing`, `Invalid` and
`MissingFacts`; RON `TestRONExileCounterConditionGameplay`, `AllHallowsEve`,
`Invalid` and `Inventory`. The real-record tests retain All Hallow's Eve's
predicates with probe actions in place of unsupported spell exile, removal and
mass return. The resolving probe uses the original event as `TriggerA` so that
its zero predicate can run independently of the intervening guard. These tests
establish prerequisite behavior, not complete-card gameplay. The unchanged full
record still rejects at `Exile([Spell(ThisSpell)], ...)`.

## Exact exile-source counter removal

`RemoveCounterFromExiledCard(card CardRef, counter core.CounterType)
ResolvingEffect` removes one available counter of the given kind from a saved
`FromCard` exile visit. Definition validation rejects other reference kinds,
nil or unwritten bindings and invalid counter kinds. Execution requires the
saved visit to remain present and face up; private visibility alone cannot
supply a face-down source. Missing, wrong-zone, departed and returned subjects
perform no removal. Zero counters remain zero, and counts above 255 decrease
without truncation. Other kinds and the zone visit stay unchanged.

The operation uses the existing saved-card resolver, exile visit storage and
source-zone trigger frames. It makes no choices and pays no costs. Later
instructions run even when removal does nothing. Resolving predicates observe
the updated count (CR 608.2c). Departure information cannot supply a subject
(CR 400.7/400.8); movement clears counters without a removal (CR 122.2).
Copies retain the same exact visit and read its current counters; clones own
separate arrays and pending frames. Two factory instances retain separate
bindings. Ordinary intervening-if checks still run at detection and resolution
(CR 603.4). Exile cards do not phase. This resolving instruction does not add
costs, simultaneous plural removals, placement replacements or a counter-removal
trigger event. Existing permanent removal likewise has no dedicated removal
event; that event contract remains separate.

RON accepts `RemoveCounters([ACounterOfTypeFromCardInExile(counter,
