ThisExiledCard)])` in an ordinary owner-upkeep `FromExile` action body, including
nested resolving `If` bodies. It requires exactly one instruction and the
current source exile reference. Counter kinds use the existing checked parser.
Other contexts, references, amounts and lists remain errors.

Evidence: native `TestExileCounterRemovalVisits` and `Definition`; RON
`TestRONExileCounterRemovalGameplay`, `AllHallowsEve`, `Invalid` and `Inventory`.
The All Hallow's Eve test retains the actual upkeep, intervening guard, removal,
zero-counter branch and owner-graveyard movement. Only spell exile and mass
entry use probes. Two upkeeps remove two counters in order; the second moves
the card to its owner's graveyard. This proves a prerequisite, not complete-card
coverage. The unchanged full record still rejects at spell exile.

## Resolving spell exile with initial counters

`ThisSpell StackObjectRef` reads the exact resolving spell through its stack ID
and the shared resolving-reference frame. An ability, absent resolution frame,
or already departed spell supplies no subject. Current stack reads and departure
information stay separate; `spellReferenceID` retains the ID for typed LKI reads.

`ExileSpell(spell StackObjectRef) ResolvingEffect` and
`ExileSpellWithCounters(spell StackObjectRef, counter core.CounterType, count int)
ResolvingEffect` move one present spell to face-up exile. Definition checks
reject nil or unwritten references, invalid counter types and negative counts.
Saved event and target references use the existing exact stack readers. A later
cast of the same card cannot replace an earlier stack visit.

The shared stack service retains departure information. Zone storage starts a
new exile visit, then sets the fixed counter amount before tracking and the
stack-to-exile zone event. Counts remain integers, including amounts above 255.
The event uses the former spell controller; the card keeps its owner. Ordinary
cleanup and permanent entry cannot move the departed spell again. A second
instruction cannot exile its new visit. Later independent instructions continue
(CR 400.7, 608.2c, 608.2m, 608.2n, 701.13a, 122.2).

Spell copies use their own cards and visits. They are observable in exile for
the rest of resolution and cease at the next state-based check (CR 704.5e).
Ceasing creates no second zone-change event. Stack and zone clones keep separate
departure flags, exile visits and counter arrays. This contract does not add
transport of an exiled spell copy into another zone before that check.

RON lowers `Exile([Spell(ThisSpell)], [])` or one
`ExilesWithNumberCounters(Integer(n), counter)` modifier, with `n >= 0`, in a
resolving instant or sorcery body. Named counter types and literal P/T counter
pairs use the existing checked parser. Other references, plural subjects,
dynamic counts, face-down modifiers, costs, zone-source rules, replacement
bodies and delayed bodies reject before gameplay. This singular operation
makes no payment or choice. Permanent entry counter replacements do not apply
to an exile card; no general exile-card counter placement rule is added.

Tests: native `TestSpellExileResolution`, `TestSpellExileDefinition`,
`TestSpellExileSavedVisitAndObservation`, `TestSpellExileResolvingClone`; RON `TestRONSpellExileGameplay`,
`Invalid`, `FizzleAndAtomicRejection`, `Inventory`, `AllHallowsEve`, and `Recall`.
The real-record tests keep original spell exile instructions. All Hallow's Eve
also keeps its original exile-source upkeep and countdown body, with a life
probe replacing only mass graveyard entry. Recall omits only unsupported discard
and result-return instructions. These projections establish prerequisites;
neither establishes complete-card gameplay coverage or a production registry.


## Simultaneous graveyard creature entry

`PutGraveyardCreaturesOntoBattlefieldUnderOwnersControl() ResolvingEffect`
selects every present nontoken creature card from both owner graveyards at
resolution. Typed saved visits prevent returned cards from replacing selected
subjects (CR 400.7); cards added during choices cannot join the batch.
Each owner controls their entrants. Entry choices run in APNAP order, with each
owner choosing their own card order (CR 101.4, 101.4c). Shared entry preparation
supplies replacements, copy choices, counters, tapped status and attachments
(CR 614.12, 616.1). Preparation uses independent card copies with physical IDs.
Uncast entrants use zero X and cast colors; the enclosing X is restored.

All saved visits, ownership, land prohibitions and required Aura hosts are
checked after choices. Prohibited or failed entries keep their graveyard visits.
All successful cards leave their graveyards and reach the battlefield before
observations. Their continuous layers apply before departure notifications. Each owner gets one `EvtCardsLeftGraveyard` with the actual count;
entry zone events report graveyard origin and the resolving controller as actor.
Entering observers can see other entrants (CR 603.6a). Clones retain separate
zones and pending execution. No cost or announcement target is added.

RON accepts exactly
`PutEachCardFromEachPlayersGraveyardOntoTheBattlefield(IsCardtype(Creature), AnyPlayer, [EntersNormally])`
in resolving spell, activated, triggered and delayed bodies, including source-zone
triggers and conditional bodies. Other filters, player sets, entry options,
costs, static rules, entry declarations and replacement bodies reject at compilation.

`TestGraveyardBatchEntry*` proves native batch timing, APNAP choices, exact visit
rechecks, fresh counters, tapped entry, entry-copy land prohibition, failed entry,
zero X, entrant observations and grouped graveyard departure notifications.
`TestRONGraveyardBatchEntry*` proves strict loading, declaration rejection,
resolution timing, pending clones and complete unchanged All Hallow's Eve gameplay.
The complete card casts to exile with two counters, ignores opponent upkeeps,
counts down on two owner upkeeps, moves itself to its graveyard, and returns both
players' creatures together. Earlier source-counter tests retain their focused
projections and now require the complete record to compile.

## Saved event player as trigger target chooser

`TargetChosenBy(player PlayerRef) PermanentTargetOption` requires a saved event
player. Definition validation rejects nil, unbound and other player reference
kinds, repeated explicit choosers and a simultaneous opponent chooser. The option
is immutable and stores no selected player or target. At trigger placement the
shared event snapshot query resolves the chooser without changing the live
resolution frame. A missing player removes the trigger. Candidate legality still
uses the detected ability controller and source, including protection, hexproof,
shroud and phasing. A required group without legal choices is removed (CR 603.3d).

Copies retain captured event players and target visits. When new targets are
permitted, the copy controller chooses (CR 707.10c). The original event player
still supplies control restrictions; resolution uses current characteristics and
control and the exact saved target visit (CR 400.7, 608.2b). Source departure,
return, control changes or phasing after detection do not change the saved player.
Clones retain independent captured maps and target state.

RON accepts `TargetPermanentOfPlayersChoice(filter, Trigger_ThatPlayer)` in
ordinary bound step-trigger bodies, as a singular or numbered permanent target
group. `ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(Trigger_ThatPlayer))` in that target
filter uses the same per-factory step binding. Existing characteristic filters
and conjunctions compose with it. Wrong arities, tuple player substitutions,
unbound reads, other chooser references and non-step contexts reject. Other
events and chooser contexts require separate adapters.

`TestTargetEventChooser`, `Invalid` and `Conflict` prove native snapshot query,
copy and definition behavior. `TestRONEventTargetChooserAbyss` covers the complete
unchanged The Abyss record: paid casting, both upkeep players, source changes,
protection and nonartifact/control legality, exact target visits, phase cycles,
indestructibility, destruction without regeneration, copy choices and clones.
`TestRONEventTargetChooserBindingsAndStrictLoad` covers two pending upkeep events,
clone isolation and atomic rejection of invalid collections. `Invalid` covers
unbound and malformed declarations in spell and bound upkeep contexts.


## Temporary P/T switch declaration and RON execution

`SwitchPowerToughness(PermanentRef) ContinuousModification` is a unary layer
7d operation. Definition inspection checks its subject and does not expose
unused power/toughness operands. Numeric P/T operations still require both
operands. A missing switch subject remains invalid. This repairs declaration
validation; the established layer execution service is reused unchanged.

`Until` captures an exact subject visit at resolution. Layer 7b base values,
layer 7c modifiers/counters and layer 7d switches keep their order regardless of
installation order (CR 613.4b-d). Repeated layer passes produce the same result;
two switches cancel. Later bonuses and base settings use the current switch,
rather than saved P/T. Switched zero or negative toughness causes the usual
state-based action. Cleanup ends the duration and clears damage together
(CR 514.2). Phasing preserves an installed switch but prevents installation
on a phased subject. Departure and return cannot transfer the effect (CR 400.7).
Copies and clones retain separate subject visits and duration state.

RON lowers the `SwitchPT` symbol only through singular
`CreatePermanentLayerEffectUntil/3`. Existing resolving scopes, target legality,
attachment information, delayed capture and durations retain their contracts.
No static, collection, entry or payment adapter is established here.

Evidence: `TestPTSwitchDefinition` verifies valid unary declarations, invalid
subjects and continued rejection of missing numeric operands. `TestPTSwitchLayers`
checks CR 613.4d examples, base/bonus/counter order, repeated passes, two switches
and actual cleanup actions. `TestRONPTSwitchTransmutation` covers unchanged-record
paid casting, failed payment, announcement and resolution legality, control,
phasing, exact visits and duration expiry. `LayersCopiesAndClones`, `StrictLoad`,
`SourceAndHost`, `SignedPowerAndStateActions`, `TriggerAndDelay` and `Invalid`
cover independent bindings, atomic loading, attachment LKI, source departure,
returned visits, state-based actions, delayed frames and invalid declarations.


## Attached creature combat events

`AttachedAttacks`, `AttachedBlocks`, `AttachedAttacksUnblocked` and
`AttachedAttacksOrBlocks` require one named permanent binding. They detect a
present, unphased creature attached to the source at the event visit. Explicit
stale event incarnations reject. The attack/block union is one typed pattern;
`GenericTriggered.CheckEventType` asks that pattern which events it accepts.
Other existing triggers retain their event-type checks.

CR 508.1 and 509.3a/g supply attack, singular block and unblocked timing.
A multi-creature block gives one singular block trigger. Pending triggers keep
CR 603.3a controller facts and the exact captured host. Reattachment cannot
redirect the body. CR 400.7 return identity and existing phasing/reference rules
control later actions. Delayed-step capture, stack copies and game clones retain
separate frames. No damage, cost, replacement or simultaneous-move service changes.

Evidence: `TestHostCombatDefinition`, `TestHostCombatEventIdentity`,
`TestRONHostCombatIdentity`, `TestRONHostCombatNative`,
`TestRONHostCombatUnionBlocksOnce`, `TestRONHostCombatImprisonClause`,
`TestRONHostCombatDelayedAndFactories` and `TestRONHostCombatInvalid`.
The Imprison test runs its unchanged complete combat clause, including optional
payment and removal from combat. Its activation clause remains unsupported.
Farrel's Mantle's native test uses its original event and a synthetic observable
body. Its complete target/payment rule now has separate evidence in
`TestRONEventTargetExclusionMantle` and `TestRONEventTargetExclusionNativeCombat`.


## Saved activation abilities and attached tap-cost nonmana events

A completed nonmana battlefield activation now emits its stack identity in
`GameEvent.ActivatedAbilityID` after the shared payment transaction commits and
the ability is placed on the stack (CR 602.2a–b). Manual and automatic mana
activations keep that field empty (CR 605.1a, 605.3b). A targeted ability that
produces mana still uses the stack and supplies an identity (CR 605.5a). Copies
neither activate nor pay again. Failed payments and illegal tap activations
emit no completed activation and keep live resources unchanged.

`ActivatedAbilityEvent().FromAttachedPermanent().WithTapCost().NonMana()`
requires the observer's current exact attachment, the event source's matching
battlefield visit, a tap symbol in the cost, and a stack activation identity.
Host phasing and observer ability removal stop new detection. The existing
trigger service supplies APNAP placement and saves the detected controller.
`WithAbility(BindAbility(name))` saves the event identity at detection. Binding
validation rejects empty or absent declarations, repeated captures, conflicting
tap filters, repeated filters, and undominated reads.

`FromAbility` uses the existing stack-identity resolution frames through a
private storage key. It returns only a present activated ability with that exact
identity. Missing facts, spells, and departed abilities cannot supply subjects.
Empty captures replace earlier facts. Reattachment, source or host departure,
return, control changes, and phasing cannot transfer the reference to another
ability. Source LKI is not needed to counter a still-present ability.
`ControllerOfAbility` uses that ability's controller rather than its source's
current controller. `CounterAbility` uses the shared counter operation and
refunds no costs (CR 701.6a–b). Later instructions still run when the ability is
absent. Factories, pending events, stack copies, delayed bodies, and game clones
keep separate frames and saved identities. No replacement-order or simultaneous
operation contract changes.

Engine evidence: `TestActivationAbilityCaptureIdentity`, `FiltersAndRollback`,
`Definition`, `MissingAndExactEvent`, and `DelayedFrame`. RON evidence:
`TestRONHostActivationImprison`, `Combat`, `Bindings`, `Invalid`, and `StrictLoad`.
The complete Imprison record casts and attaches, offers payment at resolution,
counters the saved activation on payment, destroys its exact source when unpaid,
and preserves its separate native attack/block payment behavior. Blocking removal
also makes an attacker blocked only by that creature unblocked; damage follows
the shared combat service. RON delayed ability reads remain outside this adapter.

## Combat-bounded delayed pair subscription

`WhenCombatPairUntilEndOfCombat(PermanentRef, PermanentFilter,
*PermanentBinding, ResolvingEffect)` installs a repeating delayed ability for
one exact battlefield visit. It uses the shared filtered combat-pair matcher,
`DelayedTrigger`, event capture, saved resolution frames and stack placement.
The engine accepts typed subjects, including spell targets; the RON adapter
supports the complete permanent-source union context described below.

Creation happens at resolution (CR 603.7a). Prior events cannot trigger the new
rule. Its stated duration permits repeated matches (CR 603.7b), with one pending
body for each matching pair event. The creator's controller remains the delayed
ability's controller (CR 603.7d–e), even after source control changes. Phasing
prevents new matches but preserves the watched visit. Ability removal does not
remove an independently created delayed ability. Departure and return cannot
transfer the watch or its saved opponent to a new visit (CR 400.7, 603.7c).

Detection saves the exact opposing creature before trigger placement. Each stack
body receives its own copy of the creator's saved frame plus that event fact.
Missing, returned or phased opponents cannot receive an action; other body
instructions still run. Pending bodies survive source departure and subscription
expiry. Clones and stack copies retain separate resolution frames. The existing
LKI information services remain available for information reads; LKI cannot
restore an absent subject for actions.

`TriggerSystem.ClearEndOfCombat` runs after end-of-combat priority and before
combat reset (CR 511.2). This removes only combat-bounded subscriptions.
Turn-scoped grants created by their bodies keep their separate layer lifetimes.
Cleanup removes unused subscriptions as well. No replacement ordering, cost
rollback or simultaneous damage rule changed. Optional mana payment still uses
the shared transaction service; first strike uses native combat damage timing.

RON lowers the paired source events in `CreateTriggerUntil` with identical
creature filters, `ActionList` and symbol `UntilEndOfCombat`. It keeps the
opponent alias local to the delayed body and allocates fresh binding declarations
per factory. Host subjects, single directions and other durations reject.

Evidence: `TestCombatPairDelayIdentity`, `DurationAndEvents`, `Definition`,
`EndPriority` and `IndependentCaptures` cover identity, phasing, saved controller,
continued actions, copies, clones, pending expiry, event timing, declarations,
spell-created watches and separate captures. `TestRONCombatPairDelayFlotilla`,
`Native`, `Invalid` and `InstancesAndStrictLoad` compile the complete unchanged
Goblin Flotilla record, exercise optional payment, native combat and extra
combats, and prove factory isolation and atomic invalid collection rejection.
`TestRONTextLandwalkRecords` supplies its complete-record islandwalk evidence.

## Required variable discard count and chosen graveyard hand batch

`DiscardCountInto(binding *NumberBinding) DiscardCardResultOption` adds an actual
count result to `Discard`. Definition checks require one nonnil count binding;
count and card-result options require separate instructions. Number reads must
follow a producer. Existing card-result and no-result callers retain their paths.

The new count path uses `snapshotHandGroup`, `chooseHandDiscards` and
`discardActionsTogetherWithEvents`. It reads the requested amount once, makes
one required choice capped to the hand, and uses distinct original hand visits.
Invalid, repeated or incomplete selections use the shared mandatory fallback.
Replacements are prepared before movement. Events observe the whole discard
batch. The saved count includes completed library destinations, but excludes
cancellation and visits that leave and return. Missing players and nonpositive
amounts clear old values. Shared resolution-number frames retain counts in
copies, clones and delayed captures; no global action result is added.

`ReturnChosenGraveyardCardsToHand(graveyard PlayerRef, amount ResolutionValue,
filter CardFilter) ResolvingEffect` reads the amount once and saves the current
matching graveyard visits. The effect controller makes required distinct
choices before any move. Invalid choices use the first remaining candidate.
Empty and short graveyards supply only available cards. Newly added cards cannot
join the selection; departed and returned visits cannot supply moves. Owners
receive all actual returns before per-card zone observations and one
`EvtCardsLeftGraveyard` notification with the actual count. A destination
callback in the existing graveyard movement service supplies this timing;
public `MoveCardsFromGraveyard` callers retain their prior event timing.
The player and amount retain explicit source reads for waiting queries.

CR 701.9a–c defines discard, affected-player choice and hidden replacement
characteristics. Counts require no card characteristics. CR 608.2c–d and
609.3 define instruction order, resolving choices and short operations;
CR 400.7 defines exact zone visits. This shape has no battlefield subject,
phasing read, target announcement choice or payment rollback. Recall's existing
X payment and spell-exile services remain responsible for those contracts.

RON owns the spelling and lexical result plan. It accepts direct
`DiscardNumberCards(ValueX)` and fixed nonnegative discard amounts, the symbol
`NumCardsDiscardedThisWay` after a direct discard producer, and
`ReturnNumberCardsFromPlayersGraveyardToHand(NumCardsDiscardedThisWay, AnyCard,
player)` with existing singular player references. A later producer supplies a
fresh binding. Branch-local producers do not escape. Existing delayed captures
retain saved counts. Unbound X/counts, malformed result symbols, negative fixed
amounts, other filters/return amounts and incompatible players reject before
execution. No RON source correction or card-name branch is needed for Recall.

Engine evidence: `TestDiscardCountReturnOutcomes`, `ChoicesAndVisits`,
`Definition`, `SavedFramesAndReset`, `MandatorySelection`.
RON evidence: `TestRONDiscardCountReturnRecall`, `Invalid`, `StrictLoad`,
`InstancesAndDelayed`. Recall has complete-record native payment, X=0, short
hand, copy, clone, factory, resolving return and exile evidence. Bazaar of
Baghdad, Mindstab Thrull and Mind Bomb retain their existing discard paths.

## Turn-bounded delayed permanent damage capture

`WhenReceivesDamageThisTurn(PermanentRef, PermanentFilter, *NumberBinding,
ResolvingEffect)` saves one present, unphased battlefield incarnation during
resolution. It watches actual positive damage from matching permanent sources
until cleanup. A zero filter permits any permanent source. Recipient matching
uses both object and incarnation identity. Current recipient characteristics
and control cannot alter the saved visit. Departure and return cannot supply
it; a phase cycle preserves it. Missing or phased installation subjects do not
create subscriptions.

Detection follows shared prevention, redirection and damage batches. The final
recipient and actual amount determine each event; full prevention and zero
damage produce no trigger. Source filtering uses `damageFilterSource`, including
its exact source incarnation and LKI behavior; `DamageSourceIsAttacking` uses
current combat status or saved departure information. Spell sources cannot
match this permanent-source contract. Each simultaneous packet has its own
amount. No replacement order or damage execution path is changed.

The creator's source and controller remain captured under CR 603.7d–e. Each
matching event queues a separate pending body. Trigger placement copies its
amount into a fresh saved resolution frame. Pending bodies survive cleanup and
source or recipient departure. Stack copies use their own controllers and keep
the saved amount; game clones keep independent waiting, pending and resolving
state. `WaitingDelayedPermanentSources` includes the exact watched visit;
phasing, departure and return cannot replace it. Nested delayed installations
declare source reads without running the installation. Definition validation
requires a subject, named amount binding and body,
and checks producer dominance within an isolated delayed scope.

RON supports `CreateTriggerUntil(WhenAPermanentDealsDamageToAPermanent(filter,
SinglePermanent(ref)), ActionList(nonempty_actions), UntilEndOfTurn)` in ordinary
resolving bodies. It reuses the supported prevention source-filter adapter,
including `And([IsAttacking, IsCardtype(Creature)])`, and typed permanent refs.
`Trigger_ThatMuch` is a symbol available only in this body's value scope and
nested captured bodies. It cannot escape the body or replace unrelated event
aliases. Other subjects, durations and event forms remain rejected.

Evidence: engine `TestDelayedDamageCaptureFrames`, `Identity`, `Definition`,
`SimultaneousAndRedirection` and `WaitingSources`; RON
`TestRONDelayedDamageCaptureGlyph`, `Invalid`, `Load` and `InstancesAndNested`.
Rules: CR 120.4, 120.8, 400.7, 603.7a–e and 702.26b,d. The complete Glyph
of Life record is tested with native payment, target legality, delayed event
placement, life gain, copies, clones, prevention and expiry. Its source filter
was corrected using `data/LEG.json` Oracle text: damage must be dealt by an
attacking creature, while the chosen target must be a Wall creature.


## Next main phase and typed spell-value production

`YourMainPhase` is a `TurnStepPattern` and `DelayedStepPattern`. It matches
`EvtMainPhase` for the saved controller with either flag value. Unlike the
existing first- and postcombat-only patterns, it permits either kind of main
phase (CR 505.1 and 505.1a). `AtNext(YourMainPhase, body)` uses the existing
one-shot delayed trigger service. Creation follows resolution, earlier events
cannot trigger it, and the next actual matching boundary consumes it
(CR 603.7a–b). Skipped phases emit no event; extra main phases can satisfy it.
Cleanup does not expire it. Detection queues the body for priority rather than
executing it. The controller is the creator's resolving controller; source
phasing or departure cannot change the schedule (CR 603.7d–e). Trigger copies
use their own controller and retained value frame. Clone schedules are separate.

The RON fixed-color repeated-mana adapter now reuses
`ManaValueOfSpellWithLKI(StackObjectRef) ResolutionValue` for singular typed
spell references. Live reads use current stack information; departed reads use
retained mana values keyed by stack ID, including announced X (CR 202.3e,
608.2h). Departure information does not confer target legality or stack
membership, and a recast card has a different stack identity. Target and event
bindings remain separate per factory, pending body, copy and clone. The adapter
uses `AddManaAmount` and the existing mana replacement service; no replacement
ordering, payment transaction or simultaneous-operation contract changes.
Countering failure does not prevent a later independent instruction
(CR 608.2c). Failure of all targets prevents resolution (CR 608.2b).

Evidence: `TestNextMainPhaseTiming` runs both native main phases and checks
cleanup, opponent turns, cloning and one-shot consumption. `PendingAndController`
checks detection/placement timing, phased sources and copied trigger control;
`SkippedAndExtra` runs the turn schedule with skipped and extra main phases;
`Definitions` rejects absent bodies and unbound reads. These share the
`TestNextMainPhase` prefix. `TestRONNextMainPhase*` supplies complete Mana Drain
casting, counter outcomes, returned spell visits, colorless and colored mana,
independent pending spell values, event bindings, copies, clones, declaration
rejection, semantic inventory and atomic loader evidence. Existing
`TestSpellManaValue*` and `TestRONResolutionMana*` retain their prior contracts.

Delayed frames now save typed spell-target source facts as well as spell-event
facts. `WaitingDelayedSpellSources` and the existing waiting damage-source
choice include these exact visits (CR 609.7a). No live membership is restored.
Queries use current or stack departure information, deduplicate exact identities,
return defensive copies and make no choices or mana. Pending bodies expose the
same visits through `StackBoundSpellSources`; the reference ends when the last
body resolves or is countered. `TestNextMainPhaseSavedSpellTargets` covers live,
departed and recast spells, current color/control, defensive reads, clone
isolation, filtered source choice and waiting/stack lifetime. Complete Mana Drain
tests cover counter-before-capture, spell copies and independent cloned bodies.


## Conditional static-body composition and permanent-source prevention

`PreventDamageFromMatchingPermanentsIf(subject PermanentRef,
from PermanentFilter, condition StateCondition) StaticRule` requires a valid
condition and subject. It uses the existing static permanent-source prevention
service and shared replacement pipeline (CR 604.2, 611.3a–c, 615.1, 616.1).
The condition reads the exact source visit and its current controller at each
replacement match and waiting-reference query. False conditions supply no
waiting subject. The cycle still registers the declaration while false, so an
earlier replacement can make the condition true before a recheck. Static
conditions do not use source LKI. Damage source filters retain their existing
current, departure and phase-information rules. Phasing suspends prevention;
phase-in restores it; return cannot restore a saved cycle's source visit.
Ability removal stops the rule through the existing static cycle lifecycle.
Simultaneous damage keeps independent packets and ordinary unpreventable rules.

RON owns branch validation and declaration composition for top-level static
`If`, `Unless` and `IfElse` on permanent definitions. It combines supported
conditional attack, untap, spell-target, untap-limit, damage-redirection and
permanent-source prevention declarations with the existing conditional layers.
Each family retains its supported subjects and shapes. All branches compile,
even when inactive. Bare keywords, targets, payments, triggers, resolving actions
and unsupported protection operations remain errors. Live collection prevention
now uses the consumer contract below.
Factories create separate abilities and static registrations. No result binding
or announcement state transfers between declarations.

Evidence: `TestConditionalStaticBodyPrevention`, `Definitions`,
`WaitingAndIdentity` and `ControllerAndBatch` cover condition rechecks, invalid
bindings, current control, exact visits, attachments, phasing, clones, ability
removal, departure source facts, waiting queries, unpreventable and simultaneous
damage. All engine names share the `TestConditionalStaticBody` prefix.
`TestRONConditionalStaticBodyGameplay`, `Invalid`, `LoadAndInstances` and
`RepositoryRegression` cover native paid casting, both branch directions,
attack legality, P/T and prevention together, rejected inactive branches,
independent factories and atomic loading. Repository regression uses complete
Kird Ape, Sedge Troll, Giant Tortoise, Argothian Pixies, Desert Nomads and Uncle
Istvan records. Synthetic mixed bodies establish no new full-card coverage.

## Resolving attacking-band membership

`BandedWith(subject PermanentRef) PermanentSet` reads the current attacking band
for an exact present battlefield visit. Both the subject and selected members
must match `Combat.AttackerIncarnations`. Results use battlefield order and
include the subject when it is in a band, including a one-member band. Unbanded
attackers, missing contexts and missing subjects supply no members. Definition
validation rejects nil and unbound subjects. No LKI restores combat membership.

Formation, ability loss and removal use the existing combat service under
CR 702.22c–f. Phasing removes a member from combat under CR 702.26b. Phase-in
does not restore membership. Each game clone retains separate combat state.
Waiting delayed source traversal retains explicit source operands without
resolving the set, reading combat or executing its body.

RON resolving collections accept `BandedWith(permanentRef)` and compose it
through the shared intersection and union services. Source, target, host and
event references retain their existing binding checks. Temporary grants use
`Until(EndOfTurn, GrantEachKeyword(...))`; recipients are saved at resolution
under CR 611.2c. Later removal from combat, source departure, control changes
and phase cycles cannot change this saved set. Return cannot inherit a grant.
No new payment, replacement ordering, damage batch or event service is added.

`TestBandedSetIdentity`, `Definitions` and `Waiting` cover exact visits, stale
combat identities, singleton and absent bands, ability loss, phasing, removal,
clones, definition validation and pure waiting queries. Complete Icatian
Skirmishers RON evidence is `TestRONBandedCollectionNative`, `Pending` and
`CapturedLifetime`: paid casting, the native BandFormer path before attack
trigger resolution (CR 508.1–2), simultaneous first-strike and normal damage,
expiry and saved event identity. `TargetsAndInstances`, `Invalid` and `Load`
cover independent bindings, resolution target legality and atomic loading.
Camel's static collection-recipient prevention uses the live static consumer
contract below.

## Copiable entry variants

`ChooseCopiableVariantAsEnters(variants ...[]CopyModification) Ability` requires
one option from the entering controller. Each option must contain at least one
valid modification. The declaration requires a permanent source and a tracked
`CardDefinitionPlan`. Empty options, nil modifications and invalid keywords or
subtypes fail definition validation.

The shared `battlefieldEntryAction` replacement process applies the choice
before registration (CR 614.1c). Copy replacements have priority. Each variant
rule has a stable declaration-origin and ordinal key, so a rebuilt definition
cannot apply the same rule again in one entry event (CR 614.5). Other default
replacements share the existing affected-player order. A missing chooser or an
invalid mode answer uses the first option. Option labels show P/T, types,
subtypes and keywords; option preparation does not make game choices.

`CopySetPowerToughness(power, toughness int) CopyModification` sets copiable base
P/T. `CopyAddSubTypes(subtypes ...string) CopyModification` adds distinct subtype
names without removing existing names. `CopyAddKeywords(keywords ...core.Attr)
CopyModification` adds the supported fixed keywords. These operations preserve
existing abilities, including characteristic definitions; they do not supply a
copy exception that removes a characteristic definition. `CopyAddCardTypes`
continues to provide permanent type additions. All operations use immutable
snapshots and fresh definition builders.

The selected characteristics are copiable under CR 707.2. Counters and ordinary
layer changes are excluded. A later entry copy receives the selected values and
makes its own entry choice (CR 707.5–6). Additions from its copied definition
remain. For example, a copy of the flying variant can choose 3/3 and keep flying.
Physical identity, owner and token status follow `BuildEntryCopyWithText`.
Departure returns printed physical rules; a new visit chooses again (CR 400.7).
Control changes and phase cycles do not make choices. Independent factory
instances and game clones keep separate objects and rules.

`TestEntryVariantTimingIdentity`, `TestEntryVariantInvalid`,
`TestEntryVariantPriorityAndCopy` and `TestEntryVariantInstancesAndBatch` cover
entry timing, copy acquisition, replacement reuse, physical identity, controller
choice, snapshots, counters, layers, clone isolation, control, phasing, return,
invalid answers and pre-registration batch choices. The complete RON mapping
is `TestRONEntryVariantReal`, `TestRONEntryVariantLoad` and
`TestRONEntryVariantSpellCopy` for both Primal Clay records.

## Saved numeric entry and resolution choices

`ChooseNumberAsEnters(minimum, maximum int) AsEntersBattlefieldAbility` saves
one number on the entering permanent. Bounds must be nonnegative integers in
ascending order. The entry controller chooses before battlefield registration
(CR 614.12a). A missing player or an answer outside the bounds supplies the
minimum. Copy replacements run first; an acquired entry rule makes a fresh
choice (CR 707.5–6). Entry batches finish all choices before entry observations.

`MayChooseNumber(subject PermanentRef, minimum, maximum int) ResolvingEffect`
offers a new number to the resolving ability's saved controller. Decline keeps
the previous number. The subject must be present and unphased before the offer,
after the offer and after the number choice. The service saves and rechecks the
battlefield visit, so departure and return during a choice cannot supply it.
The service refreshes existing continuous effects after a successful change.
No cost, payment transaction, zone movement or damage operation is added.

`ChosenNumberOf(subject PermanentRef) ResolutionValue` is a pure exact-visit
information read. Current state, phase information and departure LKI use the
shared permanent information service. A missing visit or missing choice supplies
zero (CR 107.2). Reading never makes a choice. The permanent stores an integer
and a presence flag. Clones and LKI snapshots copy both fields by value. Control
changes and phasing keep the choice; return requires a new entry choice
(CR 400.7, 702.26). Chosen numbers are not copiable characteristics (CR 707.6).

RON supports one `AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent,
[ChooseANumberBetween(minimum, maximum)])` declaration. That declaration binds
`TheChosenNumber` in live static P/T values and enables
`MayAction(ChooseANumberBetween(minimum, maximum))` in resolving battlefield
source bodies. Multiple entry declarations, missing bindings, nonpermanent
entry, payment contexts, zone source bodies and granted bodies without their own
entry declaration reject during compilation. Source `PermanentLayerEffect`,
with the entry number declaration, accepts a nonempty list of separate `SetPower(value)` and `SetToughness(value)` operations,
at most one of each, using the existing static numeric values. These use layer
7b; bonuses and counters use 7c and switches use 7d (CR 613.4b–d).

`TestNumericChoiceTimingAndIdentity`, `TestNumericChoiceUpdate`,
`TestNumericChoiceInvalid`, `TestNumericChoiceCopyAndBatch` and
`TestNumericChoiceLayerOrderAndNoChoice` cover bounds, timing, controller versus
owner, decline, pending control changes, exact visit rechecks, LKI, phasing,
copy entry, batch observations, missing players, definition rejection, clone
isolation and layer ordering. Complete Shapeshifter RON tests cover all eight
numbers, failed and paid native casts, ordinary upkeep priority, decline,
updates, zero-toughness state actions, spell copies, source return, independent
factories, atomic loading and native combat damage. Its unchanged source matches
local `data/ATQ.json`; no source correction is required.

## Live static collection consumers

`PlayerControlsAny(player PlayerRef, subjects PermanentSet) StateCondition`
requires a present, unphased source of the specified visit. It resolves the typed
player and live members without choices or writes. Missing players and empty
sets cannot match. The shared set difference, union, intersection, control and
attacking-band services keep their identity and duplicate-removal contracts.

`PreventDamageFromMatchingPermanentsToSetIf(subjects PermanentSet,
from PermanentFilter, condition StateCondition) StaticRule` requires a nonnil
set and condition. Definition checks reject targets and unbound saved results in
static declarations. Each cycle registration saves the source incarnation, even
when no recipient currently matches. Each replacement match reads that source's
current controller, condition and recipients. Empty membership can later become
nonempty without a new ability. Only present recipient visits can match. Existing
permanent damage-source matching retains current, phase and departure facts;
spells cannot match. Existing prevention ordering, unpreventable damage and
simultaneous packet services apply. Waiting prevention queries use the same live
condition and membership. Clones own their game state and cycle registrations.

These contracts use CR 400.7, 615.1/615.6/615.12, 616.1f/616.2, 702.22e–g and
702.26. No new cost, timing, replacement-order or combat policy is introduced.
RON owns source spelling, declaration contexts and AST composition.

Engine evidence: `TestLiveStaticCollectionPrevention`, `Condition`, `Invalid`
and `WaitingIdentity` cover live control, phasing, source and recipient return,
ability loss, source LKI, clones, replacement rechecks, waiting references,
unpreventable damage, definition errors and simultaneous recipients.
RON evidence: `TestRONLiveStaticCollectionCamel`, `CamelChanges`,
`CamelSpellCopy`, `Condition`, `Invalid` and `LoadAndScope` cover the complete
Camel record, paid native casting, native attacking bands and combat, band
removal, source copies, factories, scope errors and atomic collection rejection.

## Voluntary entry sacrifice results

`SacrificeAnyNumberAsEnters(subjects, counted PermanentFilter) Ability` lets the
entering controller choose zero through the number of eligible permanents, then
choose that many distinct visits. The controller can sacrifice only present,
unphased subjects they control. A zero filter matches all. Invalid numeric
answers supply zero; invalid required object answers use the existing legal
fallback. All choices precede movement. Subjects must retain their visit,
control and eligibility through choices and replacements.

The ability participates in the shared entry replacement process at default
priority. Copy replacements run first; acquired entry rules make fresh choices.
Competing replacements use the affected player's choice and each entry rule
applies once. The shared sacrifice service prepares replacements in APNAP order,
orders owners' graveyard arrivals, saves counted matches before movement, and
moves the batch before observers run. Exile destinations count as completed
sacrifices. Cancellation and stale visits do not count or cause another choice.
Indestructible and regeneration do not prevent sacrifice. One entry sacrifice
declaration is permitted per definition.

`PTEqualsEntrySacrificeCount() ContinuousEffect` reads the saved count in layer
7a. Layer 6 ability removal suppresses the CDA; later restoration reads the same
saved count. Base overrides, bonuses, counters and switches retain their layer
order. `Game.CardPowerToughness` supplies zero for this CDA outside the battlefield.
`EntrySacrificeCountOf(subject PermanentRef) ResolutionValue` reads the exact
current, phase or departure result. A returned permanent cannot replace that
visit. Return, spell-copy entry and copy entry make fresh choices. Explicit
permanent cloning includes the scalar result and departure snapshots.

RON accepts one `AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent,
[SacrificeAnyNumberOfPermanents(filter)])` declaration on a permanent. Filters
use existing characteristic predicates, `IsUntapped`/`IsTapped`, and nonempty
nested `And`/`Or` groups. Land predicates accept the five basic land types
and Desert; known conflicting subtype families reject. Contextual references
and controller clauses reject;
the engine supplies the controller restriction. Optional consumers require a
creature and both `CDA_Power(value)` and `CDA_Toughness(value)` with identical
`TheNumberOfPermanentsSacrificedAsPermenantEnteredBattlefield(countFilter,
ThisPermanent)` expressions. The count filter uses supported characteristic
predicates. It is checked before simultaneous departure, independently of the
selection filter. Missing producers, duplicate axes, mismatched expressions,
other source references, multiple entry operations, costs and resolving forms
reject. The source spelling is preserved.

Evidence: native `TestEntrySacrificeBatchAndHistory`, `ChoiceRechecks`,
`Invalid`, `CountedFilterAndLayers`, `BatchEntrants`, `ReplacementOrder` and
`CopyAcquisition` and `WaitingRead`; RON `TestRONEntrySacrificeReal`, `CopiesAndReturn`, `Invalid`
and `LoadAndInventory`. Wood Elemental uses its complete LEG record for native
failed and paid casting, zero toughness, eligible Forest selection, combat,
spell copying, phasing, return, cloning and strict subset loading. Sword of the
Ages still requires activation payment results, saved power and linked exile.

Rules: CR 701.21a restricts sacrifices to the controller and separates them
from destruction. CR 614.5, 614.12a, 614.13 and 616.1 govern entry replacement
choices and once-only application. CR 208.2a and 604.3 govern the CDA and zero
when its number cannot be determined. CR 400.7 gives return a new object.

## Resolving whole-graveyard exile

`ExileGraveyardFor(PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect` resolves the player once, then
saves every card's exact current graveyard visit. The operation uses the shared
`exileGraveyardVisitsTogether(playerID, []capturedCard, sourceID)` service.
Missing, returned, wrong-zone and duplicate visits cannot move. The service
removes all eligible cards, puts all of them into face-up exile, then sends
per-card `EvtZoneChange` events and one `EvtCardsLeftGraveyard` event with the
actual count. Empty batches send no departure events. Zone observations see
the completed batch; cards added during observations cannot join it. Physical
ownership and source attribution are retained (CR 400.7, 404, 406.2–3, 603.10).
The existing single-graveyard exile payment helper uses this same service after
its existing transaction has checked its locked choices. Its choices, replacement
policy, costs and rollback contract stay with the payment subsystem.

Selection is at resolution rather than announcement. Thus Tormod's Crypt's paid
source joins a self-targeted graveyard, and cards that entered or returned before
resolution qualify as current members. Countering the ability does not refund
its sacrificed source. Copies use their own player targets without paying again.
Clones retain separate pending references and zones. This operation is exile,
not sacrifice or destruction; battlefield regeneration and phasing do not apply
to graveyard cards. No new replacement ordering or payment producer is declared.

The definition inspector checks the typed player reference and its binding
producer. The effect declares explicit source reads in that reference to waiting
delayed queries. Such queries do not read the graveyard or move cards. Source
controller information uses the existing current/LKI rules for its exact visit;
a returned source cannot replace that visit. Detection transfers the existing
saved frame to the pending body.

Evidence: `TestGraveyardBatchExileEvents` checks completed movement, face-up
visibility, source and owner facts, event attribution, one batch count and a card
added during observation. `TestGraveyardBatchExileSavedVisits` checks duplicate,
missing and returned visits plus clone isolation. `TestGraveyardBatchExileDeclaration`
checks invalid/unbound references and empty/missing players. Existing
`TestSingleGraveyardExileCost*` checks shared-service payment compatibility.
`TestRONGraveyardBatchExile*` covers native casting and activation, resolution
membership, self-target payment, countering, copies, retargeting, rollback,
phasing, delayed current/LKI reads, fresh factories, inventory and atomic loading.

## Matching permanent exile payment

`ExileMatchingPermanentCost(filter PermanentFilter, text string) Cost` requires
one matching permanent controlled by the payer, including the source. Nil
filters and empty labels fail definition validation. `CanPay` makes no choice
or mutation. A tapped creature can pay; phasing excludes it. This is a choice,
so target protections do not apply. Exile is neither destruction nor sacrifice;
indestructible and regeneration do not stop the payment (CR 118, 601.2h, 602.2b).

The shared payment transaction chooses on its isolated validation state through
the payer, locks the exact `capturedPermanent`, and checks the full payment again
before commit. Missing, phased, returned, wrong-controller or changed-filter
visits fail without spending live mana, life or tap resources. Separate exile
costs cannot reuse a departed visit. No numeric, card or historical subtype
result is exported. Definitions do not retain a locked choice from direct Pay.

The shared `exilePermanent` service keeps ownership, face-up visibility, source
attribution, departure information and zone events. Tokens leave and cause a
zone event without adding a persistent exile card. Clones keep separate zones
and pending effect frames. Countering or copying a paid ability does not refund
or repeat payment. Replacement ordering and simultaneous-operation services
keep their existing contracts; this operation chooses one subject.

`TestMatchingPermanentExileCostTransaction`, `StaleVisit`,
`SourceAndDefinition` and `QueriesAndEvents` cover these contracts. RON owns
spelling and scopes; the engine owns choices, visit identity and movement.


## Source counter-count mana

`NewSourceCounterManaAbility(color core.Color, counter core.CounterType) *ManaAbility`
declares one source tap mana ability. A typed immutable plan reads the source's
live counter array in `ManaAbility.currentProductions`. Definition validation
requires a concrete mana type and a valid permanent counter kind. The plan has
no chosen or saved game state. Queries return fresh production slices.

The ability produces one mana of that type per matching counter without removing
counters. A nonpositive count returns an empty production, because the legacy
mana production service normalizes a zero production entry to one. Missing and
phased sources supply no production; tapped status does not change what the
ability could produce. No LKI is needed: this ability resolves immediately
(CR 605.1a, 605.2, 605.3b). A returned permanent starts with new counters; a phase
cycle keeps counters. Current control determines activation and payment rights.
Cloned games query their own battlefield and mana pools.

The existing manual activation, TapForMana, automatic payment, source discovery,
replacement and mana-bonus paths share this production query. Affordability
queries do not tap, add mana, emit events or choose. Insufficient casting payments
leave resources and hand/stack state unchanged. Mana type replacement changes
the produced type before matching bonuses. A three-counter source with Mana
Flare adds four mana in total; its tapped-for-mana event reports the source's
three mana, with the bonus supplied separately by the existing service. A zero
production still permits manual activation and pays the tap cost, but emits no
tapped-for-mana event and receives no bonus (CR 106.12a).

Tests: `TestSourceCounterManaQueryAndActivation`, `TestSourceCounterManaDefinition`,
`TestSourceCounterManaPaymentAndEvents`; RON-backed complete-card payment,
replacement, rollback, ability-removal, control and cloning tests are
`TestRONSourceCounterManaCity` and `TestRONSourceCounterManaPayment`.
No new replacement ordering, zone movement, payment transaction or stack-copy
service is introduced. A mana activation cannot be copied as a stack object;
City's separate counter activation can be copied and retains its source visit.

## Saved singular graveyard-entry permanent

`ReturnCardToBattlefieldInto(card CardRef, controller PlayerRef,
result *PermanentBinding, options ...BattlefieldEntryOption) ResolvingEffect`
uses the same entry operation as `ReturnCardToBattlefield`. Existing callers
retain their signatures and event timing. The internal shared service returns
its actual prepared entrant after successful registration and entry completion;
the result is not inferred from a physical card ID lookup after movement.
The binding saves the entrant's ID and battlefield incarnation. Failed card or
controller reads, prohibited entry, and graveyard-visit changes during entry
choices clear the prior result. Definition checks require a named non-nil
binding and a producer before each read on every path.

CR 400.7j permits later parts of an effect to find the public-zone object that
the effect moved. CR 400.7 prevents a later returned object from supplying that
visit. Entry preparation and choices retain the shared CR 603.6d, 614.12 and
614.12a behavior. This result adds no replacement or simultaneous-operation
order. It introduces no payment, refund or additional cost behavior.

Existing `From` actions require the present, unphased saved incarnation.
Existing information readers can use its exact departure or phase facts.
Resolution maps, copied bodies, delayed capture and clone services keep results
separate. Waiting source queries read the saved permanent frame without entry,
choice or movement. Each lexical RON producer has its own binding; a failed
later producer cannot reuse an earlier producer's result. A branch keeps its
producer local. A delayed body retains the binding in its creation scope.

Tests: `TestReturnedPermanentEntryResult`, `TestReturnedPermanentDefinition`,
`TestReturnedPermanentEntryChoiceVisit`, `TestReturnedPermanentLKIAndWaiting`,
`TestRONReturnedPermanentGameplay`, `TestRONReturnedPermanentSavedFrames`,
`TestRONReturnedPermanentInstances`, `TestRONReturnedPermanentInvalid` and
`TestRONReturnedPermanentSourceClause`. The last test extracts Soul Exchange's
actual return clause and adds a supported tap consumer. It does not establish
complete Soul Exchange gameplay. The existing complete Resurrection and typed
return regression tests retain normal entry, owner, controller and trigger
coverage. Exile-return and graveyard Aura producers need separate adapters.

## Permanent exile payment facts

`ExileMatchingPermanentCostWithFacts(filter PermanentFilter, text string,
facts ...PermanentPaymentFact) Cost` extends the existing singular permanent
exile payment. Each fact supplies `Filter PermanentFilter` and
`Result *NumberBinding`. Definition validation requires nonzero filters,
non-nil distinct outputs, and an activation or additional casting cost context.
The original constructor retains its behavior and callers.

The shared transaction chooses and locks the exact battlefield visit. Pure
queries make no choices. After the full payment is validated, each fact matches
the chosen permanent's current characteristics immediately before exile.
Successful commit puts one or zero into the stack object's paid-number frame.
The validation clone's results are not published. An intervening characteristic
change is read again at commit; departure/return, phasing and lost control make
an ineligible locked visit fail without spending resources or publishing facts.
A phase cycle keeps the visit. CR 118.10 and 601.2h keep each payment separate;
CR 400.7 prevents a returned object from replacing a saved visit.

Payment uses the existing exile service, ownership, token departure and zone
events. No replacement ordering or simultaneous movement behavior changes.
Characteristics gained through current type effects count; printed subtypes
removed before payment do not. Historical consumers read saved facts rather
than the exiled card's printed values or a later battlefield visit. Copies keep
the original facts without paying again, and use their own controller for later
player actions. Pending stack and delayed frames remain separate in clones.

Engine evidence: `TestPermanentExileFactPayment`,
`TestPermanentExileFactDefinition`, and
`TestPermanentExileFactStaleAndCommitTime`. RON evidence:
`TestRONPermanentExileFactGameplay`, `TestRONPermanentExileFactInstances`,
`TestRONPermanentExileFactInvalid`, `TestRONPermanentExileFactFilters`, and
`TestRONPermanentExileFactSourceClause`.
The source-clause test preserves Soul Exchange's real payment, target, return
and condition and substitutes a supported tap for its counter consumer. Basal
Thrull and Grizzly Bears use their complete RON records. This establishes clause
evidence, not complete Soul Exchange gameplay.


## Distinct +2/+2 counter kind

`core.P2P2` has `String() == "+2/+2"`, `PowerBoost() == 2` and
`ToughnessBoost() == 2`. It is appended before `core.NumCounters`; previous
counter values remain unchanged. The fixed counter arrays, clone storage,
departure snapshots and shared layer calculations include it automatically.

CR 122.1a and 613.4c apply each counter in layer 7c after base values and before
7d switching. CR 122.3 and 704.5q cancel only +1/+1 and -1/-1 pairs: a +2/+2
counter remains distinct from both kinds. Existing `AddCountersTo` and
`Game.AddCountersWithReplacement` use the same replacement pipeline for the
new kind. Counter doubling changes the number of counters, not their kind.
Phasing retains them (CR 702.26); departure retains exact snapshot facts but
return starts a new object without them (CR 400.7, 122.2).

`TestP2P2CounterLifecycle` covers replacement doubling, mixed counter kinds,
removal, clone isolation, phasing and departure/return. `TestP2P2CounterLayers`
uses installed base, bonus and switch effects to verify layer order.
`TestRONP2P2CounterSoulExchange` adds complete unchanged RON gameplay with
Thrull/non-Thrull payments, payment return, illegal targets, copies, clones and
counter replacement. `TestRONP2P2CounterReplacementOrder` proves affected-player ordering and
prevention with the new kind. `TestRONP2P2CounterSoulExchangeRollback` proves incomplete
casting cannot spend the creature or available mana. Existing payment and
returned-visit contracts continue to supply identity and timing.

## Saved watched subjects in ordinary combat-pair events

The patterns returned by `BlocksCreatureMatching(PermanentRef, PermanentFilter)`,
`BecomesBlockedByCreatureMatching(PermanentRef, PermanentFilter)` and
`BlocksOrBecomesBlockedByCreatureMatching(PermanentRef, PermanentFilter)` now
accept `WithSubject(binding *PermanentBinding) filteredCombatPairPattern`.
This optional producer saves the exact watched source or attached creature at
successful detection, before trigger placement. `WithOpponent` can capture the
opposing visit at the same event. Both use the shared `eventPermanentCapture`.
Nil or unnamed bindings, repeated subject declarations and using one binding
for both subjects fail definition validation. Existing callers remain valid.

Event direction, creature checks, current characteristics and explicit event
incarnations retain the existing matcher under CR 509.3b/d/f. The watched and
opposing captures are separate typed producers. Pending events keep separate
facts, including multiple events from one Aura attached to different hosts.
Reattachment, source departure, ability removal and control changes cannot
redirect saved subjects or change the detecting controller (CR 603.3a, 608.2h).
Shared pending, stack-copy, clone and nested-delay frames preserve both facts.
Actions require the exact present, unphased visit. Information reads can use
its departure LKI. Return cannot supply the saved visit (CR 400.7); phasing keeps
identity while preventing actions (CR 702.26b). No cost, APNAP, replacement-order
or simultaneous-operation service changes.

RON owns `scope.combatSubject`, alias validation and per-factory binding
allocation. Lowering requests subject capture only when the body reads an alias;
unused subjects do not add entries to stack source queries. Existing cards keep
their previous explicit source lists. Ordinary battlefield combat-pair `TriggerA` bodies expose
`Trigger_ThatCreature` and `Trigger_ThatPermanent` for this producer. Existing
opponent aliases remain distinct. Supported nested delayed step bodies keep the
same subject. Intervening pair conditions now use the set-count adapter below.
Other event conditions, watched subjects of temporary subscriptions,
and temporary combat-rule references require their separate adapters.
New pair subscriptions clear the enclosing pair subject before body lowering.
Existing nested unblocked and death producers take precedence for their local
aliases. Position-based internal names keep these declarations separate from
the enclosing watched binding. `TestRONCombatPairSubjectNestedSubscription`
requires a positioned unbound-reference error; `NestedLocalEvent` proves local
captures do not redirect actions to the enclosing creature.

`TestCombatPairSubjectDeclarations`, `Capture` and `IndependentFacts` cover the
three directions, source/host subjects, binding errors, reattachment, source
loss, return, phasing, control, pending copies, clones, independent event frames
and departure power. These names have the prefix `TestCombatPairSubject`.
`TestRONCombatPairSubjectShapes`, `Invalid` and `AtomicLoad` verify aliases,
scope rejection, fresh declarations and atomic collection rejection.
`InfiniteAuthority` executes the complete unchanged LEG record in both native
combat directions. It checks delayed timing, saved hosts, regeneration,
indestructibility, return, phasing, changed toughness, source departure, copies,
clones and counter doubling. `Casting` covers white mana, enchant restrictions,
rollback and attachment; `IndependentEvents` covers two factory instances with
two saved host/opponent pairs each and independent destruction outcomes.
These names have the prefix `TestRONCombatPairSubject`. Existing
`TestRONCombatCharacteristicNativeClauses` supplies nonmatching toughness cases.

Infinite Authority reuses `DestroyWithResult`, `DestroyedThisWayInto`, `IfPositive`,
`AtNext`, and `AddCountersTo`. A failed destruction cannot schedule its counter
award. A successful destruction schedules the next actual end step, where the
saved first creature must still be present and unphased. The full record adds
one unique card and one compiled record; compilation and gameplay are measured
separately. No RON source defect or spelling change is needed.

## Saved-subject attack restriction during the next turn

`CantAttackDuringNextTurn(subject PermanentRef, player PlayerRef) ResolvingEffect`
requires a present, unphased subject and a valid player at resolution. It saves
that exact battlefield visit, the selected player and the installation turn.
Nil and unbound references fail definition validation. Missing runtime subjects
or players install nothing. Departure facts cannot supply an actionable subject.
Explicit source operands remain visible to waiting delayed source queries.

The installed rule starts in `BeginActiveTurn` before the saved player's next
actual turn actions. It is inactive in the installation turn and in intervening
turns. Turn selection alone does not start it. A skipped turn cannot consume it;
an extra turn can. A skipped untap cannot prevent it. Repeated turn entry and
extra upkeeps do not change its window (CR 500.7, 500.11, 611.2a).

Cleanup removes the rule in the same expiration stage as end-of-turn effects,
before state-based actions and cleanup priority (CR 514.2–3). It stays active
through the end step. It cannot restart in a later turn. The shared effect manager
owns window entry and removal. Each rule keeps its own window value; cloned
rules retain separate window state.

The shared attack-rule service checks the saved visit at attack declaration.
The restriction is separate from abilities and cannot remove an attacker already
in combat. Source departure, phasing or ability loss cannot end a resolved rule.
The subject's control changes do not redirect the saved player. Subject phasing
prevents actions but keeps an installed rule; return creates a different visit.
A subject phased out before resolution cannot receive the rule (CR 611.2a–c).
No new payment or replacement service is introduced.

RON lowers `CreatePermanentRuleEffectUntil(subject, [CantAttack],
DuringPlayersNextTurn(player))` in resolving action bodies. Existing typed
permanent and player references supply the operands, including combat-pair
`Trigger_ThatOtherPermanent` and its resolution-time controller. The operation
must be one symbol. Wrong arity, unbound references, mixed operation lists and
other durations remain compilation errors. Other operations with this duration,
static declarations, entry and payment contexts gain no adapter.

`TestNextTurnAttackWindow*` supplies engine contract evidence for lifetimes,
skipped and extra turns, independent players, declarations, source loss, control,
return, phasing, waiting departure information and clone isolation.
`TestRONNextTurnAttackWindow*` maps the complete unchanged Wall of Dust record
to native blocking/damage/attack legality, printed casting costs and rollback,
identity changes before and after resolution, stack copies, pending clones,
independent factories and pending events, strict atomic loading, invalid syntax
and inventory roles. Synthetic resolving source, host and target consumers
retain the same typed reference services. Compilation and full-card gameplay
each gain Wall of Dust, one unique name and one record.

## Intervening combat-pair set conditions

`PermanentSetCountAtLeast(PermanentSet, int) StateCondition` checks a fixed
nonnegative minimum; `PermanentSetIsEmpty(PermanentSet) StateCondition` checks
zero members. Definition validation rejects absent sets, negative minima and
unbound saved operands. Typed sets retain their own identity, membership and
phasing contracts. Set difference excludes an exact present visit; current
characteristics supply property filters. There is no LKI combat membership.

`WithInterveningIf` now supplies detected permanent facts alongside player/card
facts. The condition query uses a shallow game view with a separate permanent
binding frame. It cannot overwrite or inherit another resolving event's frame.
Pending/copy resolution passes its own permanent facts to `IfState`. The shared
event service supplies source and opposing visits before trigger placement.
CR 603.4 requires checks at detection and resolution. CR 509.1g–i and 509.2a require
the complete declared blocker set before detection. CR 400.7 and 702.26 retain
existing departure and phasing boundaries. Return cannot supply a saved attacker;
new current blockers can satisfy a live count after a successful detection.
Source departure does not cancel the pending condition. Actions still require
the saved source visit. Phase cycles remove combat membership.

RON supports ordinary battlefield combat-pair `TriggerI` with fixed
GreaterThanOrEqualTo counts, absence leaves, and nonempty And/Or conditions.
Property collections accept supported property filters, And/Or, and Other with
a typed source/host/event reference. Other contexts remain separate adapters.
The existing temporary keyword service applies Banding through cleanup.
Payments, APNAP ordering, replacement ordering and simultaneous movements keep
their existing contracts; this slice introduces no new payment or movement.
Waiting delayed source inspection includes explicit operands of these conditions
without evaluating membership or granting an actionable departure subject.

Evidence: `TestPermanentSetConditionIntervening`, `Declarations`, `QueryFrame`
and `WaitingSource` cover saved event facts, minimum/empty boundaries, invalid
operands, live membership changes, exact visits, phasing, source departure,
copies, clone isolation and pure queries. `IndependentEvents` checks two
pending events from one source against separate current combat groups.
`TestRONCombatPairConditionNative`
covers complete Wall of Caltrops, native blockers, printed Defender/P/T, untargeted
shrouded attackers, required other Walls, excluded non-Walls, combat damage and
cleanup expiry. `Rechecks` covers detection/resolution changes, departure before
placement, returned attackers/blockers/source, phasing, control, ability loss,
copies and pending clones. `IndependentInstances` keeps separate event and
factory bindings. `DirectionsAndHost` covers both directions, union, nested
conditions and attachment changes. `Invalid` and `CastingLoadAndInventory` cover
source diagnostics, typed scopes, printed casting payment/rollback, factory
validation, strict reprint loading and atomic rejection, and semantic roles.

## Optional bounded library search with public reveal

`MaySearchLibraryToHand(player PlayerRef, maximum int, filter CardFilter)
ResolvingEffect` offers one optional search at resolution. Decline makes no
card choice, reveal, move or shuffle. Acceptance permits zero through maximum
matching cards (CR 701.23b). Acceptance shuffles once even with a zero bound,
an empty library or no matching cards. A missing player has no effect.
Definition validation rejects negative maxima, nil and unbound player refs.

The player chooses distinct cards from matching library visits saved after
acceptance. All choices precede movement. Nil, foreign or duplicate choices
end selection. The canonical library card supplies the result; a forged card
with an offered ID cannot change its characteristics. Every chosen visit is
checked again before movement. Departure and return cannot replace a selected
visit or join the initial search. Found cards are publicly revealed before
movement (CR 701.20, 701.23e). All cards move to their owners' hands before
individual library-to-hand zone events. The search then shuffles (CR 608.2c).
It does not draw, play lands, or make a casting payment.

The typed player operand declares explicit source reads to waiting delayed
queries. Queries make no choices or moves. Source departure keeps exact LKI
controller information for a declared controller reference. Copied abilities
use their own resolving controller; cloned libraries, visits and public reveal
history remain separate. SearchPlayer accepts the beneficial library-search
prompt so native AI simulations execute the action.

RON supports this service only for resolving
`MayAction(SearchLibrary([FindNumberCardsOfType(Integer(n),
And([IsSupertype(Basic), IsCardtype(Land)])), RevealFoundCards,
PutFoundCardsIntoHand, Shuffle]))`, with n >= 0. The two filter leaves may
appear in either order. Activation, spell, trigger and explicit PlayerActions
bodies use their existing player frames. Entry, cost, dynamic bounds, other
filters, destinations and retained search-result bindings need separate
adapters. Existing single-card search APIs and adapters remain unchanged.

Evidence: `TestBoundedLibrarySearchChoices`, `Visits`,
`DeclarationsAndEmpty`, `WaitingAndClone`, `NoMatchAndAbsent` and
`SimulationChoice`; `TestRONBoundedLibrarySearchLandTax`, `Lifecycle`,
`Invalid`, `Inventory`, `Load` and `ResolvingContexts`.
Land Tax uses its complete unchanged LEG record, including printed W payment,
rollback, own upkeep, detection and resolution land-count checks, phasing,
source departure/return/control/ability loss, independent instances and copies.
No search replacement or simultaneous multi-player search contract is added.

## Bounded entry life payment and saved P/T

`PayLifeUpToAsEnters(maximum ResolutionValue) Ability` reads the cap when its
entry replacement applies. The entering controller chooses zero through the
smaller of the nonnegative cap and available life. Zero remains legal with
nonpositive life. Invalid answers use zero. The shared life-cost transaction
checks the chosen payment before commit; failure saves zero and spends nothing.
Successful payment stores its amount on this permanent visit and uses the shared
life-loss event service. A later cancelled entry does not refund an earlier
payment; a cancellation before this replacement makes no payment or choice.

The rule participates once in the shared entry replacement process at default
priority. Copy replacements run first, including newly acquired payment rules.
Competing entry replacements use the affected player's order. Batch entry keeps
all entrants and payments complete before battlefield entry observers run.
Casting affordability and announcement do not choose or pay this entry cost.
Missing entry controllers save zero. One life producer is permitted per definition.

`PTEqualsEntryLifePaid() ContinuousEffect` applies the saved value in layer 7a.
Layer 6 ability removal suppresses this CDA; restoration reads the saved payment.
Later base P/T effects, bonuses, counters and switches keep their existing order.
`Game.CardPowerToughness` supplies zero outside the battlefield.
`EntryLifePaidOf(subject PermanentRef) ResolutionValue` reads the current,
phased or departed exact visit. Return requires a new payment and cannot replace
the former result. Factory instances, spell copies and entry copies make separate
payments; game clones and departure snapshots keep separate scalar results.
ZoneSystem clones also copy the in-progress entering permanent, so a clone made
during a choice cannot change the original entry result or later inherit its payment.
Waiting delayed queries retain explicit source subjects without evaluation or choice.

`CountGraveyardCardsAmong(players PlayerSet, filter CardFilter) ResolutionValue`
counts current matching cards in distinct existing selected players' graveyards.
Missing players contribute nothing. Typed player-set operands retain explicit
source reads in waiting queries. Existing singular `CountGraveyardCards` callers
keep their behavior. This adds a query, without a new graveyard movement service.

RON accepts one `AsPermanentEnters(ThisPermanent,
[PayAnyAmountOfLifeUpto(maximum)])` operation on a permanent. Optional paired
`CDA_Power(TheLifePaid)` and `CDA_Toughness(TheLifePaid)` require a creature and
this producer. Results are local to this source visit; they do not supply an
activation, resolving, target, host, granted or delayed RON result binding.
The cap accepts nonnegative `Integer`, recursive `Plus`, supported static
battlefield count filters, and `TheNumberOfGraveyardCards(And([cardFilter,
InAPlayersGraveyard(player)]))`. The graveyard operands can be reversed. Players
are `Opponent` or `SinglePlayer(You)`; card filters use supported characteristic
`IsCardtype`/`IsNonCardtype`, `IsColor`/`IsNonColor` and nonempty `And`/`Or` groups.
Malformed, unbound, duplicate and mixed entry declarations reject at compilation.

The sole Nameless Race record previously used `PermanentLayerEffect` with
`SetPowerAndToughnessBoth(TheLifePaid)`. Local `data/DRK.json` defines its printed
P/T ability as characteristic-defining under CR 604.3a, 208.2a and 613.4a.
The source now uses paired CDA declarations. CR 119.4/b supplies payment bounds;
614.1c, 614.5, 614.12/a and 616.1 supply entry replacement timing and order.

Evidence: `TestEntryLife*` covers legal/invalid bounds, zero and exact life,
rechecks, definition rejection, layer order, lifecycle/LKI, entry copies, waiting
reads, clones, batch entry, competing replacement order, cancellation and live
life-loss events. `TestRONEntryLife*` covers the complete corrected Nameless Race
record, casting rollback, dynamic white nontoken/opponent/graveyard cap, zero
P/T state actions, trample metadata, native combat, copied spells, pending clones,
return, control changes, phasing, strict loading, inventory and invalid contexts.

## Spell-source target facts and static prevention

`DamageSource.TargetsPermanent(permanent *Permanent) bool` reads the permanent
visits announced as targets of that exact spell. `CaptureSpellDamageSource`
saves these facts from the live stack object. `CaptureDamageSource` saves them
from the spell's resolution frame after stack departure. Missing stack identity,
abilities, UUID-only targets and returned visits cannot match. Target legality
does not erase announced references: a spell with another legal target can
still deal untargeted damage while its original permanent target is illegal.
Phasing keeps the target identity, but static subjects must be present.
Copies use their own stack identities and target lists. Saved source bindings,
resolution frames and game clones keep separate target arrays. Snapshot facts
survive spell departure and cannot follow a later cast (CR 400.7, 608.2b, 707.10).

`PreventDamageFromSpellsTargeting(subject PermanentRef) StaticRule` prevents
noncombat damage from spells that target the current subject.
`PreventDamageFromSpellsTargetingIf(subject PermanentRef,
condition StateCondition) StaticRule` requires a valid live condition.
`This` uses the source visit; `AttachedPermanent` uses an Aura's current host.
Nil subjects, undeclared target bindings and nil conditions fail validation.
The existing static lifecycle supplies ability removal, phasing, source visits,
current controller checks and pure waiting-reference queries. Conditions and
subjects are checked again after each replacement. Repeated events have no
shield limit. Unrelated recipients, permanent-source abilities and combat do
not match. Simultaneous packets, redirection and unpreventable damage retain
the shared replacement process (CR 120.1, 120.2b, 611.3, 615.1, 615.12, 616.1).

Prepared permanent damage actions now retain their recipient visit through
replacement rechecks and amount copies. Execution cannot damage a returned
visit. Existing UUID-only action constructors retain their legacy interface;
new actions made by redirection retain the existing redirect services.

RON accepts source-only static
`PreventDamage(DamageWouldBeDealtByASpellToRecipient(
TargetsPermanent(ThisPermanent), Permanent(ThisPermanent)), [PreventThatDamage])`,
including supported static If/Unless/IfElse bodies. It requires exactly one
prevention operation. Host, event, resolving, payment, other filters and other
recipient contexts reject. Spell/ability causation remains a separate contract:
a spell that makes a permanent deal damage does not make that permanent a spell
source. Silhouette uses the separate targeting-cause contract below.

Evidence: engine `TestSpellTargetDamageFacts`, `Prevention`, `Invalid`,
`CopySnapshots`, `Recheck`, `HostAndWaiting`; RON
`TestRONSpellTargetDamageBronzeHorse`, `Lifecycle`, `IllegalTargetFacts`,
`Combat`, `ActivatedAbility`, `Invalid`. Bronze Horse uses its complete unchanged repository record.
Its casting payment, 4/4 artifact creature metadata, trample and full conditional
prevention have gameplay evidence. Synthetic fixtures test the reusable service;
Silhouette gameplay evidence is in the targeting-cause contract below.

## RON indefinite singular control

`Until(core.Indefinite, ChangeController(subject PermanentRef, controller PlayerRef))`
now passes definition validation. Existing layer capture saves the subject's exact
battlefield visit and the selected controller at resolution. A missing player or
phased/departed subject installs no effect. Highest-life ties select no player.
Later life changes cannot change the saved controller. Source departure, source
control, ability loss and cleanup do not end this effect. Subject phasing retains
it; departure and return cannot inherit it. Layer 2 timestamps let later control
effects override it; removal of a temporary override restores it. Copies and game
clones retain separate resolution frames and effects. Unsupported control
durations and source-bound lifetime forms retain their existing validation.
This follows CR 611.2a–c, 613.1b, 613.7, 400.7 and 702.26.

RON accepts `CreatePermanentLayerEffect(subject, [SetController(player)])` with
one modification, or `GainControlOfPermanent(subject)` in ordinary resolving
bodies. The latter uses the scoped action player (default You). Permanent and
player references use the existing typed scope rules. The symbol
`ThePlayerWithTheMostLife` lowers to `PlayerWithUniqueHighestLife()` and is read
at resolution. Entry and draw-replacement control bodies reject. Static control,
plural control and source-bound durations retain their separate adapters.

A source-tap activation with exactly `AddMana(singleManaSymbol)` followed by
`CreateFutureTrigger(...)` uses `NewManaAbility(color, afterProduction...)` when
the symbol produces one mana. This retains automatic-payment color metadata and
runs the delayed producer immediately after production. Future bodies use their
existing declaration checks and per-instance bindings. Queries do not schedule
triggers or choose players. Failed payment planning does not tap the source or
install a delay. ManaAbility follow-up effects now pass definition validation,
including binding checks; they no longer bypass the definition walk.

Engine evidence: `TestIndefiniteControl`, `Declaration` and
`ManaFollowupValidation`. RON evidence: `TestRONIndefiniteControlOgre`,
`OgreNewController`, `RainbowVale`, `RainbowPayment`, `Invalid` and
`InventoryAndLoad`. Complete unchanged Ghazbán Ogre and Rainbow Vale records
supply gameplay evidence independently of compilation counts.


## Beginning-of-turn untapped history

`Game.BeginActiveTurn()` captures untapped status by exact battlefield visit and
untapped land counts by controller once per turn and active player. Capture
