follows beginning-of-turn duration expiry and a layer update. It precedes all
phasing and untapping. Phased-out permanents supply no facts (CR 702.26b).
Both players' land counts use their characteristics and control at capture.
The same boundary runs when untap is skipped. Drivers check skipped turns before
calling it; a skipped turn has no capture (CR 500.11). Extra turns capture again.
Direct untap execution also enters this shared boundary.

`UntappedLandCountAtTurnStart(PlayerRef) ResolutionValue` resolves the selected
player in the current frame and reads the saved count. `Game.UntappedLandsAtTurnStart`
keeps its signature; uncaptured turns return zero. `Game.StartedTurnUntapped(id,
incarnation uuid.UUID) bool` reads an exact saved visit. `TrackerReader` exposes
that pure query. `PermanentStartedTurnUntapped(PermanentRef) StateCondition`
accepts only `This`; definition validation rejects other subjects. Detection
uses the present visit. Resolution uses the saved source incarnation, including
a departed or phased source. Departure information is unnecessary because the
historical fact already has an exact visit. A new visit has no fact until the
next turn. This historical check does not permit actions on an absent, phased
or returned source (CR 400.7, 603.4, 608.2a).

Later tap, type, control and zone changes cannot change these facts. Repeated
boundaries and extra upkeep steps do not recapture. Clones copy both the counts
and the visit map. Queries do not capture or alter history. Cleanup does not
recapture; the next actual turn replaces the facts. Existing tracker setters
and Go callers remain available.

Evidence: engine `TestTurnStartUntappedFacts`, `SkippedUntap`, `Definition` and
`HistoricalTrigger`; RON `TestRONTurnStartUntappedPowerSurge`, `Intervening`,
`Invalid` and `InventoryAndLoad`. Power Surge has full-record gameplay evidence.
Rasputin's complete record now exercises entry, both counter payments, mana,
finite prevention and the history trigger with its source counter-cap rule.


## Source counter caps

`SourceCounterCap(core.CounterType, int) ContinuousEffect` declares a cap in
one source static ability. Definition validation rejects negative bounds and
invalid counter kinds. Current runtime abilities supply the cap; shared layer
ability removal and restoration therefore end and restore it. Cloned definitions
and games retain separate ability and counter state.

`Game.AddCountersWithReplacement`, entry counter placement (including extra
counter types), and `Game.AddCountersTogether` limit the final counter amount
after the existing affected-player replacement choices (CR 101.2, 122.6, 616.1).
The cap does not take part in those choices. The lowest cap for that type wins.
Other types are unaffected. Saved absent, phased or returned visits cannot use
the single placement service. Batch placements retain their existing distinct
visit checks and simultaneous preparation.

At the existing state-based boundary, excess counters on an unphased permanent
with a current cap are removed (CR 704.5r). This handles a gained or restored
ability and a copied definition. Layer application itself does not remove
counters. Phasing retains counters and suspends this check (CR 702.26b).
Entry and return use the new object's own abilities and counters (CR 400.7).
Low-level `Permanent.AddCounter` remains a bypass; state-based checks still
remove excess counters once a live cap applies.

Engine evidence: `TestSourceCounterCap`, `Definition`, `BatchAndMultipleRules`
and `StateBased`. Complete Rasputin RON evidence and rejection cases are mapped
in the API reference. No source-data correction or registry cutover is included.

## Static filtered tapped entry

`EntersTappedFor(players PlayerSet, filter PermanentFilter) Ability` attaches
one live static entry replacement. Definition validation requires a typed player
set and a permanent source. The filter's zero value matches every permanent.
Current runtime abilities supply the rule before the proposed entry. Phasing,
face-down status, source departure and ability removal suspend its availability.
Restoration and return use the current source's ability and controller. The
source's current controller supplies `You`; ownership does not select recipients.

Candidates join the shared `battlefieldEntryAction` replacement pipeline at
`ReplacementPriorityDefault`. The affected entrant's controller chooses between
competing replacements. Copy replacements apply first. Each source visit and
ability ID supplies a stable per-event identity, so an applied rule cannot repeat
when candidates are rebuilt. Replacement execution rechecks the source after a
player choice. Multiple sources retain separate identities and factory instances.
There is no saved global entry result, entry trigger, or registration-only rule.

Matching reads a separate game layer projection of the proposed entrant. This
keeps copy-modified characteristics, existing continuous effects and source-only
composed static modifications of the entrant. The entrant's general static
abilities cannot supply a new global effect before entry. The projection does
not publish a live entrant, perform an entry choice, fire events, run state-based
actions, or change the live board, life totals or stack. The supported RON filter
reads card types and the projected controller. Other entry-state query families
require their own adapters and evidence. Self-only legacy callback effects do
not have a typed subject contract and are not added as new projected effects.

The replacement sets the proposed permanent's tapped state before registration
and entry observations. It emits no tap event. Token batches still prepare every
entrant before registration and observations. Copies and game clones retain
separate controller frames, candidates and layer state. This rule consumes no
cost or resolution result; Kismet casting uses the existing rollback service.

CR 614.1d, 614.4, 614.5, 614.12 and 616.1 establish timing, availability,
characteristic matching, one application per event, and affected-player order.
Local `data/LEG.json` confirms Kismet's complete Oracle text. No source correction
is needed. Land Equilibrium uses the retained entry sequence described below.

Evidence: native `TestFilteredEntryLifecycle`, `Definition`, `Characteristics`,
`CopyAndBatch`, `ReplacementOrder`, `ChoiceRecheck` and
`LiveControlAndProjectionPurity`; RON `TestRONFilteredEntryKismet`,
`CopiedKismet`, `Invalid` and `InventoryAndAtomicLoad`.


## Retained entry and mandatory sacrifice

`PutThenSacrificeFor(players PlayerSet, entrant, counted PermanentFilter,
minimum ResolutionValue) Ability` adds a live static replacement from a
permanent source. Definition validation requires a player set, a count value
and a permanent source. The zero filter matches any permanent. RON supplies
only typed card-type filters and a source-controller permanent count.

The actor is the player who puts the proposed permanent onto the battlefield.
Entry preparation now carries this actor through direct entry, graveyard and
exile returns, and simultaneous returns. The existing controller is the default
when the caller has no separate actor. Explicit actors can differ from entry
controllers. This field does not replace entry event `ActorID` or controller
bindings.

Matching reads the actor's present, unphased controlled permanents before entry,
and compares that count with the live value in the source's controller frame.
The proposed entrant is excluded. Entrant types use the existing isolated layer
projection, after higher-priority copy replacements. Source phasing, face-down
status, departure and ability removal suspend the rule. Each source visit and
ability ID has one application per proposed event. A selected replacement
rechecks its source and predicate after competing replacement choices.

Application saves the actor and sacrifice filter on that exact proposed entrant.
This is an event continuation, not an ETB trigger or persistent linked ability.
Cancelled entry never executes it. Successful entry publishes its entry event,
then completes the required sacrifice before the entry service returns. Batch
entry registers every entrant and publishes every entry observation before any
saved sacrifice. All matching decisions use the pre-entry battlefield. Nested
retained entries finish their saved operations in reverse replacement order
(CR 616.1g). Source departure after application does not erase an instruction.
Copies and clones have separate proposed objects and continuation slices.

`SacrificeChosenBy(You, You, MatchingPermanents(filter))` runs in a separate
actor frame through `ApplyEffect`. It uses existing required choice, exact visit,
control, phasing, sacrifice replacement, ownership and zone-event services. The
actor can choose the entrant after entry. A departed and returned choice cannot
replace the saved visit. A single candidate needs no decision callback. No
resolution result leaks into the caller's frame. Unavailable sacrifices have no
effect. This is not an entry payment or an additional cost.

Rules evidence: CR 614.1a, 614.4–7, 614.12, 616.1 and 616.1g, 701.21a.
Local `data/LEG.json` supplies Land Equilibrium's complete Oracle text. The
unchanged RON record matches the pre-entry count and retained-entry sequence.
No source defect was found in this slice.

Native evidence: `TestRetainedEntryCountsAndActor`,
`LifecycleAndSavedSequence`, `BatchAndEvents`, `Definition`, `ActorAndVisit`,
`CancellationAndRecheck`, `CopyPriorityAndNestedOrder`,
`PendingCloneAndReturn`, `BatchUsesOriginalCount`,
`PhasedEntrantKeepsSequence`, and `ReturnActors`.
RON evidence: `TestRONRetainedEntryLandEquilibrium`, `CopiedSpell`, `Invalid`,
and `FactoryAndAtomicLoad`. These tests cover the complete Land Equilibrium
record. Other retained operations and player predicates remain unsupported.

## Combat declaration cardinality

`LimitAttackDeclarations(int) StaticRule` and `LimitBlockDeclarations(int)
StaticRule` restrict declarations while their battlefield source ability is
active. Limits must be nonnegative; zero permits no declarations. Multiple
sources use the lowest limit. Phasing, departure and ability removal stop the
rule. A returned source registers a new ability; copied and cloned sources keep
independent source visits. The queries read active shared continuous effects.
There is no second cached rule registry.

Both native and explicit declaration paths obey the limits (CR 508.1c/d,
509.1b/c). Attack selection maximizes independent printed and resolved attack
requirements within the cap, with stable proposal preference on ties. Creature
control, type, tap status, summoning sickness, source restrictions and Island
Sanctuary remain legality checks. Omitted creatures with attack costs are not
forced to pay. Selected creatures still use the shared payment and post-payment
identity checks. Uncapped callers retain their existing behavior.

The shared blocker search bounds selected creature rows, rather than blocking
pairs. One creature can block several attackers or all members of an attacking
band within one slot. Evasion, capacity and minimum blocker requirements remain
mandatory. The search maximizes requirements within the cap. Existing pairs
remain fixed and their distinct blockers reserve slots for additional proposed
assignments. Neither limit removes creatures already in combat or changes the
services that put a creature into combat without a declaration.

Evidence: `TestCombatCardinalityRequirements`, `BothDeclarationPaths`,
`DistinctBlockersAndRequirements`, `AttackWeightsAndCosts`, `AttackLegality`,
`LifecycleAndMinimum`, `Definition`, and `BlockingExhaustive`. The exhaustive
oracle checks 96 matrices with no limit and with limits zero through four.
`TestRONCombatCardinalityCaverns` covers the complete unchanged RON card with
2RR casting, unpaid rollback, source lifecycle, pending spell copy and game
clone. RON factory, inventory and atomic loading have separate tests. LKI and
replacement order add no new contract in this slice.

## Plural activation sacrifice payment

`SacrificeAnyMatchingCostInto(filter PermanentFilter, text string,
power *NumberBinding, cards *CardsBinding) Cost` permits zero or more distinct
matching permanents controlled by the payer. The source can pay if it matches.
Queries make no choices. Declaration validation requires a filter, text, named
results and separate producers. This result-bearing declaration is supported
as an activated ability cost; resolving and casting declarations reject.

The shared payment transaction makes the count and subject choices on its
validation game, using the live payer's decision interface. Invalid counts or
subjects fail. Locked choices retain exact battlefield visits. Commit checks the
complete payment on a separate game before spending live resources. Phasing,
changed control, changed membership and return cannot substitute payment subjects.

The shared sacrifice batch prepares replacements in active-player order and
lets owners order graveyard arrivals before any movement. All moves precede
zone and sacrifice observations; departure conditions retain the former
battlefield. Each successful move saves its new public-zone visit before these
observations. Tokens contribute their payment-time power but supply no card.
Power is read after replacement and graveyard-order choices, before any subject
leaves. Negative power remains negative. Replacement exile destinations count as paid.
Cancellation makes the complete payment fail, with no live partial payment.

The transaction publishes `NumberBinding` and `CardsBinding` results only on
success. Existing stack, copy, clone and delayed frames carry these results.
`FromCards` requires the saved current zone visit; departure and return cannot
restore an earlier card result. Zero choices publish zero and an empty set.

Rules: CR 601.2h, 602.2b, 701.21a and 400.7j. Native evidence:
`TestPluralSacrificeCostResults`, `TestPluralSacrificeCostRollback`,
`TestPluralSacrificeCostDefinition`, `TestPluralSacrificeCostStackFrames`,
`TestPluralSacrificeCostReplacementBatch`, `TestPluralSacrificeCostCancellation`
`TestPluralSacrificeCostDelayedAndFailureIsolation` and
`TestPluralSacrificeCostPowerAfterReplacementChoices`.

## Combined source and optional-subset sacrifice payment

`SacrificeSourceAndAnyMatchingCostInto(filter PermanentFilter, text string,
power *NumberBinding, cards *CardsBinding, source *CardBinding) Cost` pays one
mandatory source and zero or more distinct matching permanents controlled by the
payer in one simultaneous sacrifice batch. The source need not match the filter
and cannot enter the optional subset. The source's power and card visit remain
separate from the optional-subset results. All three result declarations must
have names and separate producers. This contract applies to activated costs;
spell additional costs and resolving payment groups reject.

The shared transaction locks the mandatory source visit before mana payment.
The payer chooses the optional count and subjects while the source is present.
The same source and subset visits must remain present, unphased and controlled
by the payer for payment. Invalid counts, duplicate/source choices, returned
visits, changed control and cancelled sacrifices fail the complete transaction
without live resource expenditure or result publication.

The shared sacrifice service prepares replacement and graveyard-order choices
before movement. Optional power is read from the complete battlefield after
those choices. All members leave before any departure observation; LKI contains
all members. The source's resulting public-zone visit is saved in the separate
card binding before observations. Each optional nontoken card supplies its own
new visit. Tokens add optional power but supply no card; a token source supplies
an empty source card result. Indestructible and regeneration do not stop
sacrifice. Exile replacements keep successful payment and save exile visits.
Zero optional choices still sacrifice the source, with zero power and an empty
optional card set.

Payment publishes the number, card-set and source-card results through existing
stack frames. Copies do not pay again. Clones and delayed bodies retain separate
frames. Later activations, changed characteristics and returned cards cannot
replace previous results. Existing `FromNumber`, `FromCards` and `FromCard`
consumers keep their exact visit contracts.

Rules: CR 601.2h, 602.2b, 701.21a, 400.7j and 608.2h. Native evidence:
`TestSourcePluralSacrificeCostBatch`, `Observations`, `Rollback`, `Definition`,
`ReplacementAndTokens`, `Frames` and `DuplicateSourceResult` with the same
`TestSourcePluralSacrificeCost` prefix. These tests also exercise a source's
static power bonus, separate owners, animated source exclusion from the optional
subset, nonactive-player activation, saved visits, cancellation of either group,
replacements, source/subject return and phasing, stack copies and game clones.
RON evidence and the complete-card boundary are documented in dsl-reference.md.

## Saved graveyard-card exile groups

`SingletonCard(card CardRef) CardSet` adapts a typed singular card reference.
`ExileGraveyardCards(subjects ...CardSet) ResolvingEffect` selects the valid
current card references, retains only graveyard visits, and uses one shared
movement batch across all owners. All selected cards move to face-up exile
before any zone event. Duplicate groups move a card once. Each affected
player's graveyard departure event contains that player's completed count.
Cards added by event observations cannot enter the saved batch. Attribution
uses the resolving source. Ownership stays unchanged.

Existing `ExileGraveyardFor` and its payment callers use the same movement
service while retaining their explicit single-player boundary. Saved references
cannot follow departure and return. Saved exile visits have no graveyard move.
Definition validation rejects missing subjects, nil references and unbound
results. The effect has no choices and creates no new result storage.

RON lowers optional sacrifice power through the existing NumberBinding and
saved card groups through CardsBinding. A separately paid source uses
CardBinding. Costs save these facts before observations; resolution, copies,
clones and delayed bodies use their own existing frames. The mandatory source
never adds power to the optional group. Tokens add power but supply no cards.

Rules: CR 400.7j permits an effect to find its payment's first public-zone
objects; CR 400.7 ends that identity on later movement. CR 608.2b stops the
entire instruction when its only target is illegal. CR 608.2c and 608.2f require
ordered instructions and simultaneous plural movement. CR 608.2h–i supplies
source LKI and saved information about the prior sacrifice.

Evidence: `TestSavedGraveyardExileBatch`, `Definition`,
`PaymentReplacement`; RON `TestRONPluralSacrificeResultSword`,
`IdentityAndLegality`, `Frames`, `Invalid`. Existing graveyard-batch and plural
payment suites retain rollback, phasing, replacement ordering and simultaneous
sacrifice LKI coverage.

## Repeated resolving mana payment

`IfRepeatedManaPaid(player PlayerRef, cost ManaCost, count ResolutionValue,
body ResolvingEffect)`, `UnlessRepeatedManaPaid` and
`PayRepeatedManaOrElse(player PlayerRef, cost ManaCost, count ResolutionValue,
paid ResolvingEffect, unpaid ResolvingEffect)` repeat a fixed generic/colored
mana cost. Validation rejects X, hybrid symbols, negative components, missing
operands and unbound typed references. Existing X payment APIs retain their
contracts. Each component is multiplied by the count read once before payment
choices or mana abilities. Nonpositive dynamic counts supply zero; payment
still requires acknowledgment. Arithmetic overflow returns an error before
choices or movement. An absent payer runs neither continuation.

The existing `unlessPaidEffect`, mana solver and total-cost transaction own
payment, spending policies, mana abilities and rollback. Spell/activation cost
modifiers do not alter this resolution payment. The complete cost must be paid;
there is no partial repeated payment. A declined or failed payment runs the
unpaid body. Results stay local to each operation. Continuation values are read
when their actions execute, independently of the saved payment count.

Typed count/payer reads and both continuation declarations participate in the
existing waiting delayed source query. Queries make no payment choice and read
no count. Existing typed permanent information preserves source incarnation,
LKI and phase facts. Return cannot replace the saved visit; actions still need a
present subject. Stack copies retain their own controller. Clones keep separate
mana, counters and resolution frames. Damage and counter replacement services
remain unchanged. CR 118.2–3, 118.5, 400.7, 608.2h and 605.3a–b supply the
payment, identity, information and mana-ability boundaries.

Evidence: `TestRepeatedManaPayment*` covers all five colors plus generic mana,
zero acceptance/decline, dynamic negatives, affordability, mana abilities,
choice-time count changes, failed-payment rollback, definition validation,
overflow, absent payer, cost reductions, clones and waiting declarations.
`TestRONRepeatedManaPayment*` covers full Cyclone casting/upkeep gameplay,
paid/unpaid paths, prevention and simultaneous observations, live counts,
departure, return, phasing, control, stack copies and independent clones;
branch polarity, adjacent payments, delayed execution, strict atomic loading,
inventory roles and invalid declarations. One unique card gains compilation
and complete-record gameplay evidence.

## Chosen resolving mana payment and local damage prevention

`PayChosenManaInto(player PlayerRef, result *NumberBinding) ResolvingEffect`
clears the output before resolving its payer. An absent player makes no choice.
The amount choice permits zero through the engine's maximum integer, without a
bound derived from damage or the current pool. `NonnegativeNumberChooser` can
supply direct input. Existing players use `ChooseMode` to finish or append a
digit, then bounded `ChooseNumber` for that digit. The last digit limit prevents
integer overflow. This keeps the existing human player's option allocation
bounded. Invalid direct input or invalid digits supply zero.

The amount is fixed before shared `tryResolutionCostPayment` and the action
payment transaction. Choosing an amount is the optional decision; there is no
second payment offer. Complete generic payment permits mana abilities, checks
spending restrictions, ignores activation reductions and retains rollback.
Failure supplies zero. Successful payment publishes the amount in the current
number frame. Definition inspection declares the output and validates the payer;
waiting queries inspect its typed source dependency without making choices.

`DealDamageWithPreventionFrom(source DamageSourceRef, recipient
DamageRecipientRef, amount ResolutionValue, prevention ResolutionValue)
ResolvingEffect` extends the existing singular damage service. Source,
recipient, damage and prevention use their normal resolution timing. One local
`instructionDamagePrevention` candidate enters the shared replacement pipeline,
with ordinary prevention priority. The affected player can order it against
other replacements. The candidate remains available after redirection, applies
once to the event, obeys prevention restrictions and never enters global or
cycle replacement storage. It cannot leave a shield for later damage.
Nonpositive damage causes no event; negative prevention supplies zero.

Exact source information uses existing current, departure and phase reads.
Return cannot substitute another source visit. Existing trigger player captures
retain the payer after host control changes or reattachment. Number bindings,
stack copies, game clones and delayed captures keep separate frames. There is
no global last-payment slot and no new zone, mana or damage subsystem. Existing
callers of replacement preparation and singular damage services are preserved.

Rules: CR 118.2–3 and 118.5 cover complete payment and zero acknowledgment;
605.3a–b permits immediate mana abilities during resolution. CR 615.1a, 615.4,
615.6 and 615.12 cover prevention, actual damage and prohibitions. CR 616.1e–f
supplies affected-player order and rechecks. CR 400.7 and 608.2h retain the exact
source information contract. Local `data/LEA.json` Oracle text agrees with all
six complete Power Leak RON records; no source correction is needed.

Evidence: `TestChosenManaPayment`, `ManaAbilitiesAndRollback`,
`BindingsAndClones`, `Definition`, `DigitDecision` and `LimitsAndRestrictions`;
`TestInstructionDamagePrevention`, `Ordering` and `RedirectAndProhibition`;
interactive `TestHumanChosenManaPayment`; RON `TestRONChosenManaPayment*`.
Power Leak gains complete-record gameplay evidence independently of its six
newly compiling records.

## Permanent mana-cost activation payment

`PermanentManaCostPayment(subject PermanentRef) Cost` supplies one live mana
component for an activated ability. Definition validation requires a non-nil,
bound permanent reference and an activated ability context. RON lowers only
source and Aura-host references in nonmana activation costs, including cost
conjunctions. Mana-producing bodies need their separate solver metadata adapter.
No casting, entry, grant or resolving-payment adapter is added.

The source and subject must be present and unphased when the cost is read.
`AttachedPermanent` checks the saved attachment visit. No LKI supplies payment;
a returned permanent cannot replace an old attachment. Current copied
characteristics supply the cost, including copies of permanent spells.
Face-down objects and objects with no mana cost cannot supply a payment.
An absent cost stays unpayable through reductions (CR 118.6–118.6a, 202.1b).
Printed zero costs can be paid. Each X is zero (CR 107.3g–h).

`ActionDefinition.CanActivate` and `prepareActionPaymentTransaction` lower the
component through the same pure read. Queries aggregate all mana components
before checking affordability; they cannot reuse one mana for two components.
The payment path reads and locks the component before shared cost choices and
mana abilities. The shared total applies activation increases and reductions
once and owns mana planning, spending and rollback. Its owned hybrid array
keeps the locked cost separate from later characteristic changes. Later host
cost changes, reattachment or departure cannot change an already locked total
(CR 601.2f–h, 602.2b). A later activation performs a fresh read.
Stack copies repeat effects without payment. Game clones keep separate zones,
resources and pending source snapshots. No mutable payment state is stored in
the cost declaration. Existing callers and cost signatures remain in place.

Evidence: native `TestPermanentManaCostPayment`, `AggregateAndLock`,
`ModifiersAndRollback`, `SubjectsAndCostFreeze`, `CopiedHost`, `HybridFreeze`
and `Invalid` cover colored/generic/zero/absent/X costs, aggregate affordability,
modifiers, pure queries, automatic mana, rollback, present visits, phasing,
copy characteristics, locked totals and validation. Complete RON Merseine tests
cover casting and enchant legality through shared Aura targets, three entry
counters, conditional untap prevention, host-controller permission, actual
counter removal, zero-counter activations, reattachment, control changes,
departure/return, phasing, ability removal, stack copies and clone isolation.
`TestRONPermanentManaCostManaSources` pays with complete RON Forests.
Declaration and strict-loading tests preserve rejection of invalid collections.
No counter, untap, replacement-order or simultaneous-operation service changed.


## Targeting-cause damage prevention

`PreventDamageCausedByTargetingThisTurn(subject PermanentRef) ResolvingEffect`
saves a present, unphased subject's exact battlefield visit until cleanup.
Definition inspection requires a valid typed subject. A resolved rule survives
source departure, control changes and ability removal. Phasing preserves the
subject visit, but an absent or phased subject cannot take damage. Return starts
a new visit and cannot inherit protection (CR 400.7, 702.26).

`ResolutionState.Begin` captures the causing stack object's ID and permanent
target visits for both spells and abilities. Target legality does not delete
these announced references. Copies capture their own stack ID and target list;
clones copy the target array. Clearing resolution clears the cause. A damage
packet saves these cause facts before replacement choices. Combat and damage
outside a resolving stack frame have no targeting cause. The damage source keeps
its existing independent characteristics, visit, controller and LKI services.
This separation follows CR 120.2b: a spell or ability specifies the object that
deals damage. A different permanent can be that source.

The common prevention matcher requires the saved subject in the cause's target
visits, the same current recipient visit, and noncombat damage. It has no amount
limit and applies to each matching event. Source-only damage target facts do not
satisfy the cause predicate. Common single-packet and simultaneous replacement
paths, including selected-source batch redirection, retain cause facts when a
replacement changes damage amount or recipient. Candidates are checked again
against the new recipient. Existing affected-player order, one application per
rule and packet, prevention prohibitions and simultaneous event observations
remain in the shared pipeline (CR 615.1, 615.6, 615.12, 616.1).

RON accepts the same typed singular reference in `TargetsPermanent` and
`Permanent`, the symbol `AnyDamageSource`, one symbol `PreventThatDamage` and
`UntilEndOfTurn`, in resolving action lists. The compiler owns spelling, arity,
matching reference plans and scope. The engine owns identity and damage rules.
No new cost, zone, damage-source or replacement-order service is introduced.

Evidence: native `TestDamageCausePrevention`, `TestDamageCauseSnapshots`,
`TestDamageCauseReplacementRecheck`, `TestDamageCauseDefinitionAndWaiting`;
complete repository Silhouette in `TestRONDamageCauseSilhouette`,
`TestRONDamageCauseInstallationLegality`, `TestRONDamageCauseInvalid` and
`TestRONDamageCauseStrictLoadAndInventory`. These cover paid casting, illegal
announcement without spending, illegal resolution without installation, spell
and activated-ability causes, another permanent as the damage source, untargeted
effects, stack copies, snapshot independence, clones, source departure, subject
return, phasing, cleanup, unpreventable damage, pure waiting queries, nil subject
rejection, amount changes, redirection into and out of protection and packet
rechecks after subject departure. No RON source correction was required.

## Single-target spell predicate

`SpellWithSingleTarget() SpellFilter` matches a spell with exactly one announced
target occurrence (CR 115.9a). Two target groups that select the same object count
as two occurrences. This is distinct from the unique-object check for “targets
only” in CR 115.9c. Abilities, missing spell cards and absent stack objects do not
match. The predicate reads `StackObject.Targets`; it does not query target
legality, current characteristics or departure information. Phasing, departure,
return and protection do not erase occurrences. A changed target list supplies
the current count. Copies and game clones keep separate lists.

The existing `SpellTargetBinding.WithFilter` applies the predicate at selection
and resolution. Failed selection spends no resources. The existing cast-event
filter checks detection once; pending triggers retain that result. Immutable
And/Or/Not composition and definition validation use the shared spell filters.
There is no new targeting, identity, copy or event subsystem.

RON accepts the strict symbol `TargetsOnlyASingleTarget` in contextual
`TargetSpell` and `WhenAPlayerCastsASpell` filters, including existing And/Or and
ExceptFor composition. Tuple forms and card-only static spell restrictions
reject it. Despite the RON spelling, Reflecting Mirror's local DRK Oracle says
“with a single target”; the occurrence contract follows that wording. Its full
record remains unsupported. `CanTargetOnly`, target-dependent announcement X,
player-target predicates and retargeting remain separate capabilities.

Evidence: native `TestSpellSingleTargetOccurrences` and
`TestSpellSingleTargetSavedAndCurrentLists`; RON `TestRONSingleTargetGameplay`,
`RejectAndDeclarations`, `CastEvents` and `ActivationAndComposition`. These use
complete Lightning Bolt and Llanowar Elves RON definitions with synthetic
predicate consumers. They establish the prerequisite, not complete Reflecting
Mirror gameplay. Replacement order, payment amounts, LKI reads and simultaneous
movement are unchanged by this query.

## Declared permanent target subtype constraints

`TargetHasSubtype(subtype string) PermanentTargetOption` enforces a subtype on
one permanent target group. `TargetRequiredSubtypes(target Target) []string`
returns a separate list of these constraints, in declaration order, without
choices or game-state reads. Duplicate constraints appear once; distinct
constraints apply together. An empty list means no declared proof is available.
It does not mean the group can target every permanent. Existing opaque filters,
negation and disjunction do not supply this proof.

RON lowers `IsCreatureType(symbol)` in a permanent target filter to this typed
option. Direct predicates and nested `And` keep the declaration alongside all
other filters and controller restrictions. Fixed and X-count groups use the same
service. `IsNonCreatureType`, `Or`, Aura enchant filters and other filter contexts
retain their existing behavior and supply no new declaration proof. The subtype
uses the existing RON name normalization. This does not add a creature card-type
restriction to the existing subtype predicate.

The engine enforces the constraint even if a caller replaces the group's public
additional filter list. `PermanentTarget.Filter` includes the same constraints.
Bindings and count/random wrappers retain them. Aura attachment checks use the
same combined filter without applying targeting restrictions to an existing
attachment. Spell text continuation checks retain the exact constraints. Invalid empty names and names
with outer spaces fail definition validation, including through wrappers.
Malformed RON arguments and incompatible action or spell-filter contexts reject
before publication. Returned query lists and fresh factory instances do not
share mutable result storage.

Selection and resolution read current subtypes through the existing targeting
service (CR 115.1a, 601.2c, 608.2b). A declaration persists when targets phase,
leave, return or change subtype. It does not authorize actions on those objects:
existing incarnation, phasing, protection and live filter checks still apply.
Copies and clones keep the declarations and their own chosen target facts.
Zero-count groups retain declarations even with no selected occurrences. A future
whole-spell/ability domain consumer must inspect every applicable declaration;
selected `StackObject.TargetSpecs` alone omit zero-choice groups.

This is the bounded declaration prerequisite for Wall of Shadows. Active
ability identity uses the separate targeting-ability service below. CanTargetOnly
and complete spell/domain classification remain unsupported, so the complete
Wall record still rejects.

Evidence: native `TestTargetSubtypeDomain` and
`TestTargetSubtypeDomainDeclarations` and `TestTargetSubtypeDomainCallers`; RON `TestRONTargetSubtypeDomainGameplay`
(Tunnel), `Activation` (Goblin Digging Team), `ResolutionRecheck`,
`CountDeclarations`, `Conjunction`, `Records`, and `InvalidAndBoundaries`.
`Records` checks complete accepted definitions for 15 unique names / 24 records;
the complete Delusion, Reincarnation and Shadows records remain rejected.
Existing Glyph gameplay tests also exercise the changed target lowering.
No new full-card compilation or gameplay completion is claimed for rejected
records. Payments, replacement order and simultaneous operations use the existing
engine contracts.

## Active targeting ability declarations

`(*Game).AbilityTargetSource(card Card, ability Ability, declared []Target) Card`
retains one activated, triggered or mana ability's declaration ID and the
complete applicable target list in the existing typed source-information view.
`TargetSourceAbility(source Card) (uuid.UUID, []Target, bool)` returns that ID,
a separate list and a known flag. A known empty list is not an unknown ability.
Absent cards, absent abilities, zero IDs and spell/static abilities cannot
create a new ability declaration view. The ID identifies the declaration;
stack IDs identify separate executions. Existing source visits identify the
source incarnation. These identities must not be replaced by a source card name.

The caller supplies ordinary or selected-mode declarations before target choice.
The list includes fixed-zero and optional groups with no chosen occurrences.
Input and query slices cannot change the saved list. Underlying declarations
keep their existing ownership contract; this API does not grant permission to
change an ability's target specification. Queries make no choices or payments.
Current source characteristics and exact departure/phase information use the
existing source-information service. Ability facts survive those information
reads without following a returned source (CR 400.7, 602.2a, 608.2b).

Activation target validation, forced/random/opponent choices, grouped targets,
modal legality and interactive target queries use the selected ability view.
Graveyard activation validates targets before the shared payment transaction
and saves aligned specs for resolution. Illegal targets retain the source card
and resources. Pending ordinary and modal triggers use their saved declaration,
including after source departure, control changes or phasing (CR 603.3c–d).
Scheduled delayed triggers receive separate declaration IDs; copies and clones
retain the scheduled declaration. No global last-ability field is used.

Stack copies and game clones keep ability facts with their independent chosen
visits and resolution frames. Ability-copy retargeting uses complete saved
declarations when available, preserving the announced count; legacy callers
without the new view retain their existing path (CR 707.10c). Resolution
rechecks current target legality. Protection and source-type restrictions still
use current source characteristics or exact LKI, not printed characteristics.

RON's existing `Activated`, `ActivatedWithModifiers`, `TriggerA`, `TriggerI`,
`Modal_ChooseOne`, `Targeted` and target-count lowering already produces fresh
ability instances and complete groups. No spelling adapter or source edit is
needed for this engine prerequisite. It does not implement `CanTargetOnly`,
spell-domain classification or Aura/disjunctive domain proofs. Unknown domains
must not be treated as unrestricted. Wall of Shadows remains rejected.

Evidence: native `TestTargetingAbilityView`, `Activation`,
`CurrentCharacteristics`, `Queries`, `PendingAndDelayed`, and `Graveyard`;
RON `TestRONTargetingAbilityGameplay` (Ali Baba, Goblin Digging Team), `Modal`
(Balm of Restoration), `Trigger` (The Abyss), `ZeroGroup`, and `Records`.
`Records` checks distinct factory IDs and exact declaration groups for eleven
existing accepted subtype-targeted names. These are declaration integration
checks, not new complete-card gameplay claims.

Interactive regression evidence also includes `TestTargetingAbilitySearch`,
`TestTargetingAbilityCombat` and `TestTargetingAbilityCombatSolver`. Search,
regeneration, pump planning and the combat solver keep the actual selected
ability rather than deriving one from its source card.
